title: Quality Technician II (1st Shift)
description:
At Jabil (NYSE: JBL), we are proud to be a trusted partner for the world's top brands, offering comprehensive engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions. With 60 years of experience across industries and a vast network of over 100 sites worldwide, Jabil combines global reach with local expertise to deliver both scalable and customized solutions. Our commitment extends beyond business success as we strive to build sustainable processes that minimize environmental impact and foster vibrant and diverse communities around the globe.

Location/Division Specific Information

** On-site at our Prince George, VA facility. **

This role is to support a new factory in Prince George, VA (onsite) startup manufacturing large form-factor equipment. The product will be large (shipping container size), heavy (50+ tons), and complex. This position will be part of the core factory startup and onboarding team responsible for building the operations and manufacturing staff, fitting out the building, and creating the process flow/work instructions/etc. from the ground up. Skills to include panel and point to point wire assembly, Medium Voltage, Low Voltage, and High-Power Electronic assemblies.

How will you make an impact?

You will help build a culture of quality by performing inspections, identifying and containing issues before they reach the customer, and supporting the implementation and continuous improvement of quality controls. Through inspection, data analysis, problem-solving, and collaboration with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Quality teams, you will play a key role in supporting the successful launch and growth of a world-class manufacturing operation.

What will you do?

  • Perform in-process and final inspections of assemblies, components, and materials as required to support production and quality objectives.

  • Conduct visual, dimensional, and functional inspections using measuring and test equipment.

  • Verify products meet engineering drawings, specifications, work instructions, and quality standards.

  • Identify, document, and report nonconforming materials, processes, and products.

  • Support containment activities, nonconformance investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective action implementation.

  • Collect and analyze quality data to support trend analysis, Pareto analysis, and continuous improvement activities.

  • Maintain accurate inspection records, quality documentation, and test data.

  • Partner with Production, Engineering, and Supply Chain teams to resolve quality concerns and drive continuous improvement.

  • Assist in developing and improving inspection procedures, quality plans, work instructions, and quality controls.

  • Support internal audits, process audits, and quality system activities as required.

  • Support Gauge R&R studies, measurement system evaluations, process validations, and quality improvement initiatives.

  • Support factory startup activities, including process validation, training, and operational readiness.

  • Assist Quality Supervisors with training, qualification, onboarding, and day-to-day support of Quality Inspectors and quality personnel.

  • Ensure compliance with all safety, quality, customer, and regulatory requirements.

How will you get here?

Education

  • High School Diploma or GED required.

  • Associate degree or technical certification in Quality, Manufacturing, Electronics, Engineering Technology, or a related field preferred.

Experience

  • 2+ years of experience in a Quality Technician, Quality Inspector, Quality Control, Manufacturing, or Quality Assurance role within a manufacturing environment.

  • Experience performing inspections in an industrial, electrical, electronics, or manufacturing setting.

  • Experience supporting quality investigations, corrective actions, quality improvement activities, or manufacturing quality processes preferred.

  • Experience supporting process validation, NPI, or startup manufacturing activities preferred.

  • Experience supporting large assemblies, industrial equipment, power systems, heavy manufacturing, or other complex manufacturing environments preferred.

  • Experience in a startup manufacturing environment is a plus.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities

  • Ability to read and interpret advanced engineering drawings, blueprints, schematics, and technical specifications required.

  • Proficiency using inspection and measurement tools such as calipers, micrometers, tape measures, height gauges, and related inspection equipment.

  • Strong attention to detail and ability to identify defects and nonconformances.

  • Experience supporting containment activities, nonconformance investigations, and corrective actions preferred.

  • Ability to collect and analyze quality data to support continuous improvement activities preferred.

  • Strong communication, teamwork, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

  • Basic computer proficiency, including Microsoft Office applications.

  • Ability to work independently in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

  • Ability to support training and qualification activities for Quality Inspectors and quality personnel.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting electrical assemblies, panel assembly, wiring, electro-mechanical assemblies, or similar manufacturing environments.

  • Knowledge of ISO 9001 or similar quality management systems.

  • Familiarity with root cause analysis, corrective action methodologies, and continuous improvement tools.

  • Experience working with large fabricated, mechanical, electro-mechanical, or other large form-factor assemblies.

title: Field Service Representative - Part Time
description:
What Matters at Magid? YOU do!

We’ve built an innovative and collaborative environment where diversity is celebrated, ideas are valued, and personal and professional growth never stops. As a Field Service Representative (FSR), you'll play an important role in keeping workers safe. By making sure our customer vending machines are stocked, organized, and running smoothly, you'll help ensure employees have access to the gloves, safety glasses, and other Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) they need to do their jobs safely - when and where they need it. Your work may happen behind the scenes, but its impact is seen every day.

  • Flexibility, with structure — Choose when to complete your service within the customer's required days and operating hours.
  • Work independently — Take ownership of your assigned customer locations with minimal supervision.

What You'll Do

  • Restock Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) vending machines with safety products such as gloves, safety glasses, and other equipment
  • Monitor inventory levels and keep products organized
  • Perform basic vending machine maintenance and replace simple parts when needed
  • Transport inventory between storage areas and vending machines
  • Build positive relationships with customer contacts while providing excellent service

Schedule

This role supports two customer locations in Tomah, WI and Black River Falls, WI.

Service is performed three days per week: Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, with approximately 2 to 3 hours per day. The position averages approximately 8 hours per week.

All service must be completed between 7:00 AM and 4:00 PM, providing flexibility to plan visits within that time frame based on customer needs.

Mileage reimbursement is provided for travel between customer locations in accordance with company policy.

  • Comfortable performing light mechanical tasks

Requirements

  • Reliable vehicle, valid driver's license, and satisfactory Motor Vehicle Report (MVR)
  • Personal smartphone
  • Basic computer skills
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds
  • Ability to work in manufacturing environments that may be noisy or have varying temperatures
  • Flexibility to provide on-call support for emergency maintenance and repairs

Safety Requirements

  • Mandatory PPE is required at customer locations. Magid will provide the required PPE.

title: F-18 Flight Operations 3
description:
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: No relocation assistance available

CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: Yes

CLEARANCE TYPE: Interim Secret

TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman Aeronautics Systems has an opening for F-18 Flight Operations Technician 3 to join our team of qualified, diverse individuals within our F-18 organization. This role is located in Belle Chasse, LA

Job Duties

  • Performs a combination of responsibilities consisting of complex mechanical duties in all fields of specialization for the flight line, including power plant, run-in plumbing, hydraulics, rigging, and controls, and structures and surfaces on the complete airplane.

  • Performs mechanical and operational duties for pre-flight and post-flight service and inspection and/or in preparation of customer acceptance of completed airplanes

  • Performs operations such as disassembling, repairing, replacing, rechecking, testing, re-rigging, servicing, and re-installing, as necessary.

  • Operates aircraft power plants and ground equipment during acceptance checks, trouble shooting and routine maintenance of aircraft.

  • May troubleshoot malfunctions/defects and schedule/modify maintenance procedures.

  • Maintain practical knowledge of certified aircraft and ground support systems such as controls, fuel, hydraulic, pneumatic, electronic, fire control and armament components.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Must have a High School Diploma or equivalent (GED) and at least 4 years of aircraft maintenance experience.

  • Must have the ability to obtain and maintain a DoD Secret clearance within a reasonable amount of time as determined by business needs.

  • Able to read and interpret schematics, assembly drawings, process specifications, technical manuals, written instructions, test procedures, etc.

  • Able to perform assigned duties on all shifts without encumbrances due to weather or physical location and conditions.

  • This position requires the ability to perform moderate strenuous physical and repetitious work to include: bending, stooping, kneeling, carrying tools, lifting up to 50 pounds, working overhead, and accessing small, confined spaces

  • Must be able to pass a physical/respiratory evaluation to obtain and maintain necessary respirator clearance and compliance with all respirator fitting requirements

  • Must be able to work outside for 8–10 hours per day in temperatures ranging from [40°F to 110°F].

  • Must be willing to work in rain, snow, sleet, high winds, and high humidity.

  • Ability to lift 30 bs, climb ladders, aircraft stands, or stand for long periods in uneven or slippery terrain.

  • Must be able to pass a physical and weigh in for fall protection.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Fighter type aircraft maintenance experience

  • A&P license

  • U.S. Navy or USMC background

  • Active Secret DoD clearance

Primary Level Salary Range: $55,800.00 - $93,000.00

title: Plant Director – Aerospace Manufacturing
description:
Plant Director – Aerospace Manufacturing

Location: Arkansas
Employment: Full-Time | Permanent | On-Site
Industry: Aerospace / Advanced Manufacturing

Lead the Operation. Transform Performance. Build for Growth.

We’re partnering confidentially with an established aerospace manufacturing organization seeking an accomplished Plant Director to lead a large, complex manufacturing operation in Arkansas.

This is a senior site leadership mandate with responsibility for approximately 300 employees across multiple facilities, with broad accountability for operational performance, people leadership, financial results, quality, delivery, productivity, and continuous improvement.

The operation is entering an important period of growth and transformation. We’re looking for a manufacturing leader who can strengthen operational discipline, develop the leadership team, improve performance, and build the organizational capability required for the next stage of growth.

The successful leader will be equally comfortable on the manufacturing floor and at the executive table.

What You’ll Own

Site & Operational Leadership

  • Lead overall performance and day-to-day manufacturing operations

  • Lead, coach, and develop the site's management team

  • Establish clear priorities, KPIs, operating rhythms, and accountability

  • Align people, capacity, processes, and resources with production and customer requirements

  • Partner across Quality, Engineering, Supply Chain, HR, Finance, IT, Sales, and executive leadership

Operational Excellence

Own and improve performance across:

  • Safety

  • Quality

  • On-time delivery

  • Productivity and throughput

  • Manufacturing cost and efficiency

  • Inventory

  • Customer commitments

Identify operational bottlenecks, strengthen performance management, and implement sustainable improvements throughout the operation.

Transformation & Continuous Improvement

  • Lead operational transformation and continuous improvement initiatives

  • Strengthen standardization, accountability, and execution

  • Apply Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma principles

  • Identify opportunities for automation and manufacturing modernization

  • Improve processes, systems, and operating discipline

  • Build the capacity required to support future growth

P&L & Business Performance

This role carries meaningful responsibility for the financial performance of the operation.

  • Own and influence site-level P&L performance

  • Develop and manage operating budgets

  • Review financial performance and key variances

  • Manage headcount, operating expenses, productivity, and capital requirements

  • Make operational decisions with a clear understanding of their impact on cost, margin, cash, and business performance

People & Organizational Leadership

  • Build a high-performance culture centered on accountability and execution

  • Maintain a visible leadership presence on the manufacturing floor

  • Develop managers and strengthen leadership succession

  • Partner with HR on workforce planning, organizational development, and employee relations

  • Operate effectively within a unionized manufacturing environment

What We’re Looking For

  • Progressive leadership experience within complex manufacturing operations

  • Experience leading managers and multidisciplinary operational teams

  • Strong plant/site leadership capability

  • Strong understanding of P&L, budgeting, manufacturing costs, productivity, and financial performance

  • Demonstrated success improving manufacturing performance

  • Experience leading through growth, transformation, integration, or organizational change

  • Experience within a unionized manufacturing environment

  • Strong executive communication and decision-making ability

  • Hands-on leadership style with strong shop-floor credibility

Highly Valued

  • Aerospace and/or defense manufacturing

  • Large-site manufacturing leadership

  • Lean Manufacturing / Six Sigma

  • AS9100 or comparable regulated quality environments

  • Manufacturing automation and modernization

  • ERP-driven manufacturing operations

  • Operational transformation or integration

  • Complex engineered products

The Leadership Profile

We’re looking for a hands-on, business-minded manufacturing leader who thinks and acts like an owner.

You can set strategy while staying close enough to the operation to understand what's actually happening on the floor.

You develop leaders, challenge existing processes, make decisions, establish accountability, and understand the relationship between people, operations, customers, and financial results.

This isn't about maintaining the status quo.

It's about building a stronger operation.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

  • Lead a significant, approximately 300-person manufacturing operation

  • Broad ownership of operational and financial performance

  • Direct exposure to senior leadership

  • Lead meaningful operational transformation

  • Influence automation and manufacturing modernization

  • Build leadership capability and succession

  • Help prepare the operation for significant future growth

  • Comprehensive executive benefits package

Important Requirement

Due to applicable controlled products, programs, and technical information, U.S. citizenship is required for this position.

Apply Today

If you’re an accomplished manufacturing leader who combines operational excellence, financial discipline, transformation experience, and shop-floor credibility, we’d welcome a confidential conversation.

All applications and conversations will be handled discreetly.

title: Program Supervisor
description:
Who We Are:
Our story began in 2011 when a group of office workers at a major logistics company in Chicago had a lunch problem. Nearby options were limited, and the team was spending too much time and money traveling to their favorite restaurants. They had an idea: bring Chicago’s local restaurant culture inside the office to sell food. It was an immediate hit. When they discovered people from other companies sneaking into their office, they knew they were on to something.

Fooda pioneered the concept of rotating popup restaurants inside offices. Today, we operate in 60 cities with over 100 million meals served and continue to grow rapidly.

Powered by technology and a network of 3,500+ restaurants, we feed hungry people at work through a platform of unique food programs located within companies, office buildings, hospitals, schools, distribution centers, and more. At Fooda, we believe a workplace food program should be something employees love and look forward to every day.

Position Overview:
We are looking for a Program Supervisor in Burlington, Texas. A travel stipend will be included in compensation for anyone outside of the area.

This person is the onsite leader responsible for delivering a consistent, hospitality-driven Fooda experience at a client location. As the primary point of contact for clients, consumers, and vendors, this role ensures that daily service runs smoothly, issues are resolved quickly, and the overall experience reflects Fooda’s standards of quality and care.

This role also plays an important role in shaping the restaurant network that serves your location—building strong relationships, communicating expectations, and ensuring partners are set up for success. Operating with a high degree of autonomy, this role blends hospitality, operational judgment, and client care, and is key to maintaining overall satisfaction and trust in Fooda’s service.

What You Will Be Doing:
  • Lead the day-to-day onsite experience, ensuring Fooda’s programs run smoothly, on time, and with a hospitality-first mindset.
  • Serve as the primary onsite contact for the client and their employees, building trust through consistency, communication, and quick problem solving.
  • Provide onsite guidance and support to staff or coordinators when needed, helping everyone stay aligned and prepared for service.
  • Partner with restaurant teams to ensure they’re set up for success each day—communicating expectations, supporting setup, and addressing issues as they arise.
  • Keep a close pulse on the customer experience, noticing trends, resolving concerns, and escalating when appropriate to the Sr Strategic Account Manager.
  • Maintain the operational details that keep service running well—menus, point-of-sale updates, signage, daily flow, and overall presentation.
  • Influence the restaurant network supporting your location by sharing feedback, reinforcing standards, and helping ensure strong vendor performance.
  • This role is 100% onsite in Burlington, TX.

Who You Are
  • You’re naturally hospitality-driven and enjoy creating a warm, smooth experience for clients and customers.
  • You’re a steady, reliable onsite presence who takes ownership and operates confidently with a high degree of autonomy.
  • You communicate clearly and professionally—whether you’re working with clients, staff, or restaurant partners.
  • You’re calm under pressure and think quickly when plans shift, viewing challenges as opportunities to problem-solve.
  • You’re organized, detail-oriented, and committed to keeping day-to-day operations running at a high standard.
  • You’re comfortable offering direction and support onsite without being a formal people manager.
  • You have experience in hospitality, food service, catering, or operations, and enjoy being the person who “keeps everything moving.”

What We’ll Hook You Up With:
  • Competitive base salary, bonus plan, and stock options, based on experience
  • Comprehensive health, dental and vision plans
  • 401k retirement plan with company match
  • Paid maternity and parental leave benefits
  • Flexible spending accounts
  • Company-issued laptop
  • Travel stipend
  • Daily subsidized lunch program (ours!)
Must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. No recruiters please.

title: Category Implementation Buyer-Engineering/Professional Services
description:
We made history and now we work to transform the future – for our customers, our communities and our families. You'll see your work on the road every day, helping people move freely and pursue their dreams. At Ford, you can build more than vehicles. Come build what matters.

The Ford Supply Chain team adds critical value to the entire organization. You’ll help us source the highest quality parts and services from around the globe while ensuring optimal cost and on-time delivery. You’ll also contribute to establishing a robust supply chain so that we can continually produce the vehicles our customers want.

In this position...

Ford Motor Company is seeking a strategic, results-driven Category Implementation Buyer to lead sourcing and category strategy for Engineering/Professional Services. This role is responsible for shaping the future of Services procurement by driving cost competitiveness, advancing sourcing strategies, and enabling Product Development through high-performing supplier partnerships.

The ideal candidate brings a strong combination of commercial acumen, stakeholder alignment, and forward-thinking strategy, transitioning traditional purchasing models into outcome-based, value-driven engagements that deliver measurable cost savings and operational efficiency.

  • Strategic thinker who challenges the status quo and drives innovation in sourcing approaches
  • Cost-focused leader who proactively identifies and delivers value beyond traditional savings
  • Strong collaborator who can influence business stakeholders with credibility
  • Data-driven decision-maker with a passion for continuous improvement and operational excellence
  • Influential leader who drives alignment across teams, customers, while fostering a high-performing, accountable culture
  • Resilient and adaptable, able to navigate ambiguity and lead through transformation

Operational Excellence & Governance

  • Ensure timely execution of sourcing events, contract renewals, and compliance with corporate purchasing policies.
  • Implement robust contracting frameworks (MSAs, SOWs, SLAs) that incentivize performance and mitigate risk.

What you'll do...

Category Strategy & Transformation

  • Lead development and execution of forward-looking category strategies aligned with Product Development priorities, with a strong focus on cost optimization and value delivery.
  • Drive transformation from time & material engagements to deliverable-based, performance-driven sourcing models to improve cost predictability and accountability.
  • Identify and implement innovative sourcing levers including global benchmarking, should-cost modeling, demand management, and supplier consolidation.

Cost Leadership & Financial Performance

  • Deliver year-over-year cost savings through strategic negotiations, commercial restructuring, and continuous market testing.
  • Analyze spend, supplier cost structures, and industry benchmarks to uncover cost reduction opportunities and improve total cost of ownership.
  • Partner with Finance and other key stakeholders to align budgets, forecasts, and sourcing strategies with enterprise cost targets.

Supplier Strategy & Relationship Management

  • Build and manage a high-performing, competitive supply base across specialized service providers.
  • Lead supplier negotiations for complex, high-value contracts, ensuring optimal pricing, terms, and service levels.
  • Drive supplier performance through KPIs, SLAs, and continuous improvement initiatives focused on efficiency, quality, and innovation.
  • Continuously improve procurement processes, tools, and systems to enhance efficiency, transparency, and data-driven decision-making.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Act as a key interface between Supply Chain, Business Owner Stakeholders, Finance, Legal, and external partners to ensure alignment on sourcing strategy and execution.
  • Influence stakeholders to adopt best-in-class sourcing practices and challenge legacy ways of working.
  • Lead or support strategic initiatives, workshops, and supplier engagements (e.g., tech days, benchmarking reviews) to drive innovation and capability building

You'll have...

Minimum

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or related field.
  • 3+ years of experience in supply chain, purchasing, or category management, with exposure to services or technical procurement.
  • Strong track record of delivering measurable cost savings and driving strategic sourcing initiatives.
  • Experience developing and executing category strategies, including market analysis, benchmarking, and supplier segmentation.
  • Advanced negotiation skills with experience in complex commercial agreements and contract structuring.
  • Ability to translate technical requirements into effective sourcing and commercial strategies.
  • Strong financial and analytical acumen, including spend analysis and cost modeling.
  • Proven ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and lead without direct authority.
  • Experience managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced, transformation-driven environment.
  • Proficiency in procurement tools (e.g., Ariba), Excel (advanced), and PowerPoint.

You may not check every box, or your experience may look a little different from what we've outlined, but if you think you can bring value to Ford Motor Company, we encourage you to apply!

As an established global company, we offer the benefit of choice. You can choose what your Ford future will look like: will your story span the globe, or keep you close to home? Will your career be a deep dive into what you love, or a series of new teams and new skills? Will you be a leader, a changemaker, a technical expert, a culture builder…or all of the above? No matter what you choose, we offer a work life that works for you, including:
• Immediate medical, dental, vision and prescription drug coverage
• Flexible family care days, paid parental leave, new parent ramp-up programs, subsidized back-up child care and more
• Family building benefits including adoption and surrogacy expense reimbursement, fertility treatments, and more
• Vehicle discount program for employees and family members and management leases
• Tuition assistance
• Established and active employee resource groups
• Paid time off for individual and team community service
• A generous schedule of paid holidays, including the week between Christmas and New Year’s Day
• Paid time off and the option to purchase additional vacation time.

This position is a range of salary grades 6-8 and ranges from $63,480-$166,200.

Final determination of salary grade will be based on candidate's skills and experience, and base salary will be set within the applicable range according to job scope, responsibility and competitive market value.

Responsible for ensuring accurate CPT and/or ICD-10 documentation for the patient billing process and educating colleagues and providers in accurately document services performed and using the appropriate codes representing those services. Maintains documentation regarding charge capture processes. Performs regular reviews of process adherence and identify missing charges.

Coordinates with key stakeholders regarding impacts of system change requests and upgrades to processes to ensure capture accuracy. Provides oversight of charge reconciliation processes for assigned departments; ensuring daily and appropriate monthly reconciliations are occurring.

Performs charge entry, charge approvals, and/or quality charge reviews; including but not limited to, appending modifiers, and checking clinical documentation. Provides feedback to intra-departmental Revenue Integrity colleagues including areas of opportunity.

As a mission-driven innovative health organization, we will become the national leader in improving the health of our communities and each person we serve. By demonstrating reverence, commitment to those who are poor, justice, stewardship, and integrity, our organization will continue to provide better health, better care, at lower costs.


Knows, understands, incorporates, and demonstrates the Trinity Health Mission, Vision, and Values in behaviors, practices, and decisions.

Responsible for coding and/or validation of charges for more complex service lines, advanced proficiencies in surgical or specialty coding practice.

Review's chart, including nursing notes, physician orders, progress notes, and surgical or specialty notes thoroughly to interpret and validate and/or extract all charges. Ensures each chart is complete according to specified guidelines. Ensures charges captured on the correct patient, correct encounter, correct date of service, with any required modifiers.

Review's documentation, abstracts data and ensure charges/coding are in alignment within AMA and Medicare coding guidelines. Ensures medical documentation and coding compliance with Federal, State and Private payer regulations.

Performs coding functions, including CPT, ICD-10 assignment, documentation review and claim denial review. Responsible for proofing daily charges for accuracy and clean claim submission

Responsible for balancing charges and adjustments. Maintains productivity standards

Maintains compliance with regulatory requirements. Assist Nurse Auditor and/or Coordinator with denial coordination process; including analysis of clinical documentation, root cause analysis and tracking as needed.

Educates clinical staff on need for accurate and complete documentation to ensure revenue optimization and integrity. Performs outpatient clinical documentation improvement review (acute only) as needed. Performs research on charges and communicate findings to intra and inter-departmental colleagues, as needed.

Maintains a minimum productivity standard, based on service line and charge type; including but not limited to chart review, charge extraction, E&M level assignment and charge entry.

Documents lessons learned and works with colleagues in Revenue Integrity department on creating standard charge capture and process reference materials. Assists with project initiatives to deploy information and provides education to departmental colleagues.

Reviews and responds to various quality reports, including reports that identify missing charges, duplicate charges, late charges, etc. Maintain and update required reference logs and other reporting tools. May develop and present information.

As needed, performs daily reconciliation processes and/or provides “at-elbow support” to ancillary departments including, but not limited to; ensuring supply charges are appropriate captured (may include implants), identify duplicate charges and initiate appropriate communications when there are documentation and/or charge deficiencies or charge errors. Other duties as assigned.

Must possess a demonstrated knowledge of clinical processes, clinical coding (CPT, HCPCS, ICD-9/10, revenue codes and modifiers), charging processes and audits, and clinical billing. Strong understanding of various medical claim formats.

Strong knowledge of Ambulatory Payment Classification (APC), and Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) reimbursement structures and prebill edits including Outpatient Coding Edits (OCE)/Correct Coding Initiative (CCI) edits and Discharged Note Final Billed (DNFB).

Ability to perform charge capture processes, including understanding technical integration of electronic medical record and the automation of charge triggers, and ability to investigate charge errors accordingly. Epic experience desired.

Experience and knowledge of working on appeals for insurance denials and identifying root cause.

Knowledge of Hospital and/or Physician group practice revenue cycle front-end functions such as patient registration and provider payment enrollment and back-end functions that may impact charge related errors.

Ability to organize and to prioritize work in a diverse, fast-paced environment while working on multiple projects simultaneously.

Strong problem-solving skills, analytical abilities, excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills. Ability to communicate effectively with other departments, including leadership, for the areas of charge capture, HIM, PBS, and other key stakeholders.

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
Job Description

Are you searching for an opportunity to play a key role in driving the dramatic growth of a highly successful software company?

And we do that at enterprise scale. Our omnichannel employee communications, customer communications, and workplace experience platform is trusted by over 6,000 organizations today, reaching more than 35M employees and delivering content to 500,000+ digital signs.

We know there’s no such thing as a “perfect" candidate - we’re all a work in progress and are growing new skills and capabilities all the time. We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to contribute to the technical excellence and scalability of our SaaS Employee Experience platform. You will serve as a senior hands‑on engineer within your team - designing and implementing complex features, improving system performance and reliability, and supporting the growth of other engineers.

This role is a key technical contributor within the engineering team. You will translate architectural guidance into robust, maintainable implementations and contribute to architectural discussions through strong technical execution and domain expertise.

The ideal candidate brings solid SaaS experience, hands‑on exposure to AWS managed & serverless technologies, and a strong understanding of distributed systems and modern software engineering best practices.

Key Responsibilities
  • Design and develop high-quality, scalable systems and services aligned with architectural standards and product requirements.
  • Implement microservices and APIs with strong emphasis on maintainability, performance, observability, and reliability.
  • Own complex features or components from design through deployment, including testing, monitoring, and operational support.
  • Collaborate closely with Principal Engineers, Architects, Product Managers, and DevOps to ensure high-quality and consistent delivery.
  • Build and enhance services leveraging AWS serverless, event-driven, and container-based technologies (Lambda, ECS, SNS, SQS, DynamoDB, Event-Bridge, RDS, etc.).
  • Ensure solutions adhere to authentication, authorization, and security best practices (OAuth2, OIDC, RBAC, etc.).
  • Participate in code reviews and uphold best practices in coding, design, testing, and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Support observability initiatives by contributing to metrics, logging, tracing, and alerting improvements.
  • Proactively identify and address technical debt, reliability risks, and areas for continuous improvement.
  • Contribute to compliance and data protection requirements including GDPR and PII handling best practices.
  • Participate actively in agile ceremonies and contribute to continuous improvement of engineering processes.
  • Demonstrate alignment with company values and promote an inclusive, collaborative engineering culture.
Education & Experience
  • 5–8 years of software development experience delivering production-grade applications in distributed or SaaS environments.
  • Strong experience in either Node.js / TypeScript (including asynchronous programming and modular architecture) or Java (Spring Boot, concurrency, RESTful services), and familiarity with React (or similar modern front-end frameworks).
  • Solid understanding of distributed systems, multi-tenancy concepts, RBAC, and SaaS security principles.
  • Hands‑on experience with Microservices Architecture, Docker, Kubernetes, and AWS cloud services a plus.
  • Experience implementing observability best practices (metrics, logging, tracing, alerting).
  • Working knowledge of event-driven systems (Kafka, SNS/SQS, Event-Bridge, Kinesis).
  • Experience contributing to CI/CD pipelines, Git workflows, and automated testing (JUnit, Jest, Playwright, etc.).
  • Demonstrated ability to design for scalability, performance, and fault tolerance within a defined product domain.
  • Familiarity with infrastructure as code (Terraform, CDK) is desirable.
  • Strong problem‑solving skills and the ability to troubleshoot complex production issues.
  • Effective communication skills with technical and cross‑functional stakeholders.
  • Commitment to continuous learning and improving engineering practices.
Compensation

Annual base salary gross: 61,000 - 75,000 plus variable EUR Annual. The base salary range represents the low and high end of the Company's contemplated salary range for this position. Actual salaries will vary and will be based on various factors, such as the candidate’s qualifications, skills, competencies, and geographic location. The salary is one component of Company's total compensation package for employees. Other rewards and benefits include variable compensation, short-term incentives, health insurance, accident and life insurance, access to the best in class learning and development platforms, flexible work arrangement, to name just a few!

Hybrid Working

This role follows a flexible hybrid working model. While our office is based in Cork, we welcome applications from candidates across Ireland. Office attendance can be planned flexibly, with expectations agreed directly with your reporting manager based on team and business needs.

We welcome applications from candidates with the right to work in Ireland. For this hiring process, preference will be given to candidates currently based in Ireland.

Why Us?
  • Company performance-related bonus
  • Medical insurance
  • Educational assistance
  • In-house soft skills training
Who We Are

We are a values-driven organization that encourages our employees to bring their authentic selves to work every day and empowers everyone to make a tangible impact on our products, clients, and culture. We offer a dynamic environment with driven, fun, and flexible individuals who thrive on challenge and responsibility. This is an opportunity to contribute to our culture and join a company that’s on the move.

We live the Poppulo values each day, as they are key to everything we do.

  • Bring Your Best Self

We show up authentically, are self-aware and always strive to be better.

  • See it. Own it. Solve it.

We proactively innovate and solve for our customers and each other. We set an example with high standards for our work. We foster a culture of learning, acknowledging our successes and our failures.

  • Together We’re Better

We value and celebrate our diversity. We learn from others, respecting their expertise, and focus on building trust. That's what makes us a team.

Named a Great Place to Work in 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, and 2021, we are a fast-growing global technology company, with offices in Ireland, the US, and the UK.

title: Training Coordinator (science background a must)
description:

Resolian is a leading global Contract Research Organization (CRO) providing specialized services in GxP and non-regulated bioanalysis, drug metabolism/pharmacokinetic (DMPK), and GMP CMC analytical and materials science. Its team of more than 400 experts across the US, UK, and Australia, Resolian supports pharma and biotech companies’ programs throughout the entire drug development continuum.

About the role:

The Site Training & Development Coordinator is responsible for developing, implementing, coordinating, and continuously improving a comprehensive site-wide training and development program within a regulated Contract Research Organization (CRO) environment. This role supports the growth, competency, and compliance readiness of employees across laboratory operations, sample management, project management, quality, scientific, operational, and support functions.

The coordinator serves as the central point of accountability for training governance, onboarding, role-based qualification programs, competency assessment, leadership development, and continuous learning initiatives. Working closely with department leaders, Quality Assurance, Human Resources, and Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), this individual designs and maintains training systems that support employee development, operational excellence, regulatory compliance, inspection readiness, and organizational growth.

This role offers the opportunity to build and mature a best-in-class training culture by establishing scalable learning frameworks, career development pathways, and site-wide competency programs that enhance employee engagement and business performance

Essential Functions:

Training Program Administration

  • Coordinate onboarding and training activities for new laboratory employees.
  • Maintain laboratory training curricula, qualification matrices, and competency assessments.
  • Schedule, track, and document instructor-led, hands-on, and electronic training programs.
  • Ensure training records are complete, accurate, and audit-ready.
  • Monitor training completion and compliance metrics and provide regular status reports to management.

Compliance and Quality Support

  • Ensure training programs comply with GLP, GCP, GMP, CAP, CLIA, ISO, and other applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Support internal audits, client audits, and regulatory inspections by providing training documentation and records.
  • Collaborate with Quality Assurance to address training-related observations, deviations, and corrective actions.
  • Review and update training procedures to align with evolving regulatory requirements and laboratory processes.

Learning and Development

  • Develop training materials, presentations, job aids, and standard operating procedure (SOP) training content.
  • Support implementation and administration of Learning Management Systems (LMS).
  • Facilitate classroom and virtual training sessions as required.
  • Promote continuous learning and professional development within laboratory operations.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with laboratory managers, scientists, technical leads, Human Resources, and Quality Assurance teams.
  • Coordinate training requirements related to new client studies, method validations, equipment qualifications, and process improvements.
  • Communicate training expectations and compliance requirements to stakeholders.

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in biology, Chemistry, Life Sciences, Medical Technology, Education, Training, or a related field preferred.
  • Equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

Experience

  • 3+ years of experience in laboratory operations, training coordination, quality systems, or a regulated healthcare/life sciences environment.
  • Experience within a CRO, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, clinical laboratory, or diagnostic laboratory preferred.
  • Experience managing training records and Learning Management Systems preferred.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Working knowledge of GLP, GCP, GMP, CAP, CLIA, ISO 15189, or related regulatory requirements.
  • Strong understanding of laboratory workflows, SOPs, and quality management systems.
  • Excellent organizational and project management skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple projects and meet deadlines.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and Learning Management Systems.
  • Strong attention to detail and documentation accuracy.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Certification in Training and Development, Quality Management, or Adult Learning.
  • Experience supporting regulatory inspections and client audits.
  • Experience developing laboratory competency programs and training curricula.
  • Familiarity with electronic quality management systems (eQMS).

title: Software Developer II (One year fixed-term position) [611]
description:
About the role

D-Wave is seeking a skilled Software Developer to join our Processor Software team, which plays a key role in creating and maintaining software that supports both the Processor Development (PD) and Hardware Engineering (HWE) teams. The PD team focuses on developing the quantum processor, and the HWE team designs and maintains the hardware necessary to operate and interface with the quantum processor. Together, these teams form the core of D-Wave's advanced quantum computing technology.

The ideal candidate will have a strong background in software and engineering physics, physics, or a related field. A Software Developer on this team will collaborate with programmers, engineers, scientists, and physicists to design, implement and maintain software and infrastructure that interact with our quantum processors in both production and lab environments. The software this position develops will play a role in the calibration, operation, and testing of our quantum processor. The primary language used in the development is Common Lisp (SBCL). The work this position delivers directly impacts the core functionality of our quantum computing system. If you're passionate about software development, quantum computing, and working at the intersection of hardware and software, with a collaborative mindset and a strong desire to learn and solve complex problems, we want to hear from you!

What you'll do

  • Contribute to the full software life-cycle, including development, testing, validation, deployment, maintenance, and decommissioning
  • Collaborate with team members, engineers and scientists to develop the software for quantum processor calibration, hardware interfaces, and operation infrastructure, including system testing and monitoring
  • Enhance the reliability, usability, and maintainability of the software systems by improving test coverage, documentation, and code architecture
  • Maintain, extend, and optimize custom-built software tools for supporting lab operations and ensure smooth interaction between the quantum hardware and software systems
  • Participate in an on-call rotation supporting ensuring the availability and performance of our QPU solvers on the Leap cloud platform


About You

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering physics, electrical/computer engineering, physics, or computer science with a strong aptitude for physics and hardware experience, with 2+ years relevant software experience
  • Proficient in implementing hardware interfaces
  • Experience with Git: branching, merging, issuing pull requests, etc.
  • Experience working in a Linux environment
  • Strong ability to collaborate effectively in interdisciplinary teams and tackle a variety of problems
  • Demonstrated curiosity, flexibility, and passion for learning
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly explain complex concepts
  • Strong critical thinking, problem-solving, and collaboration skills
  • This is a one-year fixed-term position


Bonus Points

  • Familiarity with quantum computing concepts and technologies, including quantum processors and their operational environments
  • Experience developing and optimizing software in compiled languages and in multithreaded environments
  • Experience with Common Lisp or similar language, like Scheme, Clojure, or Scala
  • Experience with Emacs, Docker, Jenkins, SQL, MongoDB, InfluxDB, Grafana, Redis
  • Experience leveraging AI-assisted development tools (e.g., code generation, code review, testing, or documentation) and building AI-powered solutions to improve engineering productivity or automate workflows


A D-Waver's DNA

  • We look at the future and say “why not”; we see possibilities where others see problems or routines. We show the way ahead and are committed to achieving ambitious goals.
  • We practice straight talk and listen generously to each other with empathy. We value different opinions and points of views. We ensure that we connect outside as well as inside to learn from others and inspire each other.
  • We hold ourselves accountable for delivering results. We make decisions & take responsibility so that we can act & support each other.
  • As leaders we motivate & engage our teams to undertake beyond what they originally thought possible, by developing our teams & creating the conditions for people to grow and empower themselves through enabling & coaching.


Our Compensation Philosophy is Simple but Powerful:

We believe providing D-Wavers with company ownership, competitive pay, and a range of meaningful benefits is the start of creating a culture where people want to give the best they’ve got — not because they’re simply making money, but because they’ve fallen in love with our vision, mission, values, and team.


During the interview process, your Recruiter will review our total rewards (base, equity, bonus, perks, benefit, culture) offerings. The final offer is determined by your proficiencies within this level.


Inclusion:

We celebrate diverse perspectives to drive innovation in our pursuit. Our employees range from distinguished domain experts with decades of experience in their respective fields, to bright and motivated graduates eager to make their mark. Our diverse and innovative team will make you feel appreciated, supported and empower your career growth at D-Wave.

We are looking for a highly knowledgeable and experienced Web Analytics Subject Matter Expert with deep expertise in Google Analytics4 (GA4), Google BigQuery(GBQ), and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). As the Associate Director, Web Analytics and the SME, you will provide strategic guidance and technical leadership in the design, implementation, and optimization of analytics solutions. A key focus of this role is owning and managing the integrations between GA4, GBQ, and GCP, enabling scalable data pipelines, advanced reporting, and actionable insights across the organisation. Provide technical consultation and strategic direction for analytics implementations, ensuring scalability and compliance with governance standards. Translate business objectives into robust analytics frameworks and data integration strategies.

Data Integration & Management

Own the setup, governance, and optimization of integrations between GA4, GBQ, and GCP. Design and implement scalable data pipelines and automated workflows for analytics data collection and reporting. Partner with analytics, marketing, and engineering teams to enable advanced reporting, predictive modeling, and activation through GA4-GBQ-GCP integrations including other enterprise data cloud and data lakes.

Business Engagement & Value Demonstration

Lead discussions with business teams to showcase the value of GBQ and GCP analytics solutions. Highlight the business impact of analytics initiatives through storytelling, measurable KPIs, and case studies. Influence stakeholders by demonstrating how GA4-GBQ-GCP integrations drive efficiency, better decision-making, and ROI.

Analytics Implementation and Optimization

Oversee GA4 configuration and maintenance, including event tracking, custom dimensions/metrics, and enhanced eCommerce. Ensure seamless data flow from GA4 into GBQ for advanced analytics and reporting use cases. Provide strategic input into digital marketing measurement (Google Ads, attribution, campaign analytics).

Data Layer & Tagging (Secondary Scope)

Guide and review data layer designs to ensure completeness and scalability. Provide oversight for GTM and other tagging systems where required, while keeping focus on integration with analytics and cloud platforms.

Quality Assurance & Reporting

Define data quality frameworks and oversee validation processes to ensure accuracy across GA4, GBQ, and GCP datasets. Support teams in building advanced dashboards and reports using Looker Studio, GA4, and BigQuery, aligned to business KPIs.

  • Degree qualified in a relevant business or Technical area.

•Ability to grasp, lift and/or carry or otherwise move goods weighing a maximum of 150 lbs. with or without reasonable accommodation.

•Sufficient manual dexterity in hands with or without reasonable accommodation.

•Ability to climb stairs and ladders at a rapid pace with or without reasonable accommodation.

•Ability to perform duties within extreme temperature ranges with or without reasonable accommodation.

•Effective verbal and written communication skills.

•Ability to adapt communication style to suit different audiences, such as effectively communicating with supervisors, coworkers, public etc.

StraitSys is seeking talented professionals to join our successful and growing team to provide support services to the FBI's Finance and Facilities Division (FFD) Huntsville Strategy Team (HST). StraitSys is tasked with coordinating the realignment of FBI resources to Huntsville, Alabama, as part of the FBI’s Strategic Realignment Initiative (SRI). Additionally, this position may explore smaller transition opportunities to Clarksburg, West Virginia, and Pocatello, Idaho.

The SRI includes the potential realignment of over 3,000 positions outside the National Capital Region (NCR), with a focus on enhancing operational efficiency and creating synergies between FBI programs. Areas of emphasis include evaluating current program structures, relocating existing employees, and recruiting and hiring individuals in the Huntsville area. To ensure successful realignment of resources, the FBI has assembled the HST to focus on change management strategy and Division support.

StraitSys is responsible for preparing and assessing the effect of the realignment on the workforce and recommending opportunities for cross-division collaboration.

The Intermediate Communications Specialist will serve as a key communications resource supporting HST leadership and program initiatives. This position will lead and coordinate communications activities, contribute to communications and stakeholder engagement strategy, and provide guidance and quality oversight for communications products. The Intermediate Communications Specialist will work closely with leadership, project teams, stakeholders, and junior communications staff to ensure messaging is consistent, timely, accurate, and aligned with organizational and transition objectives.

Essential Duties

  • Develop, coordinate, and execute communication plans and strategies aligned with organizational priorities, transition objectives, and stakeholder needs.

  • Provide strategic communications support and recommendations to leadership regarding messaging, audiences, communication methods, timing, and stakeholder engagement.

  • Lead the development of executive-ready PowerPoint briefings, presentations, talking points, messaging, and other stakeholder engagement materials supporting leadership communications and decision-making.

  • Develop, review, edit, and coordinate communication products including announcements, presentations, newsletters, reports, talking points, and other internal and external-facing materials.

  • Lead and maintain communication and stakeholder engagement plans, identifying key audiences, communication needs, messaging priorities, communication channels, and opportunities for engagement.

  • Support leadership in developing messaging frameworks and communication approaches for organizational change, workforce transition, strategic initiatives, and other sensitive or high-visibility activities.

  • Lead or support the development and implementation of branding, awareness, outreach, and marketing campaigns that promote program objectives and stakeholder understanding.

  • Coordinate communications activities supporting stakeholder meetings, workshops, outreach activities, town halls, leadership engagements, and special events, including development and review of supporting materials.

  • Serve as a day-to-day communications resource for leadership and project teams, proactively identifying communication needs and recommending appropriate approaches.

  • Review communications products for quality, consistency, tone, accuracy, and alignment with established messaging and organizational objectives prior to leadership review or distribution.

  • Provide day-to-day guidance and coordination to junior communications personnel, including assignment support, review of communication products, and assistance establishing priorities and deadlines.

  • Coordinate communications activities across project teams and stakeholders to promote consistent messaging and reduce duplication or communication gaps.

  • Maintain and improve communication products, presentation libraries, templates, SharePoint content, messaging resources, and other stakeholder-facing materials.

  • Monitor the effectiveness of communication and stakeholder engagement activities and recommend improvements based on stakeholder feedback, emerging needs, and program priorities.

  • Identify communications risks, stakeholder concerns, and emerging issues and elevate recommendations to leadership as appropriate.

Supervisory Responsibilities

This position does not have formal supervisory responsibilities but may provide day-to-day functional leadership, coordination, mentoring, and quality review for junior communications personnel.

Desired Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Experience developing and executing communication strategies, communication plans, stakeholder engagement plans, and messaging frameworks.

  • Experience providing communications support and recommendations to senior leaders and project teams.

  • Demonstrated experience developing executive-level PowerPoint briefings, presentations, talking points, and stakeholder engagement materials.

  • Experience supporting organizational change, workforce transformation, stakeholder engagement, or change management initiatives.

  • Ability to independently develop, review, and refine communications products for senior leadership and diverse stakeholder audiences.

  • Experience coordinating communications for meetings, workshops, town halls, events, outreach activities, and other stakeholder engagements.

  • Strong writing, editing, proofreading, and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor messaging based on audience, purpose, and sensitivity.

  • Ability to translate complex, technical, or sensitive information into clear, concise, actionable, and visually compelling communications.

  • Ability to provide guidance, feedback, and quality review to junior team members while managing competing priorities and deadlines.

  • Strong judgment and interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively with senior leaders, project teams, government stakeholders, and cross-functional teams.

  • Experience with SharePoint and Microsoft 365 tools, including PowerPoint, SharePoint, Teams, and Word.

  • Strong organizational and project coordination skills with the ability to independently manage multiple priorities and deadlines.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university or college with four (4) years or more of relevant business analysis, communications, stakeholder engagement, change management, or related professional experience. Additional relevant professional experience may be substituted for the educational requirement.

  • Active Top Secret Clearance is required.

  • Five (5) years or more of professional experience involving the comprehension, analysis, interpretation, and communication of complex information.

  • Demonstrated ability to develop and present information to leadership and stakeholder audiences and respond effectively to sensitive or complex issues.

  • Demonstrated ability to independently analyze problems, develop recommendations, and coordinate activities involving multiple stakeholders and priorities.

Preferred Experience

  • Five (5) or more years of experience in communications, public relations, strategic communications, stakeholder engagement, change management, or a related field.

  • Experience developing or contributing to strategic communication plans and advising leadership on communication approaches.

  • Experience providing functional leadership, mentoring, work coordination, or quality review for junior communications professionals.

  • Experience supporting federal government programs, preferably within the Department of Justice or FBI environment.

  • Experience supporting large-scale organizational change, workforce transition, transformation, or relocation initiatives.

  • Advanced PowerPoint development and executive briefing skills.

  • Demonstrated ability to operate independently, anticipate communications needs, and manage multiple high-priority deliverables and deadlines.

PREFERENCE STATEMENT

title: VP of Engineering (Canadian candidates only)
description:
Marble is the authorization layer for protected information. The world's most valuable data, from health records to insurance, identity, and legal information, can't be scraped, bought, or moved. It's regulated, it demands consent, and it stays locked behind portals, paper, and legacy systems. Marble is the infrastructure that lets businesses, institutions, and individuals securely access, permission, and use that data, turning trapped records into the compliant, structured information behind high-stakes decisions.

Today, our platform powers two products: Medchart, the medical record request and release platform built on patient consent, and Settlit, which gives US personal injury and mass-tort law firms fast, compliant access to the health and claims data their cases depend on. We started with health and legal, and we're building toward the same consent-driven network across every regulated industry.

We're a Toronto-based team, growing fast and guided by three values: Hungry, Humble, and Care.

The Opportunity

This role exists to bring strategic, technical, and people leadership, and an AI-first operating model, to Marble's engineering organization, so the platform scales reliably and compliantly across Medchart and SettLiT.

We need a leader who owns technical strategy and architecture, instills the operating discipline that turns a growing team into a reliable delivery engine, invests in the engineers we already have, and, critically, leads the AI-first transformation that will define how we build for the next decade.

This is a player-coach executive role. You'll set direction and you'll be in the room for the hard technical calls. You'll design the future of the engineering org, and you'll spend real time coaching the engineers we already have. You'll report directly to the CEO and sit on the Senior Leadership Team, partnering closely with Product, Operations, Sales, and Data Partnerships.

What you'll own in your first year

  • Technical strategy & architecture. Set and socialize a clear technical strategy and architectural-ownership model spanning Medchart and SettLiT (~6 months).
  • Delivery discipline. Install engineering operating rhythms: planning, estimation, code-review standards, release and incident management, so delivery becomes predictable (~6 months).
  • AI-first operating model. Stand up the norms, guardrails, and playbooks that make AI a core part of how we build, ship, and operate, with measurable adoption and productivity impact (~9–12 months).
  • Team design. Define the future engineering org structure and hiring plan; raise the technical bar and clarify career paths for senior and intermediate engineers (~9 months).
  • Quality & compliance. Raise quality-assurance standards across development and data-source implementations, with disciplined release gates that reduce production surprises, and keep our regulated, consent-driven workflows audit-ready as customers, data volumes, and integrations grow.

What you bring

  • 10+ years of engineering experience, including significant time leading engineering teams, most likely as a VP, Director, or Head of Engineering. We care more about demonstrated capability leading through scale than raw tenure.
  • Deep technical and architectural ability. You're comfortable leading architecture reviews, challenging technical assumptions, and coaching a team in a cloud-native, regulated environment. We're an Azure shop, so comfort operating in and around the Azure ecosystem matters; you don't need to be the deepest expert in every service.
  • A track record of embedding AI into engineering, with a clear point of view on what “AI-first engineering” actually means, beyond individual productivity tools.
  • Structure without bureaucracy. Evidence you've brought discipline to a lean team without slowing it down. You know the difference between the process that makes a startup faster and the process that makes it slower.
  • Executive-level cross-functional partnership and clear communication with technical, product, commercial, and executive audiences.

Bonus points

  • HealthTech, Health Data, LegalTech, InsurTech, FinTech, or another regulated-industry background.
  • Familiarity with HIPAA, PHIPA, SOC 2, and consent/authorization frameworks; health data interoperability standards including FHIR, CCDA, claims, pharmacy, and EHR.
  • Experience scaling engineering organizations through growth stages and leading distributed teams.
  • Hands-on with Azure OpenAI, GitHub Copilot, and AI evaluation frameworks covering accuracy, reliability, explainability, and human review.
  • API, data infrastructure, platform-product, or data-orchestration experience.

Where you'll work

Hybrid work, Greater Toronto Area preferred, with regular time at our downtown Toronto office.

How we work

Our three values shape how this role shows up:

  • Hungry. Startup urgency. You proactively drive the AI-first change rather than waiting for permission, and you ship despite ambiguity.
  • Humble. Player-coach. You coach and unblock without taking over, credit the team, invite dissent, and are comfortable saying “I don't know yet.”
  • Care. You invest in the engineers you lead, and you protect security, privacy, and customer trust in every decision.

Why Marble

  • Real mission, real impact. The systems you build move sensitive records that matter to patients, lawyers, insurers, and providers every day.
  • A mandate to set direction. You'll define how engineering operates here, not inherit an org chart someone else built.
  • AI-first, seriously. We are committing to AI as an operating model, not a productivity gimmick. You'll help shape that commitment.
  • A seat at the table. You'll report to the CEO and sit on the Senior Leadership Team, with direct influence on business strategy.
  • A high-caliber team. Small enough that your decisions matter, strong enough that you'll be working with great people from day one.
  • Executive compensation, meaningful equity, comprehensive benefits, and the flexibility of a modern remote-friendly team.

Note: Successful candidates will be asked to undergo a background check.

Marble is proud to be a diverse and equal opportunity employer and as such does not discriminate on the basis of race, colour, religion, sex, national origins, age, sexual orientation, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws. Selection decisions are solely based on job-related factors.

Please note, you will be asked to complete the Plum Discovery Survey, a behavioural assessment provided by our partner, Plum, after submitting your application. After completing the assessment, you will receive your personalized Plum Profile that reveals your Plum Talents, so you can gain a greater understanding of your natural strengths and what makes you, you! You will be provided with a link to complete this survey once you have submitted your application.

Existing Vacancy Disclosure: This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Compensation: The salary for this role is expected to be over $200,000 annually.

title: Analyst (Student Assistant), Talent Analytics & AI
description:
​Do you want to join a global fund manager in energy infrastructure investments? If so, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) is currently looking for an Analyst to join our Talent team based in Copenhagen.

Team

You will join the Talent team, responsible for how CIP attracts, develops and engages the people who drive our long-term success. The team combines people expertise, analytics, technology, and emerging AI capabilities to support strategic talent decisions and enable a high-performing organisation. The team's work spans talent attraction, onboarding, leadership and employee development, performance management, employee engagement, succession planning, and people analytics, ensuring CIP has the talent and capabilities needed to support its continued growth

Role

As a Talent Analytics & AI Analyst in the Talent team, you will support data-driven decision-making across the Talent Area by developing analytical insights, reporting solutions, and decision materials for senior stakeholders. Working closely with colleagues across Talent and the broader business, you will contribute to strategic initiatives spanning people analytics, AI-enabled ways of working, technology, and organisational effectiveness.

This role offers a unique opportunity to work on high-impact business challenges at the intersection of people, data, and technology, making it an ideal environment for someone who thrives in analytical, fast-paced settings and is eager to contribute to talent decision-making in a global organisation. This is an excellent stepping stone toward future roles in people analytics, Talent strategy, or broader business analytics.

The position is approximately 20-25 hours per week alongside your studies, with full flexibility around exam periods.

Responsibilities will consist of but are not limited to:

  • Break down complex business and people-related challenges using structured problem-solving, quantitative analysis, and data-driven thinking to generate insights and recommendations.
  • Develop and evolve reporting solutions, dashboards, and data products across Excel, Power BI, and PowerPoint, leveraging AI-enabled approaches to enhance transparency, improve data quality, and enable better business decisions
  • Apply AI, automation, and workflow technologies to streamline recurring reporting tasks, enhance insight generation, and improve turnaround time on people data requests.
  • Contribute to strategic People & Culture initiatives through research, benchmarking, stakeholder engagement, and project implementation support.

You

We are looking for a highly analytical and intellectually curious student with top academic credentials, proficient Excel and PowerPoint skills, a keen interest in the People space and people analytics, and a history of delivering high-quality work.

You are currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Economics, Business, Finance, Psychology, Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field. Previous experience from consulting, finance, analytics, research, student organisations, or similar analytical environments is beneficial.

We look for the following in a candidate:

  • Analytical & Quantitative Mindset

Solid analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to structure complex challenges, identify key insights, and develop evidence-based recommendations.

  • Advanced Excel & Data Skills

Proficient Excel skills, including pivot tables, lookups, data manipulation and a keen interest in analytics, AI, automation, and data-driven decision-making.

  • Communication & Storytelling

Good communication skills, with the ability to translate analyses and insights into clear, concise, and compelling messages tailored to different audiences.

  • High Work Ethic & Ownership

Demonstrates ownership, intellectual curiosity, and consistent academic excellence and high-quality work while balancing multiple priorities.

Academic performance will be considered as an indicator of discipline, learning agility, and work ethic.

  • Curiosity About People & Talent

Genuine interest in talent, leadership, organisational effectiveness, people analytics, and the future of work.


The process

Please apply online as soon as possible as applications will be processed on an ongoing basis. For questions related to the role, please reach out to our Talent Acquisition team at recruitment@cipfs.com. We do not include CV's and Cover Letters sent by email.


As we continue to improve our candidate experience, diversity and avoid unconscious bias, please avoid having a photo in your CV. We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality for all applicants.


Please be aware that we will not accept speculative CV submissions for any of our roles from recruitment agencies, and any unsolicited candidate submissions will be exempt from any payment expectations and ownership.


---

Building value that matters
Founded in 2012, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners P/S (CIP) today is the world’s largest dedicated fund manager within greenfield renewable energy investments and a global leader in offshore wind. To date, CIP has developed and constructed more than +50 greenfield renewable projects around the world. CIP is developing a greenfield project portfolio of ~160GW total, and ~16 GW is in operation or under construction. CIP manages 13 funds and has to date raised approximately EUR ~35 billion for investments in energy and associated infrastructure from more than ~200 international institutional investors.

CIP has a multinational team of ~500 full-time employees with extensive experience and knowledge within the fields of renewable energy project development and regulated infrastructure. In addition, CIP has a broad range of competencies within corporate finance, mergers & acquisitions, engineering, construction, project development, and project management.

CIP has built a prominent investment team capable of originating proprietary investment opportunities and executing projects and investments based on the team’s industrial background, large industrial network, and extensive experience in structuring, executing, and managing investments within energy infrastructure. Headquartered in Copenhagen, CIP also operates from key locations across the globe, including offices in Hamburg, Munich, London, Utrecht, New York, Tokyo, Melbourne, Luxembourg, Kuala Lumpur, Seoul and Singapore. In addition, CIP has 17 local project offices globally.
