title: Robotics Engineer
description:
The Role

Joining Moderna offers the opportunity to help advance mRNA medicines by developing, testing, and improving engineering solutions that enable Research teams to explore new scientific questions, prototype new capabilities, and accelerate discovery.

This Robotics Engineer role is a hands-on research engineering position for someone with expanded conceptual knowledge in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, mechatronics, automation, robotics, or a related technical discipline. You will independently support the design, assembly, integration, testing, troubleshooting, and refinement of laboratory instruments, experimental platforms, fixtures, prototypes, and automation-enabled research systems. The role requires sound engineering judgment, ownership of moderately complex technical work, the ability to mentor junior team members, and close collaboration with scientists and engineers to translate research needs into reliable, well-documented technical solutions.

Here’s What You’ll Do

  • Independently support the design, assembly, testing, troubleshooting, and iterative improvement of laboratory instruments, fixtures, prototypes, and automation-enabled research systems.

  • Assist with mechanical, electrical, and mechatronic design work, including component selection, basic drawings, wiring, panel layout, sensor integration, and equipment modifications.

  • Participate in system integration and testing, helping connect instruments, controls, sensors, software, and physical hardware into reliable workflows.

  • Develop and execute moderately complex experimental test plans, analyze results using sound engineering judgment, document findings, and recommend next steps based on research objectives and system performance.

  • Solve technical problems through analysis of existing solutions, equipment behavior, data, and user feedback, applying practical engineering experience and judgment to select and implement effective solutions.

  • Provide technical support and guidance for researchers, engineers, and project teams during design, build, commissioning, experimental use, troubleshooting, and iterative improvement activities.

  • Create and maintain clear documentation, including design notes, build records, test data, experimental observations, operating guidance, parts lists, and design change rationale.

  • Identify and implement improvements that increase research system reliability, usability, safety, data quality, experimental flexibility, and team effectiveness.

  • Work within team guidelines and evolving research engineering practices while broadening understanding of system interactions, related technical disciplines, and user needs.

  • Mentor junior engineers or technical team members by sharing practical knowledge, reviewing work, and supporting development of good engineering and documentation practices.

  • Explain complex technical information in straightforward situations, check for understanding, and collaborate effectively with cross-functional research partners.

Here’s What You’ll Need (Basic Qualifications)

  • B.S. or higher with 2+ years or more of relevant experience in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, mechatronics, robotics, automation, research engineering, or a related technical discipline.

  • Demonstrated hands-on experience building, testing, troubleshooting, improving, or maintaining electromechanical systems, prototypes, equipment, fixtures, or automated hardware with increasing independence.

  • Working knowledge of electrical and/or mechanical fundamentals such as sensors, actuators, motors, wiring, power distribution, controls, mechanical assemblies, CAD, or fabrication methods.

  • Ability to use technical experience, data, and engineering judgment to solve moderately complex problems, evaluate options, and recommend practical solutions.

  • Strong documentation habits and attention to detail for design notes, test records, experimental observations, build documentation, and operating guidance.

  • Ability to explain complex technical information clearly, check for understanding, and collaborate with scientists, engineers, and cross-functional research partners.

  • Ability to mentor junior team members, support good engineering practices, and contribute to the quality and effectiveness of work across the team.

  • This position is site-based, requiring you to be at Moderna’s site full-time. This position is not eligible for remote work.

Here’s What You’ll Bring to the Table (Preferred Qualifications)

  • Experience with hands-on electrical or mechanical fabrication, prototyping, machining, 3D printing, wiring, soldering, panel assembly, or equipment repair.

  • Experience with CAD tools, basic electrical schematics, controls hardware, PLCs, microcontrollers, motion systems, sensors, or data acquisition systems.

  • Experience supporting laboratory instruments, research prototypes, experimental automation, or hardware development in a biotechnology, pharmaceutical research, medical technology, or life sciences environment with demonstrated ownership of moderately complex technical work.

  • Programming or scripting experience in Python, C#, MATLAB, LabVIEW, Arduino, or similar tools for experimental testing, data collection, instrument control, automation support, or data analysis.

  • Comfort working directly with equipment, tools, and users in a fast-paced, experimental environment.

  • A desire to make an impact in a mission-driven organization that is Bold, Relentless, Curious, and Collaborative.


Pay & Benefits

At Moderna, we believe that when you feel your best, you can do your best work. That’s why our benefits and well-being resources are designed to support you—at work, at home, and everywhere in between.

  • Competitive healthcare, plus voluntary benefit programs to support your unique needs
  • A holistic approach to well-being, with access to fitness, mindfulness, and mental health support
  • Family planning benefits, including fertility, adoption, and surrogacy support
  • Generous paid time off, including vacation, volunteer days, sabbatical, global recharge days, and a discretionary year-end shutdown
  • Savings and investments to help you plan for the future
  • Location-specific perks and extras

The salary range for this role is $100,400.00 - $160,700.00. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An individual’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, performance, and business or organizational needs.

The successful candidate may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, other incentive compensation, or equity award, subject to company plan eligibility criteria and individual performance.

About Moderna

Since our founding in 2010, we have aspired to build the leading mRNA technology platform, the infrastructure to reimagine how medicines are created and delivered, and a world-class team. We believe in giving our people a platform to change medicine and an opportunity to change the world.


By living our mission, values, and mindsets every day, our people are the driving force behind our scientific progress and our culture. Together, we are creating a culture of belonging and building an organization that cares deeply for our patients, our employees, the environment, and our communities.


We are proud to have been recognized as a Science Magazine Top Biopharma Employer, a Fast Company Best Workplace for Innovators, and a Great Place to Work in the U.S.


If you want to make a difference and join a team that is changing the future of medicine, we invite you to visit modernatx.com/careers to learn more about our current opportunities.


Equal Opportunities

Moderna is committed to equal employment opportunity and non-discrimination for all employees and qualified applicants without regard to a person's race, color, sex, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, ancestry or citizenship, ethnicity, disability, military or protected veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, marital or familial status, or any other personal characteristic protected under applicable law. Moderna is a place where everyone can grow. If you meet the Basic Qualifications for the role and you would be excited to contribute to our mission every day, please apply!


Moderna is an E-Verify Employer in the United States. We consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.


Accommodations

title: Superintendent Environment
description:
• Lead a team of environmental professionals responsible for delivering environmental compliance, risk management and performance outcomes across Rio Tinto Iron Ore operations.

  • Influence environmental strategy, governance, assurance and operational decision-making while developing the capability of a high-performing technical team.

  • Join a collaborative leadership team where you can drive meaningful environmental outcomes and contribute to the safe and sustainable delivery of major operational priorities.

We’re Finding Better Ways™ to provide materials the world needs, now and in the future. Our values – care, courage and curiosity – guide how we work and how we treat each other

About the role

We are looking for a Superintendent Environment to lead a team of Environment Specialists and Site Environmental Advisors to deliver environmental compliance, risk management and performance outcomes across supported assets.

You will provide leadership of environmental delivery through planning, prioritisation, resource coordination, assurance and stakeholder engagement, ensuring environmental obligations, standards and environmental management system requirements are consistently implemented.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced leader to influence environmental performance, support operational decision-making and strengthen environmental capability across a large and complex operational environment.

What you'll be doing

Reporting to the Manager Technical Delivery, you will:

• Lead and develop a team of Environment Specialists and Site Environmental Advisors, fostering a strong safety culture, technical excellence and high performance.

• Provide technical leadership and oversight for Environment Specialists and Site Environmental Advisors, strengthening capability, consistency and quality of environmental delivery.

• Balance environmental priorities and allocate resources across multiple supported assets to optimise risk management and delivery outcomes.

• Provide coaching, mentoring and capability development to strengthen environmental risk, compliance and governance expertise across the team.

• Drive environmental compliance, risk management and performance outcomes across supported assets through effective planning, prioritisation and resource management.

• Act as the primary environmental interface for asset leadership teams, supporting operational decision-making and delivery of environmental obligations.

• Provide technical oversight of environmental approvals, commitments, licences, compliance requirements and environmental management systems.

• Lead environmental incident response, investigations, corrective actions and learnings to improve environmental performance and prevent recurrence.

• Coordinate environmental assurance activities including audits, inspections, critical control verification and action management, ensuring findings are translated into measurable outcomes.

• Build effective partnerships with technical, operational, regulatory and external stakeholders to manage complex environmental issues and improve environmental performance.

About you

We’re looking for someone whose experience aligns with the key requirements below. You do not need to meet every “Helpful for Success” item to apply. If you bring relevant experience and are excited by the opportunity, we encourage you to submit an application.

Required for Success

• A commitment to the safety of yourself and your team.

• Demonstrated leadership experience within environmental, technical or operational teams in a complex industrial environment.

• Strong knowledge of environmental compliance, environmental risk management, governance and assurance processes.

• Extensive experience implementing environmental management systems and driving continuous improvement initiatives.

• Proven ability to prioritise work, manage resources and deliver outcomes across multiple workstreams and stakeholders.

• Strong stakeholder engagement, influencing and communication skills, with the ability to support operational decision-making and manage complex environmental issues.

Helpful for Success

• Tertiary qualification in Environmental Science, Environmental Management, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resource Management or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

• Extensive experience managing environmental approvals, licences, obligations and regulatory requirements within mining, resources or other heavy industry sectors.

• Experience working with environmental assurance frameworks, audits, inspections and critical control verification processes.

• Experience engaging with regulators, Traditional Owners, communities and other external stakeholders to deliver integrated environmental outcomes.

• Demonstrated success leading organisational change, capability development and performance improvement initiatives.

What we offer

Be recognised for your contribution, your thinking and your hard work, and go home knowing you’ve helped the world progress.

· A work environment where safety is always the number one priority

· A permanent position working directly for Rio Tinto

· A competitive base salary reflective of your skills and experience with annual incentive program

· Comprehensive medical benefits including subsidised private health insurance for employees and immediate family

· Attractive share ownership plan

· Company provided insurance cover

· Extensive salary sacrifice & salary packaging options

· Career development & education assistance to further your technical or leadership ambitions

· Ongoing access to family-friendly health and medical wellbeing support

· Leave for all of life’s reasons (vacation/annual, paid parental, personal & cultural leave)

· Exclusive employee discounts (banking, accommodation, cars, retail and more)

· Possible domestic relocation assistance

Where you'll be working

Our modern office located in Central Park tower in Perth provide an inspiring environment for collaboration and professional growth. You'll be able to enjoy a range of benefits, including access to a modern gym, wellness programs, and convenient amenities that support a healthy work-life balance. Situated in the heart of Perth, we are close to public transport and several parking options.

Applications for this role will close Monday 28th September 2026.

About Rio Tinto

Rio Tinto is a leading global mining and materials company. We operate in 35 countries where we produce iron ore, copper, aluminium, critical minerals, and other materials needed for the global energy transition and for people, communities, and nations to thrive.

We have been mining for 150 years and operate with knowledge built up across generations and continents. Our purpose is finding better ways to provide the materials the world needs – striving for innovation and continuous improvement to produce materials with low emissions and to the right environmental, social and governance standards. But we can’t do it on our own, so we’re focused on creating partnerships to solve problems, create win-win situations and meet opportunities.


Respect and Inclusion

At Rio Tinto, we particularly welcome and encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, women, the LGBTQ+ community, mature workers, people with disabilities and people from different cultural backgrounds.

We are committed to an inclusive environment where people feel comfortable to be themselves. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are essential to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation or anything else that makes us different.

description:

Job Description Summary:

The Inspector A is responsible for performing inspections and/or audits of purchased parts, materials, equipment and quality control programs. Interprets manufacturing drawings, diagrams, specifications and lists to approve or reject units or systems for in-process or final assemblies. Performs sampling and testing of incoming components and raw materials. Ensures raw materials, in-process, and finished products meet company standards. Determines or assists in determining methods and procedures necessary for inspection.

Job Description:

Duties/Responsibilities

  • Performs inspections on a variety of materials, components, assemblies, and systems. Types of inspections include visual, workmanship, dimensional, and electrical.

  • Generates and/or revises inspection procedures and associated flows.

  • Performs source inspections at off-site facilities.

  • Identifies problem areas and bottlenecks and assists in resolution.

  • Documents work results and generates inspection reports. Generates procedures to ensure work is performed in a consistent manner.

  • Complies with safety and security rules and observes good housekeeping practices.

  • Assists and trains lower grade personnel toward achievement of inspection tasks. Includes training of new hires to department and lab policies.

  • Accomplishes assignments independent of supervision.


Skills/Abilities

  • Knowledgeable in Microsoft applications such as Word and Excel.

  • Good time management, planning/organization, and decision-making skills.

  • Able to use and interpret engineering drawings, sketches, and work to inspection procedures.

  • Able to follow and execute to verbal and written instructions.

Education

  • A minimum Associates Degree in engineering or science program, A Bachelor's Degree is strongly preferred.

In Lieu required college degree, a minimum of two years of technical schooling may be satisfied through one of the following.

  • High school diploma or its equivalents, plus two years of technical schooling related to engineering or science.

  • Quality Inspector Certification (CQI) from the American Society of Quality (ASQ)

  • Completion of Military Technical School

Experience

  • When education requirements are met, requires a minimum of 5 years’ experience performing tasks related to the inspection of mechanical, electrical and/or electronic components*.

  • When education requirements are not met, requires a minimum of 10 years' experience performing tasks related to the inspection of mechanical, electrical and/or electronic components*.

*Typical Components:

  • For Electronic Inspection - electronic components, printed wiring boards, circuit card assemblies, wafer die, MCM/MEMs products, harnesses, connectors, or other electro-mechanical assemblies.

title: Associate Director, Graduate Business Student Services
description:
Position Title:

Associate Director, Graduate Business Student Services

Position Type:

Regular

Hiring Range:

$33.94 - $40.74 / hour; Compensation will be based on education, experience, skills relevant to the role and internal equity.

Pay Frequency:

Hourly

The Associate Director of Graduate Business Student Services serves as a dynamic, working operational lead within Graduate Business Programs (GBP), balancing advanced individual student advising with the progressive development of departmental leadership capabilities. Operating with a high degree of autonomy and minimal supervision, this position manages an active student portfolio while driving the daily operational success of the Student Services team. Positioned strategically between the Assistant Director and Senior Director roles, the Associate Director translates high-level strategic vision into actionable daily workflows, provides direct work direction and mentorship to Assistant Directors, and partners closely with the Senior Director on programmatic design, enterprise technology implementation, and registration/enrollment forecasting.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Academic Support & Records Management

  • Academic Support Management: Lead the implementation and continuous improvement of the academic support strategy; lead the execution of academic record-keeping structures utilizing current platforms and future admissions/student lifecycle management systems.

  • Advising Strategy & Active Caseload: Formulate and spearhead the comprehensive advising and academic counseling framework designed to optimize retention and satisfaction. Maintain an active, specialized graduate student advising caseload, providing expert guidance on complex degree requirements and academic planning.

  • Systems & Data Integrity: Oversee and authorize critical data updates within the Workday platform for GBP, ensuring absolute data integrity regarding student academic histories.

  • Academic Standing & Performance Analytics: Lead the evaluation, production, and escalation workflows for quarterly academic standing portfolios, managing formal processes for academic warnings, probations, and prestigious recognitions (e.g., Dean’s List, Beta Gamma Sigma), preparing complex cases for Senior Director review.

  • Enrollment Management & Registration Architecture: Architect and manage operational timelines for quarterly registration cycles; direct the generation of strategic enrollment intelligence reports, oversee complex waitlist logistics, and continuously analyze metrics to streamline registration workstreams.

  • Cross-Functional Advocacy: Serve as an institutional champion and liaison to the Bursar’s Office, navigating complex tuition, fee structure, and student account escalations.

  • Degree Conferral & Graduation Logistics: Direct the end-to-end graduation and degree auditing lifecycle; provide executive-level consulting to students on degree path completion and orchestrate the strategic data data aggregation required for Commencement exercises.

2. Student Engagement Operations & Strategic Modeling

  • Programmatic & Operational Excellence: In collaboration with the Sr. Director, oversee the execution and logistical integration of all high-impact programming, managing multi-tier dependencies including off-site programming, catering, grading workflows, and course evaluation tracking.

  • Student Engagement Operations: In collaboration with the Sr. Director, oversee the planning, coordination, and execution of student life programming, ensuring a cohesive and engaging student experience.

  • Fiscal Management: Maintain budget expenditure tracking, and projections for all student engagement initiatives, facilitating data for the Senior Director's budget creation.

  • Compliance Leadership: Partner with and lead departmental collaboration alongside the Title IX Office to guarantee total student compliance with federally mandated training guidelines.

  • Brand Strategy & Vendor Management: Champion and cultivate external vendor networks to source and curate high-quality branded collateral that elevates GBP’s institutional identity.

  • Data-Driven Evaluation: In collaboration with the Sr. Director, conduct comprehensive quarterly analyses and data-driven projections of Student Life operations to evaluate program effectiveness, and optimize future event programming..

3. Graduate Business Programs Curricular & Technological Support

  • Curricular Research & Planning: Research initiatives including "Faculty ASK" data modeling (analyzing unit trends, headcount capacity, and enrollment velocity) to provide the Senior Director with actionable insights for future Academic Year (AY) course offerings and capacity planning.

  • Institutional Liaison: Act as a consultant and institutional liaison across core university pillars, including the Office of Student Life (OSL), Auxiliary Services (AOE), Office of the Registrar, One-Stop, the Bursar's Office, and the Office of the Dean.

  • Continuous Process Improvement: Chair and lead continuous evaluation discussions to rigorously audit services, identify operational friction points, and maximize efficiency across all GBP segments.

  • Program Communications: Oversee student messaging schedules, web content, surveys and newsletters in collaboration with Sr. Director.

  • Information Dissemination & Strategic Partnerships: Co-lead signature GBP events in close partnership with the Senior Director of Graduate Business Programs; oversee the unified deployment of program communication channels including web infrastructure, newsletters, blogs, and targeted campaigns.

PROVIDES WORK DIRECTION

  • Assistant Director: Provides daily operational tasking, mentorship, and delivers annual performance evaluations.

  • Student workers

RECEIVES WORK DIRECTION FROM

  • Senior Director of Graduate Business Programs

  • Assistant/Associate Dean of Graduate Business Programs

GENERAL GUIDELINES & MANAGEMENT COMPETENCIES

  • Quality & Performance Optimization: Act as an internal consultant and champion for quality assurance initiatives, driving systemic changes that directly elevate departmental service delivery.

  • Root-Cause Analysis & Consultation: Conduct comprehensive diagnoses of operational bottlenecks and systemic issues; formulate and deliver formal executive recommendations to senior leadership to optimize established workflows.

  • Productivity & Workforce Enablement: Maximize departmental output by troubleshooting legacy processes and establishing high-efficiency workstreams via the deployment of advanced software tools, structured staff training, and performance metrics.

  • Operational Reporting: Evaluate workflows and provide enrollment/program data to the Senior Director. Synthesize complex operational metrics into executive summaries and progress reports, delivering critical strategic counsel to the Senior Director and the Assistant Dean of GBP to steer long-term institutional goals.

QUALIFICATIONS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The items below are representative of the knowledge, skills, abilities, education, and experience required or preferred. This position requires the ability to effectively establish and maintain cooperative working relationships within a diverse multicultural environment.

Job Title: Scrum Master

Job Location: US - Remote

The Scrum Master owns delivery cadence, team flow, capacity visibility, and blocker removal for a cross-functional digital product team spanning engineering, data, enterprise systems, and design. This role is accountable for how the team works: whether ceremonies drive real decisions, whether capacity and commitments are visible, and whether blockers get cleared before they cost a sprint. The Scrum Master owns the process, rhythm, and health of how the team executes, working directly with functional leads to keep the team unblocked, the cadence predictable, and delivery performance improving over time. This role ensures the team can do its best work, consistently.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own delivery cadence: sprint rhythm, ceremony effectiveness, and team operating norms.
  • Own capacity visibility, ensuring leadership and the Product Owner always have an accurate read on what the team can realistically take on.
  • Own blocker removal, proactively identifying and resolving impediments — technical, organizational, or interpersonal — before they slow delivery down.
  • Own team flow, monitoring work-in-progress, cycle time, and throughput to keep work moving smoothly through the pipeline.
  • Own the health of the delivery process, changing it when it stops working rather than defending it out of habit.
  • Accountable for: Throughput, delivery predictability, cycle time, and team flow health.

Ceremonies & Cadence

  • Facilitate sprint planning, daily standups, sprint reviews, and retrospectives so each ceremony drives a real decision or improvement, not a status recital.
  • Partner with the Product Owner to bring triaged, ready work into the sprint.
  • Keep sprint scope protected once committed, surfacing and pushing back on mid-sprint scope change.
  • Run retrospectives that produce concrete process changes, and track that those changes actually stick.

Flow & Capacity

  • Track and report team capacity, velocity, and commitment reliability on a consistent cadence.
  • Monitor work-in-progress limits, cycle time, and throughput; identify bottlenecks in the delivery pipeline and drive changes to resolve them.
  • Maintain clear, accurate forecasts so the Product Owner and engineering leadership can plan with confidence.
  • Flag capacity risks early, each with a likely impact and a path to resolution.

Delivery Health & Process

  • Track delivery health — flow, throughput, and predictability trends — and report status on a weekly cadence to the Head of Product Engineering.
  • Continuously improve team process and tooling; remove ceremonies or steps that no longer earn their place.
  • Coach the team and functional leads on Agile/Scrum principles, fostering self-organization and continuous improvement.
  • Partner with the Product Owner to keep delivery process aligned with sprint commitments and release scope.
  • Establish and track flow metrics, including cycle time, throughput, capacity utilization, and blocker resolution time, to identify opportunities and drive improvements in delivery performance.

Communications & Collaboration

  • Serve as the team's primary point of contact for questions on process, capacity, and impediments.
  • Communicate team flow health, risks, and blockers clearly to the Product Owner and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Work directly with the Product Owner, UX designer, developers, business systems analysts, and engineers day-to-day.
  • Facilitate cross-team coordination with other Scrum Masters and Product Owners to manage dependencies across teams.

Profile

  • Take ownership without being asked; makes decisions under ambiguity and stands behind them.
  • Direct and decisive in protecting team focus; able to push back on scope creep and hold the team to its commitments.
  • Precise and structured in tracking capacity, flow, and delivery health data.
  • Runs multiple concurrent workstreams without dropping threads; steady under pressure.
  • Improves systems rather than maintaining them.
  • Builds trust and alignment across functional leads and the Product Owner; influences without relying on formal authority.
  • 3+ years of experience as a Scrum Master or in an equivalent agile delivery role, with demonstrated ownership of team flow and delivery predictability.
  • Experience facilitating delivery for multi-platform or cross-functional teams.
  • Strong working knowledge of Agile/Scrum and Kanban methodologies.
  • Comfortable using flow, capacity, and delivery data to identify bottlenecks and drive process improvement.
  • Experience with agile tooling (e.g., Jira, Linear, Azure DevOps) for tracking capacity, velocity, and flow metrics.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Certified ScrumMaster (CSM), Professional Scrum Master (PSM), or equivalent certification.
  • Experience in enterprise software environments.
  • Familiarity with SAFe or other scaled agile frameworks.
  • Background coaching multiple teams simultaneously.
  • Experience working with digital products at scale and within data-driven product teams.

title: Mortgage Lending Representative
description:
Company Overview

County National Bank was founded in 1934 as community bank, and we continue to be committed to serving the communities of southern Michigan. With 13 full-service branches and several other financial services offices, our decisions are made by local associates and board members who have a vested interest in the communities we service. Our mission is to sustain a deep commitment to our community and our tradition of banking excellence.

Our associates are our greatest asset; they are committed to building lasting relationships with clients and coworkers. When you join CNB, you will become a part of a legacy that supports the success of our associates and our communities. If you are looking for a career with purpose and a team that values friendly and knowledgeable service, we encourage you to apply.

CNB is looking for a qualified, motivated, and client- and team-focused individual to join our team as a Mortgage Lending Representative. This position will be housed ON-SITE at either of our Tecumseh or Adrian locations.

JOB SUMMARY

The Mortgage Lending Representative is a developmental position designed to provide hands-on experience and training in the mortgage lending process with the goal of preparing the individual to become a successful Mortgage Lender. The role will develop knowledge and proficiency in loan origination, credit analysis, underwriting guidelines, compliance requirements, and mortgage products. The individual will work closely with experienced mortgage professionals to gain practical knowledge of the lending process from application through closing. Responsibilities will progressively increase as skills and knowledge are developed, including assisting with client interactions, gathering and reviewing loan documentation, and supporting loan production activities. The position requires a strong commitment to learning, attention to detail, client service, and the ability to build effective relationships with borrowers and internal partners.

Key Responsibilities

• Develop mortgage lending knowledge by participating in structured training and on-the-job learning to build knowledge of mortgage products, loan programs, credit requirements, underwriting guidelines, and the overall mortgage lending process.
• Assist with loan origination activities by supporting Mortgage Lenders with loan applications, documentation, disclosures, and other activities involved in originating and processing mortgage loans.
• Develop the ability to effectively communicate with prospective and existing borrowers, understand their financing needs, answer questions, and provide a positive lending experience.
• Assist in gathering, organizing, and reviewing borrower information and supporting documentation for completeness and accuracy while developing an understanding of credit and financial analysis.
• Maintain compliance and risk awareness by learning and consistently following applicable lending laws, regulations, policies, procedures, and internal controls to ensure mortgage lending activities are conducted accurately and compliantly.
• Build relationships with borrowers, real estate professionals, and internal partners while learning effective strategies for generating and developing mortgage lending opportunities.
• Demonstrate increasing knowledge, skill, and proficiency in mortgage lending responsibilities, with the goal of transitioning into a Mortgage Lender role capable of independently managing customer relationships and loan opportunities.

Qualifications

Required:
• High School diploma or equivalent
• Previous experience in banking, financial services, sales, client services, or related field
Preferred:
• Associate or Bachelor's degree in business, economics, or related field

Skills

• Exceptional leadership and development skills
• Ability to think strategically and plan business objectives
• Strong relationship building abilities
• Outstanding verbal, written and presentation skills with executive presence
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
• Ability to influence and collaborate without direct authority
• Effective decision-making skills with sound business judgement

Work Environment

This position is an on-site position located in one of our Tecumseh or Adrian offices, requiring occasional travel.

Physical Requirements
• Sit/stand for long periods of time
• Ability to see difference between colors, shades, and brightness to identify documents
• Comfort with using a phone, fax, or other devices for calls, document sharing, and communication

title: Press Assistant Trainee - Night
description:
Rotating Night Shift 6PM-6AM

Position Summary:

The Press Assistant is responsible for assisting the Press Operator in setting up and operating a Press to produce print on label rolls as well as being able to operate a press or die-cutter with basic blank or simple color products safely and effectively.

Essential Job Functions:

Operation

· Setup and verify the placement of specified anilox rolls, setting print cylinders in proper print stages, filling ink, and the proper material at the press

· Setup and verify the placement of the correct inks, coating, and varnish

· Setup and verify correct plate and registration, unwind position, size/height/width during make ready

· Load proper film onto unwind

· Fill ink pumps, secures hoses, and transfers ink to designated printing unit

· Set ink viscosities to prescribed standards using Zahn cup and timer

· Lift and transport ink kits as necessary

· Evaluate and monitor color and defects during the run and adjust accordingly

· Evaluate and adjust register during make-ready and run

· Proper monitoring, upkeep, change and disposal of doctor blades

· Assist operator in matching printed ink samples to color standards at prescribed intervals

· Watch web for problems during operator absence and reacts accordingly

· Secure materials for impending jobs as production activity allows

· Return ink and other materials to their designated storage areas with proper information attached

· Perform other duties and/or responsibilities as assigned

· Report any safety concerns to management immediately

Quality Control

· Verify adequate number of feet have been run to satisfy the order quantity

· Check for defects and correct side to print on using base film guide

· Check ink viscosities at prescribed intervals and ensures ink volume sufficiency

Maintenance

· Maintain accurate weight records

· Maintain adequate ink and film supplies to press and replenishes unwind material as required

· Clean equipment and keep work area neat and organized

Reporting and Record Keeping

· Document ink viscosities at prescribed intervals

· Verify all job-related items (job bag and contents, Flexo Inspection Verification signoffs, Job History Sheet, press and press area clean, etc.) are complete prior to next job

· Record of all data and comments regarding position of colors, plates, and anilox rolls on the ink history sheet

Compliance/Other tasks

· Comply with all company policies and procedures including GMP, PPE, HACCP, LOTO, and JSA regulations.

· Responsible for ensuring, where applicable, the product safety, quality, regulatory compliance and legality of all products produced and sold.

Qualifications:
High school diploma or GED is required. Technical or trade school background is preferred. Printing Flexo experience or equivalent printing experience is strongly preferred. Candidates should have working knowledge of mechanical, pneumatic, and hydraulic systems. Familiarity with RF scanning, warehouse systems, and material handling equipment such as pallet jacks or powered industrial trucks is required. Must be able to read and understand production documents, safety guidelines, and quality control checklists. Good communication skills, attention to detail, and basic math skills are essential. Candidates must be able to lift up to 50 pounds and stand for long periods of time in a manufacturing environment.

Work Environment

· Safety glasses with side shields, hearing protection, and steel-toed shoes are required. In addition, task specific PPE may be required.

· Our Manufacturing plant is not environmentally controlled. Changes in humidity and temperature occur throughout the year.

Other

Work in accordance with all company policies and procedures regarding employment.

Help transform our multimodality product development labs from manual, time intensive workflows, into an automated, scalable, and scientist-friendly ecosystem by defining ontologies, vocabularies, and metadata models that accelerate decisions, strengthen data integrity, and ready the organization for advanced automation and AI/ML. As the team’s primary interface to the Alexion Data Office (ADO) and the lead point of contact to Alexion IT, you will drive bidirectional alignment on data standards and platform implementation while partnering closely with Lab Automation and Orchestration leads. Help us accelerate life-changing therapies to patients with rare and ultra-rare diseases.

This is what you will do:
  • Design ontologies and metadata models for key domains (chromatography, spectroscopy, assays, automation runs, process parameters, samples/lineage) with governance, versioning, and change control.
  • Define and publish data contracts and canonical schemas; embed standards into ingestion, validation, and transformation; enforce lineage, provenance, and data quality rules.
  • Build reference implementations (schema registry, conformance tests, enrichment services) integrated with Databricks on AWS and enterprise catalogs; align with ELN/LIMS/SDMS connectors.
  • Curate data products exposing consistent entities/relationships; enable self-service discovery, governed APIs/views, and downstream ML feature stores.
  • Lead cross functional standards forums; deliver documentation, examples, and training; measure adoption, conformance, and time to data improvements.
  • Serve as primary liaison to ADO and Alexion IT for data standards, catalogs, and governance tooling; maintain a bidirectional communication cadence with Lab Automation and Orchestration leads to ensure implementation fidelity
You will be responsible for:
  • Enterprise grade ontology/vocabulary releases with governance artifacts (stewardship roles, RACI, version notes) and deprecation/change communications.
  • Contracted schemas and metadata policies embedded into pipelines and catalogs, including automated conformance checks, issue triage, and remediation guidance.
  • Cataloged, discoverable data products with lineage and role-based access controls suitable for audit sensitive environments, with periodic quality reviews and reporting.
  • A roadmap and backlog for semantic standards aligned with product and platform roadmaps, measurable gains in adoption, conformance, time to data, and reuse across teams.
  • External/internal stakeholder alignment: single point ownership for ADO/IT coordination on standards, catalogs, and reference implementations supporting PDCS use cases.
You will need to have:
  • Education/experience: PhD + 4 years, or MS + 8 years, or BS + 12 years in Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Engineering, or related, including 7+ years of hands‑on data modeling, ontology, and metadata engineering with standards embedded in production pipelines and experience with lakehouse/catalog platforms (for example, Databricks on AWS).
  • Demonstrated skills in semantic modeling, schema design, data contracts, lineage/provenance, and data quality frameworks/governance tooling.
  • Proficiency in Python/SQL for implementation and validation.
  • Strong cross functional communication and the ability to drive consensus across data, IT, and laboratory stakeholders.
  • Ability to travel to New Haven, CT ~4x/year, 2–4 weeks per trip, to work face to face with laboratory practitioners and gain hands on familiarity with equipment and robotics.

The duties of this role may require periodic work in a laboratory or manufacturing environment. As is typical of such roles, employees must be able, with or without an accommodation to: lift/carry 15/30 pounds unassisted/assisted; work comfortably in a controlled environment with and around hazardous materials; gown/degown PPE; use a computer; engage in communications via phone, video, and electronic messaging; engage in problem solving and non-linear thought, analysis, and dialogue; collaborate with others; maintain general availability during standard business hours.

We would prefer for you to have:
  • CMC/lab data familiarity (ELN/LIMS/SDMS, instrument domains) and experience operationalizing metadata services and ML feature workflows; domain experience preferred but not required.

Date Posted 03-Sept-2026

Closing Date 16-Sept-2026

We welcome and consider applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of characteristics. We offer reasonable adjustments/accommodations to help all candidates to perform at their best.

title: Sr Software Engineer - DevOps & Automation Tools Engineer
description:
At MiniMed, you can begin a lifelong career of exploration and innovation, while helping make a difference in the lives of people living with diabetes around the globe. You'll lead with purpose, breaking down barriers to innovation for a more connected, compassionate world.

About the Role

A Day in the Life

Our Global Diabetes Capability Center in Pune is expanding to serve more people living with diabetes globally. Our state-of-the-art facility is dedicated to transforming diabetes management through innovative solutions and Technologies that reduce the burden of living with diabetes.

This position is an exciting opportunity to work with Minimed’s Diabetes business. Medtronic has announced its intention to separate the Diabetes division to promote future growth and innovation within the business and reallocate investments and resources across Medtronic, subject to applicable information and consultation requirements. This separation provides our team with a bold opportunity to unleash our potential, enabling us to operate with greater speed and agility. As a separate entity, we anticipate leveraging increased investments to drive meaningful innovation and enhance our impact on patient care.

#BetterDaysStartNow

DevOps + Automation Engineer with a proven track record of managing and automating end-to-end CI/CD lifecycles in a fast-paced environment or in regulated industries (such as Medical Devices, Aerospace, or Automotive).

Responsible for designing, automating and maintaining robust build pipelines, automating software control (SCM) processes, and seamlessly integrating automated testing frameworks—including Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) environments. A critical part of this role will be automating compliance reporting, code quality gates (MISRA/SAST), and audit trail documentation to conform with medical device standards like IEC 62304.

  • End-to-End Regulated SCM & Gatekeeping: Expert-level mastery of Git workflows (GitLab/GitHub) configured with strict, automated compliance gates to guarantee absolute audit trails and change control.

  • Continuous Compliance & Automated DHF Reporting: Hands-on ability to automate code quality scans (MISRA/SAST) and auto-generate audit-ready test reports for the Design History File (DHF) to satisfy IEC 62304 and FDA requirements.

  • Hardware & Software-in-the-Loop Integration: Proven experience bridging the digital-to-physical gap by integrating virtual hardware emulators (like Renode) and physical HIL test fleets directly into the automated CI/CD pipeline.

  • Robust Multi-Platform Build Orchestration: Deep expertise building reusable, scalable pipelines (GitLab CI/GitHub Actions) capable of handling both cloud services and low-level embedded/firmware cross-compilation toolchains.

  • CI/CD Orchestration: Deep expertise in GitLab CI/CD and GitHub Actions, with an emphasis on building reusable, modular, and secure pipeline templates.

  • Pipeline/Lab Observability: Establishing dashboards (Elasticsearch, Grafana, or native tool reporting) to monitor pipeline health, test pass/fail trends, and build performance metrics.

  • Multi-Platform Compilation: Experience managing build toolchains for cross-compilation (e.g., GCC, Clang, IAR, Keil for ARM/STM32/Nordic microcontrollers).

  • Artifact Lifecycle: Strong management of secure artifact repositories (JFrog Artifactory, Nexus, or native GitLab/GitHub package registries) with strict versioning and immutable release tagging.

  • Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Proficiency in Terraform, Ansible to manage physical or virtual build agents/runners reliably.

  • Traceability Automation via Tooling: Skilled at using APIs and manifest files to programmatically link requirements (Jira) to source code and test execution results, eliminating manual mapping errors.

  • Python (and frameworks), Yaml, React, AI+MCP+RAG etc. (Nice to have)


Responsibilities may include the following, and other duties may be assigned.

  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines. Work with cloud
  • Utilize multi-cloud infrastructure as code (IAC) and application deployment skills.
  • Develop and manage software configuration management plans (SCMP) for product development.
  • Automate SCM workflows with scripts for end-to-end pipelines and compliance.
  • Enhance developer experience through engineering tools for productivity, quality, and test automation in the SDLC.
  • Improve product quality and development efficiency by implementing new tools.
  • Scale and architect CI/CD workflows.
  • Provide DevOps coaching and support.
  • Responsible for testing, troubleshooting, and fixing code and deployment errors on Linux and Windows.
  • Generates systems software engineering policies, standards and procedures.
  • May work across a variety of software lifecycle activities as determined by program needs.

Must Have Competencies

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering or Computer Science with 5+ years of experience.
  • Extensive experience in building CI/CD pipelines with DevSecOps practices and compliance-as-code.
  • Proficient in Infrastructure as Code (IaC) using Terraform and CloudFormation for application deployments and quality checks.
  • Significant experience in production test automation within CI/CD pipelines.
  • Comfortable working in command-line environments on Windows, Linux, and MacOS; system administration is a plus.
  • Experience in Docker, Git/GitHub, Artifactory, Ansible, Terraform, AWS, Azure DevOps, and Kubernetes.
  • Seeking a skilled DevOps Engineer focused on operational excellence through automation.
  • A self-starting and motivated individual with strong collaboration skills and the ability to present ideas confidently.
  • Skilled at crafting detailed and engaging documentation that informs and inspires.

TECHNICAL SPECIALIST CAREER STREAM: An individual contributor with responsibility in our technical functions to advance existing technology or introduce new technology and therapies. Formulates, delivers and/or manages projects assigned and works with other stakeholders to achieve desired results. May act as a mentor to colleagues or may direct the work of other lower level professionals. The majority of time is spent delivering R&D, systems or initiatives related to new technologies or therapies – from design to implementation - while adhering to policies, using specialized knowledge and skills.

DIFFERENTIATING FACTORS

Autonomy: Seasoned individual contributor. Works independently under limited supervision to determine and develop approach to solutions. Coaches and reviews the work of lower level specialists; may manage projects / processes.

Organizational Impact: May be responsible for entire projects or processes within job area. Contributes to the completion of work group objectives, through building relationships and consensus to reach agreements on assignments.

Innovation and Complexity: Problems and issues faced are difficult, and may require understanding of multiple issues, job areas or specialties. Makes improvements of processes, systems or products to enhance performance of the job area. Analysis provided is in-depth in nature and often provides recommendations on process improvements.

Communication and Influence: Communicates with senior internal and external customers and vendors. Exchange information of facts, statuses, ideas and issues to achieve objective, and influence decision-making.

Leadership and Talent Management: May provide guidance, coaching and training to other employees within job area. May manage projects, requiring delegation of work and review of others' work product.

Required Knowledge and Experience: Requires advanced knowledge of job area combining breadth and depth, typically obtained through advanced education combined with experience. May have practical knowledge of project management. Requires a Baccalaureate degree (or for degrees earned outside of the United States, a degree which satisfies the requirements of 8 C.F.R. § 214.2(h)( 4)(iii)(A) and minimum of 4 years of relevant experience, or advanced degree with a minimum of 2 years relevant experience.

Physical Job Requirements

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this position, but they are not an exhaustive list of all the required responsibilities and skills of this position.


Benefits & Compensation


MiniMed offers a competitive salary and flexible benefits package

At MiniMed, we put people first. A commitment to our employees lives at the core of our values: We recognize their contributions. They share in the success they help create. We offer a wide range of benefits, resources, and competitive compensation plans designed to support you at every stage of your career and life.



About MiniMed

We want to make every day a better day for people living with diabetes. Our team of creative innovators around the globe share a passion for finding the simplest solutions to the problems that people with diabetes face on a daily basis. For more than 40 years, we've been redefining what's possible, from intelligent dosing systems designed for real life to predictive insights that stay a step ahead, and we're dedicated to continuing to support our customers through every step of their journey — meeting them where and how they need it.

title: Community Health Worker
description:
We’re unique. You should be, too.

We’re changing lives every day. For both our patients and our team members. Are you innovative and entrepreneurial minded? Is your work ethic and ambition off the charts? Do you inspire others with your kindness and joy?

We’re different than most primary care providers. We’re rapidly expanding and we need great people to join our team.

The Social Complex Coordinator, CHW is a vital HCT member who will use strong local community knowledge to help engage patients in our primary care model, deepening the patient relationship with us and the patient's understanding of their care plan. The incumbent will facilitate visits with our physicians through video during these community visits. The Social Complex Coordinator, CHW, Complex Care will also use telephonic outreach to ensure patients are doing well after hospital discharge and during other times of increased medical risk to the patients. The incumbent will work closely with our nurse care managers and social workers to support a multidisciplinary approach to meeting our most complex patients' medical and social needs. The incumbent will also help the HCT with patient scheduling and other tasks as determined by the team leaders.

ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Assists patients in their homes with telehealth visits with their Primary Care Physicians
  • Works with patients assigned to us who are not actively engaged in care to link them to our physicians with the goal of full engagement in our model of care.
  • Assesses patient need for transportation to and from appointments with primary providers. Coordinates with centers to schedule or assist patients with transportation for specialty appointments outside our centers based on their health plan policies.
  • Assists patients and families with connecting to community resources, including help with applications for eligible programs such as Medicaid.
  • Performs discharge phone calls within 24-72 hours post-discharge from the inpatient setting. (Hospital, SNF, Long Term Acute Care Hospital (LTACH) using post-discharge script explaining our services and obtaining consent for visits and uploading to patient's chart.
  • Communicate between the patient and discharge champion in the center to ensure the patient has a 4-day post-discharge appointment to see their Primary Care Physician (PCP).
  • Works collaboratively and effectively within the team of Community Nurses and Community Social Workers on their visit schedule, maintaining excellent communication with Nurses and Social Workers while maintaining their schedule and calendar.
  • Coaches patients in effective management of their chronic health conditions and self-care
  • Motivates patients to be active, engaged participants in their health.
  • Continuously expands knowledge and understanding of community resources, services, and programs provided; human relations and the procedures used in dealing with the public as part of a service or program; volunteer resources and the practices associated with using volunteers, operations, functions, policies, and procedures associated with the department or program area, procedures, and resources available to handle new, unusual, or different situations.
  • Attends meetings and reports on patients as assigned.
  • Performs other duties as assigned and modified at the manager’s discretion.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

  • Competent-level business acuity
  • Comprehensive knowledge and understanding of general/core job-related functions, practices, processes, procedures, techniques and methods
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills and ability to work effectively with a wide range of people in a diverse community with our values of Love, Accountability and Passion.
  • Ability to work autonomously.
  • Strong time management skills and ability to prioritize patient visits and tasks.
  • Comfort working in fast-paced setting with a willingness to adapt to change.
  • Proficient in Microsoft office suite products including Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook database and presentation software.
  • Ability and willingness to travel locally to patient homes up to 50% of the time.
  • Spoken and written fluency in English (bilingual preferred)

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE CRITERIA:

  • High School diploma or equivalent required.
  • Experience working with geriatric patients is a plus.
  • Established a track record of excellent data management skills.
  • A minimum of 2 years working in a healthcare setting with patient-facing responsibilities.
  • A minimum of 2 years working directly with a primary care physician in an outpatient setting is preferred.
  • Any combination of three (3) years of health/social services experience and/or education
  • Must possess a valid driver's license with a verifiable good driving record and reliable transportation.




PAY RANGE:

$20.2 - $28.83 Hourly

The posted pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for this position. Final compensation will depend on a variety of factors including but not limited to experience, education, geographic location, and other relevant factors. This position may also be eligible for a bonuses or commissions.

EMPLOYEE BENEFITS

We’re ChenMed and we’re transforming healthcare for seniors and changing America’s healthcare for the better. Family-owned and physician-led, our unique approach allows us to improve the health and well-being of the populations we serve. We’re growing rapidly as we seek to rescue more and more seniors from inadequate health care.

ChenMed is changing lives for the people we serve and the people we hire. With great compensation, comprehensive benefits, career development and advancement opportunities and so much more, our employees enjoy great work-life balance and opportunities to grow.   • Manage end-to-end user research, including participant recruiting, interviews, surveys, analysis, and synthesis.
  • Conduct user research, interviews, and surveys and translate findings into:
    • Sitemaps
    • User flows
    • User journey/customer journey maps
    • Wireframes
    • Mockups
    • Prototypes
  • Facilitate the client's product vision through researching, conceiving, sketching, prototyping, and user-testing experiences.
  • Design experiences optimized for a wide range of devices and interfaces.
  • Identify design problems and develop elegant, intuitive solutions.
  • Make strategic UX and design decisions relating to existing and new product functions and features.
  • Gather user feedback and use it to configure and improve existing interfaces.
  • Design user interfaces for web and mobile applications, as well as digital displays, publications, media, and other creative materials as required.
  • Work within the limitations and appropriate use of web development technologies.
  • Consider the emotional aspects of the human experience when designing online programs.
  • Collaborate with developers, QA specialists, business stakeholders, and cross-functional teams to achieve project objectives.
  • Manage competing priorities while meeting deadlines and maintaining effective client/stakeholder relationships.
  • Prepare clear, concise, and comprehensive design documentation, reports, reviews, and assessments.


Requirements

Mandatory Skills & Experience
Candidates must demonstrate experience in the following areas:
UX / UI Design
  • Relevant experience creating GUI designs based on user interaction and performance.
  • Experience as a UX Designer, Interactive Designer, UI Designer, or similar role, designing for web and mobile applications.
  • Ability to define and lead UX projects and facilitate design workshops and alignment sessions with stakeholders and business users.
  • Experience managing end-to-end user research, from recruiting participants through research synthesis.
  • Proficiency with design and prototyping tools.
  • Experience with Figma, Canvas, and similar design tools.
  • Thorough understanding of the limitations and appropriate use of web development technologies.
  • Experience designing online programs with emphasis on the emotional aspects of human experience.
  • Experience conducting user research, interviews, and surveys and translating findings into sitemaps, user flows, user journey maps, wireframes, mockups, and prototypes.
  • Experience designing overall product functionality and iterating designs based on user-testing.
  • Experience designing and delivering wireframes, user stories, user flows, user journeys, mockups, and prototypes optimized for a wide range of devices and interfaces.
  • Experience facilitating a client's product vision through research, conceiving, sketching, prototyping, and user-testing.
  • Experience identifying design problems and devising elegant and effective solutions.
  • Experience making strategic design and UX decisions related to core and new functions/features.
  • Experience gathering user feedback and using it to configure existing interfaces.
Accessibility / Ontario Public Sector
The successful candidate must also have:
  • Knowledge of accessibility testing.
  • Ability to work with the Ontario Design System.
  • Knowledge of the Ontario Digital Service Standard.
  • Proficiency in designing with accessibility in mind and meeting WCAG 2.1 AA requirements.
  • Experience dealing with complex design challenges, particularly legacy systems and nuanced stakeholder/approval relationships.
Communication & Collaboration
  • Demonstrated ability to prepare clear, concise, and comprehensive documentation, including reports, reviews, and assessments.
  • Ability to communicate design concepts and development processes clearly to diverse stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated effectiveness working with cross-functional teams, including developers, QA specialists, and business stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated experience working collaboratively with team members at different organizational levels.
  • Strong track record of meeting deadlines and managing competing priorities.
  • Client relationship management experience.
Desirable Experience
The following experience is considered an asset:
  • Prior Ontario Public Service / Public Sector experience.
  • Experience working with the Ontario Design System and Digital Service Standard.
  • Experience with accessibility testing and WCAG 2.1 AA compliance.
  • Experience working with complex legacy applications and systems.
  • Experience navigating complex stakeholder groups and approval processes.
  • Experience designing for multiple device types, platforms, and interfaces.
Communication & Stakeholder Requirements
The successful candidate will be expected to:
  • Clearly communicate UX concepts, research findings, design decisions, and recommendations.
  • Translate complex technical and user requirements into understandable design solutions.
  • Facilitate workshops, stakeholder discussions, and design alignment sessions.
  • Collaborate effectively with business users, product teams, developers, QA teams, and other stakeholders.
  • Produce professional documentation and design deliverables.
  • Manage multiple priorities while maintaining quality and meeting project timelines.
Work Arrangement
This is a 100% onsite position requiring the successful candidate to work onsite 5 days per week in Ontario.
Candidates should be comfortable working in a highly collaborative environment involving frequent interaction with stakeholders, business users, developers, QA specialists, and project teams.
Ideal Candidate Profile
The ideal candidate will be a Junior UX Designer with hands-on experience in web and mobile UX/UI design, strong user research and prototyping capabilities, and practical experience with Figma, Canvas, accessibility, the Ontario Design System, and Digital Service Standards.
Candidates should be able to demonstrate a complete UX lifecycle—from research and stakeholder engagement through journey mapping, wireframing, prototyping, user testing, feedback, iteration, and final design delivery.
Important: Candidates must clearly demonstrate the mandatory UX, accessibility, Ontario Design System, Digital Service Standard, Figma/Canvas, research, workshop facilitation, and user-testing experience in their resumes.

title: Community Director
description:
With more than 225 branch offices across North America, Associa is building the future of community for nearly five million residents worldwide. Our 11,000+ team members lead the industry with unrivaled education, expertise, and trailblazing innovation. For more than 43 years, Associa has brought positive impact and meaningful value to communities. To learn more, visit .



Job Description

Are you an experienced community association leader who thrives on building trusted relationships, solving complex problems, and delivering exceptional service?

Blue Mountain Community Management, an Associa company, is seeking a Community Director to serve as our local leader and client advocate in the Seattle market. This highly visible role is ideal for someone who understands Washington community association requirements, enjoys working directly with boards and vendors, and knows how to strengthen client relationships through proactive, high-touch support.

You will serve as the primary local presence for our Seattle-area clients while partnering closely with our Oregon-based community management team. Your focus will be on board relationships, client retention and satisfaction, vendor oversight, statutory guidance, and identifying opportunities to deliver additional value. You may also directly manage a select portfolio of high-touch communities.

What You’ll Do

Serve as a Local Leader and Trusted Advisor

  • Build strong, trusted relationships with Seattle-area boards, homeowners, vendors, and business partners
  • Maintain a visible presence in the Seattle market and provide on-site leadership when needed
  • Serve as a strategic advisor to boards, helping them navigate operational challenges and make informed decisions
  • Proactively monitor client satisfaction, address concerns, and identify opportunities to strengthen long-term relationships
  • Represent Blue Mountain professionally within the local community association market

Support and Retain Key Clients

  • Oversee the service experience, retention, and overall satisfaction of Seattle-area clients
  • Provide high-touch support to key accounts and potentially manage a select portfolio of complex or high-value communities
  • Coordinate with the Oregon-based community management team to ensure routine operational needs are handled efficiently
  • Step in when local expertise, board engagement, vendor coordination, or an on-site presence is required
  • Develop a strong understanding of each client’s priorities, challenges, and expectations

Provide Washington-Specific Expertise

  • Maintain current knowledge of Washington statutes and requirements affecting community associations
  • Translate regulatory information into practical guidance for community managers, boards, and internal partners
  • Keep the team informed of relevant legislative and regulatory developments
  • Help promote consistent, compliant community management practices throughout the Seattle portfolio

Oversee Vendors and Revenue Opportunities

  • Develop and maintain productive relationships with local vendors and service providers
  • Provide on-site oversight for significant projects, higher-value work, and complex vendor matters
  • Identify and manage billable service opportunities that create value for clients and support branch performance
  • Assist with bids, contract discussions, project coordination, and vendor accountability as needed

Support Strategic Partnerships and Growth

  • Provide local support for strategic homebuilder and developer relationships, including association-related matters connected to land acquisitions
  • Help ensure continuity of service and institutional knowledge during leadership transitions
  • Identify opportunities to expand Blue Mountain’s presence and relationships in the Seattle market
  • Contribute to business development, strategic planning, and financial performance

Requirements

What You Bring

  • Five or more years of community association management experience, with direct experience in Washington strongly preferred
  • Demonstrated success working with community association boards, homeowners, vendors, and business partners
  • Strong working knowledge of Washington statutes and requirements affecting community associations
  • Experience managing complex, high-touch, or large-scale communities
  • Proven ability to strengthen client relationships, resolve concerns, and support retention
  • Strong business judgment and the ability to identify opportunities that benefit both clients and the organization
  • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills
  • A proactive, self-directed approach with strong organizational and prioritization skills
  • Ability to work collaboratively with team members located in another market
  • Ability to travel locally throughout the Seattle area and attend evening board meetings as needed
  • Bachelor’s degree preferred
  • Industry certification such as CMCA, AMS, or PCAM preferred
  • Any location-specific license required for the position

Why Join Blue Mountain?

This is an opportunity to become the face of Blue Mountain in the Seattle market and make a meaningful impact from day one. You will have the autonomy to build relationships, shape the local client experience, and provide the hands-on leadership our boards and partners value, while also benefiting from the resources, training, and support of Associa.

Compensation

$95,000–$100,000 annually. Directly related community association experience, Washington market knowledge, professional designations, and overall qualifications will be highly considered when determining compensation.

Benefits Summary

  • Vacation accrual begins after 90 days at 6.67 hours per month, with a cap of 160 hours depending on years of service
  • Employees who are active and full-time are eligible to accrue 3.34 hours of sick time per month, up to a maximum of 40 hours (5 days) per calendar year
  • 401(k) offered
  • 9 paid holidays
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage offered
  • Short- and long-term disability coverage, plus other voluntary insurance options
  • World-class training
  • Individual and branch achievement bonuses
  • CAI (Community Associations Institute) course and designation assistance
  • Employee Referral Bonus Program
  • Wellness incentives

The above information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed in this position. It is not intended to be a comprehensive list of all duties, responsibilities, and qualifications required.

Associa is an Equal Opportunity Employer.




We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, age, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.
