title: Primary Care Physicia (Locum)
description:
We’re unique. You should be, too.

We’re changing lives every day. For both our patients and our team members. Are you innovative and entrepreneurial minded? Is your work ethic and ambition off the charts? Do you inspire others with your kindness and joy?

We’re different than most primary care providers. We’re rapidly expanding and we need great people to join our team.

ChenMed, a physician-led and mission-driven, primary care organization, is currently one of the most successful full-risk Medicare Advantage providers in the nation and has a vision to be America’s leading primary care provider, transforming care of the neediest population. Our mission is to honor seniors with affordable VIP care that delivers better health. In order to achieve our vision and deliver our mission, we need the best primary care providers that are seeking to fulfill purpose and personal opportunity and join the ChenMed family.

The Primary Care Physician (PCP) in our organization demonstrates:

• Accountability for outcomes: The PCP demonstrates accountability for outcomes, strong clinical care, and cost-effectiveness for each patient in their panel of up to 450 patients. They understand that they can strongly influence the patient’s outcomes by building a trusting relationship and helping them change behaviors.
• Coaching for health: The PCP acts as a health coach, rather than just a consultant for sickness, by helping patients set short and long-term health goals, partners with the patient to work toward the goals, and frequently follows up on those goals on the path to improved health for their patients.
• Simplifying for action: The PCP simplifies and prioritizes appropriately so that behavior change is more actionable, both for the patient in helping them achieve their goals, and when leading their care teams towards their performance goals.

We are an outcomes-focused, value-based organization and for their panel of patients, the following metrics are regularly measured to help PCP’s become successful and reach partnership status: patient admissions/thousand, using between 18-21 appointment slots per day (each new patient count for 2 slots, follow-up patients 1 slot), CGCAHPS (patient experience), clinical gaps closures, and medical cost measures. Each PCP will have goals for these metrics and will be expected to work towards those targets with their center and market leadership as well as their care teams. Culture is very important in the medical centers and because PCP’s are leaders in our organization and centers, they are expected to help champion a positive culture of love, accountability, and passion along with center leadership.

The PCP will be required to demonstrate the ability to function both independently and in collaboration with other health care professionals. The PCP will work closely with the applicable managers and medical directors to ensure compliance with guidelines along with participating in risk and quality management programs, clinical meetings and other meetings as required that promote patient health and company goals.
The PCP will adhere to strict departmental goals/objectives, standards of performance, regulatory compliance, quality patient care compliance, and policies and procedures.

ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • The PCP independently provides care for patients with acute and chronic illnesses encountered in the older adult patient.
  • The PCP will take full accountability for patient care and outcomes and will appropriately seek consultation from specialists when needed, though will still stay involved in, and be responsible for, the detailed care of the patient.
  • It is expected that the PCP will engage with the hospitalist whenever one of their patients is in the hospital (regardless of whether the hospitalist works for ChenMed or not).
  • The PCP is responsible for assessment, diagnosis, treatment, management, education, health promotion and care coordination and documentation for patients with acute and complex chronic health needs.
  • The PCP leads their care team consisting of care promoter (medical assistant), care facilitator, and care coordinator for patients able to come to the office.
  • For patients that are unable to come to the office—in hospital, SNF, LTC or homebound, PCP will engage with the transitional care team and others including case managers, acute and transitional-care physicians, and other resources that may be available depending on the market.
  • PCP will have an active role in the management of their center and will help cover for other providers who may be out for various reasons. It is also expected that each PCP will take an active role as needed in recruiting patients for the center and additional providers for the company.
  • Supervises, collaborates with, participates with, or functions within a practice or collaborative agreement with an Advanced Practice Practitioner (APP) and remains accountable for the actions of the APP while employed with the company.
  • Performs other duties as assigned and modified at manager’s discretion.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES:

Competencies for Success

  • Availability and Accessibility for patients to build trust from their patients. It is expected that PCP’s will make themselves as available to their patients as possible by being open and available for walk-in visits and answering phone calls and messages in a timely manner.
  • Service Orientation — PCP’s provide care that they would want for a family member or for themselves to each patient at every interaction.
  • Evidence Based Medicine — The PCP remains updated on evidence-based medicine, but also recognizes that factors outside of traditional medicine, like lifestyle and nutrition, have a large impact on patient health outcomes. The PCP stays up to date on clinical, nutritional, and lifestyle-based interventions to improve outcomes.
  • Physician Leadership is integral to good healthcare, so the PCP must be willing to continuously work to develop and improve leadership skills for the benefit of one’s patients, their team, their center and the company.
  • Quality — Our patients deserve the highest quality of care. This requires a willingness to work with the care teams towards achieving high quality outcomes and quality measures. At the same time, PCPs will always be looking for ways to continuously and systematically improve their practice of medicine and the operations of their center.
  • Influence — PCP’s must competently and compassionately influence their patients, their teams, and themselves to achieve the best outcomes.
  • Self-Care — A PCP can take the best care for their patients when they are adequately caring for themselves. That means physically, mentally, socially and spiritually. Physician wellness is important for sustainability and promoting the health of physicians, staff, and patients.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite products including Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook, plus a variety of other word-processing, spreadsheet, database, e-mail and presentation software as used in the company
  • Ability and willingness to travel locally as needed in their market, if applicable, nationally for initial training (2 weeks) and then occasionally regionally and nationally for recruiting or training purposes.
  • Fluency in English, verbal and written. There may be jobs in some centers that require fluency in other languages, and this will be made known at the time of application.
  • This job requires use and exercise of independent judgment
  • Flexible to work evening, weekends and/or holidays as needed

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE CRITERIA:

  • MD or DO in Internal Medicine, Family Medicine, Geriatrics or similar specialty required

  • Must be able to obtain a State Medical License or already have a current, active State Medical License for the state(s) in which he/she will be working

  • Board certification in Internal Medicine, Family Medicine, Geriatrics or similar specialty is preferred. Board Eligibility is required

  • Once Board certified, PCP will maintain board certification in their specialty by doing necessary MOC, CME and/or retaking board exams as required

  • Must have a current DEA number for schedule II-V controlled substances

  • Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from the American Heart Association (AMA) or American Red Cross required w/in first 90 days of employment.





PAY RANGE:

$221,141 - $315,915 Salary

The posted pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for this position. Final compensation will depend on a variety of factors including but not limited to experience, education, geographic location, and other relevant factors. This position may also be eligible for a bonuses or commissions.

EMPLOYEE BENEFITS

We’re ChenMed and we’re transforming healthcare for seniors and changing America’s healthcare for the better. Family-owned and physician-led, our unique approach allows us to improve the health and well-being of the populations we serve. We’re growing rapidly as we seek to rescue more and more seniors from inadequate health care.

ChenMed is changing lives for the people we serve and the people we hire. With great compensation, comprehensive benefits, career development and advancement opportunities and so much more, our employees enjoy great work-life balance and opportunities to grow. Join our team who make a difference in people’s lives every single day.

Designs, implements, oversees and manages a comprehensive Parks and Recreation system including operations, programs, and facilities. Supervises assigned staff in the operation of the department.

Applicants are required to attach a resume and cover letter.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Essential functions, as defined under the Americans with Disabilities Act, may include any of the following representative duties, knowledge, and skills. This is not a comprehensive listing of all functions and duties performed by the incumbents of this class; employees may be assigned duties which are not listed below; reasonable accommodation will be made as required. The job description does not constitute an employment agreement and is subject to change at any time by the employer. Essential duties and responsibilities may include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Provides direction and vision to assigned staff in the operation of the department.

  • Provides direct and indirect supervision to department staff; performs supervisory functions including recommending for hire, training, evaluating, counseling, developing and disciplining of assigned staff.

  • Develops, implements and maintains policies, procedures and regulations pertaining to parks and recreation; ensures compliance with all local, state and federal regulations and laws governing department activities.

  • Oversee operation and programming of all recreation facilities including the recreation center, tennis center, swimming pools, athletic complex, challenge course and departmental special events.

  • Monitors and oversee Parks and Recreation major capital projects.

  • Prepares operational budgets; predicts income and outlays; reviews fees for services to meet cost recovery goals; monitors revenues and expenditures.

  • Oversees all aspects of department grants including application, distribution and reporting.

  • Develops and implements long-range departmental plans goals, strategies and objectives; ensures that performance measures are met.

  • Attends City Council meetings and Parks and Recreation Board meetings; makes presentations to represent the department’s services, programs, activities and expansion.

  • Provides oversight to the Youth Advisory Board.

  • Promotes good public relations with the community and with special interest groups; participates in partnerships and coalitions that align with the City’s mission.

  • Responds to and resolves customer complaints, concerns and questions regarding the department programs, facilities, vision, policies and procedures.

  • Provides quality customer service to city staff, the general public, and all other work contacts.

  • Serves in extension of current duties as required for emergency management, particularly in the area of sheltering.

  • Performs other duties as assigned or required.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

Education, training and Experience Guidelines

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with major coursework in Parks and Recreation Administration, Public Administration, Business Administration, or related field. Seven (7) years of full-time progressively responsible experience in parks and recreation administration. Five (5) years of the required experience must have been in a supervisory capacity. OR Any equivalent combination of experience, education and/or training that provides the required knowledge, skills, and abilities.

Knowledge of:

  • Parks and recreation development, implementation and management practices and techniques.

  • Long- and short-range facility and open space development, maintenance and repair.

location: New York, New York, United States
description:
In compliance with applicable laws, HSBC is committed to employing only those who are authorized to work in the US. HSBC may engage in immigration sponsorship for this position if needed.

Our purpose – Opening up a world of opportunity – explains why we exist. Here at HSBC, we use our unique expertise, capabilities, breadth, and perspectives to open up new kinds of opportunity for our more than 40 million customers. We’re bringing together the people, ideas and capital that nurture progress and growth, helping to create a better world – for our customers, our people, our investors, our communities, and the planet we all share.

The role of the Communications function is to protect and enhance the reputation of HSBC, and to engage our colleagues, build pride and confidence in, and commitment to, HSBC.

The role holder is responsible for all communications for HSBC Bank USA. This includes leadership, employee communications and culture change communications, as well as oversight of integrated communications and media relations.

The role holder supports the CEO of the US Bank, as well as the wider Executive Committee, in delivering the communications plan. The role functionally reports to the Global Head of Communications for Corporate and Institutional Banking whilst entity management reporting is to the CEO of the US Bank.

The focus of the role is to drive a strategic communications strategy that mobilises and engages the entire employee population of the HSBC Bank USA, overseeing leadership communications, implementing effective integrated internal communications strategies, supporting transformation communications and mobilising culture change. It also has responsibility for positioning the US business within the wider global network through effective integrated communications strategies. It also has responsibility for managing the reputation of the business, supporting effective communications with key stakeholder groups in the market and across the HSBC Group. This includes overseeing business-aligned integrated communications strategies, issues management and reputational risk, and the ability to navigate geopolitical sensitivites for an industry leader defined by its unique footprint spanning Asia, Middle East, Europe and the Americas.

The role holder will work seamlessly with the regional and global Communications teams, as well as with colleagues from Brand, Marketing, Public Affairs and Corporate Sustainability to execute the firm’s strategy in the USA.

Principal Accountabilities:

  • Execute a cohesive employee communications and insight strategy for the US business, in support of country business objectives with a priority of growth
  • Support integrated leadership communications and drive insight-based strategy and culture change communications programmes with a strong focus on the HSBC Bank USA employee population
  • Develop narratives and and position HSBC Bank USA as a crucial connector within HSBC’s global network including raising its profile in other regions, supporting inbound and outbound commercial flows
  • Actively engage with functional and business peers to safeguard the reputation of HSBC in the US, including in-depth understanding and risk escalation of business and customer trends that could impact the businesses’ reputation and performance
  • Oversee a focused integrated communications strategy for HSBC in the US supporting commercial outcomes across both businesses
  • Guide and steer Communications activity in the US
  • Maintain knowledge of stakeholder requirements, competitor activities and market trends to influence the future communications direction of the US team
  • Lead an integrated communications strategy for US leadership engagement including development of messaging, briefing documents, and positioning pieces as relevant
  • Provide key internal stakeholders, including HSBC US’s CEO and Management Team, with informed counsel on all communications matters
  • Oversee a team that maintains relationships with core media and key external stakeholders in the US in partnership with global CIB media relations and corporate media relations teams
  • Deliver fair outcomes for our customers and ensure own conduct maintains the orderly and transparent operation of financial markets
  • Maintain connectivity and dialogue with other regional communications teams, including Latin America
  • Ensure colleagues in the direct team, create a sense of followership across the broader function
  • Develop and communicate a powerful and compelling purpose of the US business and the role of communications in influencing our key audiences
  • Close collaboration with Head of Media Relations, CIB and IWPB, for oversight of proactive and reactive media relations in the US
  • Lead, develop and motivate the team to attract and retain talent to provide for succession and ensure delivery of objectives

Key attributes:

  • An innovator – a strong desire to drive change, introduce new ideas and to take thoughtful risks
  • Strategic mindset and an inspirational people leader
  • Executive presence with C-suite executives – confident and effective interaction with senior business leaders
  • Strong strategic abilities – use a diverse set of insights to develop a broad perspective and lay out a vision of what the bank/team can achieve
  • An internationalist. Understand the East/West and North/South role played by the US business. Ability to take a ‘beyond-just-our-market’, international perspective on issues, opportunities and solutions
  • A ‘can do’ mindset – a sleeves-rolled-up approach to getting things moving and making progress
  • The ability to deliver high-quality products and exceptional services that provide value and exceed client expectations
  • Strong integrity, and a demonstrable commitment to ethics
  • A champion for inclusion – creates an environment in which all people feel like they belong
  • A focused approach to maintaining HSBC’s brand and reputation
  • Comfortable dealing with ambiguity
  • A strong client-service orientation
  • An inspirational team leader with high EQ and excellent interpersonal skills. A strong ability to motivate others – instill confidence and coach people to find meaning in their work to help achieve exceptional results
  • Superb influencing skills and ability to manage multiple senior stakeholders – including the ability to persuade others to act

As an HSBC employee, you will have access to tailored professional development opportunities to ensure you have the right skills for today and tomorrow. We offer a competitive pay and benefits package including a robust Wellness Hub, all in a welcoming and inclusive work environment. You will be empowered to drive HSBC’s engagement with the communities we serve through an industry-leading volunteerism policy, and generous matching gift program. You’ll want to join our Employee Resource Groups as they play a central part in life at HSBC, including the development of our employees and networking inside and outside of HSBC. We value difference. We succeed together. We take responsibility. We get it done. And we want you to help us build the bank of the future!

title: Maintenance Parts Coordinator
description:
Position Summary: The Maintenance Parts Coordinator is responsible for maintaining an organized, accurate, and efficient maintenance parts inventory to support production and facility equipment within a food-manufacturing environment.

This position will manage the day-to-day operation of the maintenance parts room, including receiving, stocking, issuing, tracking, and ordering maintenance parts and supplies. The Parts Coordinator will work closely with Maintenance Technicians and Maintenance leadership to ensure critical spare parts are available when needed and to reduce equipment downtime caused by unavailable parts.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, dependable, comfortable working with computerized inventory systems, and able to communicate effectively with Maintenance, Purchasing, Receiving, and outside vendors.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Maintain an organized and clean maintenance parts room.
  • Receive, inspect, label, and properly store incoming maintenance parts.
  • Issue parts and supplies to Maintenance Technicians and accurately document usage.
  • Maintain accurate inventory quantities and locations.
  • Perform routine cycle counts and correct inventory discrepancies.
  • Maintain appropriate minimum and maximum inventory levels.
  • Monitor inventory and identify parts that need to be reordered.
  • Assist with creating purchase requests and tracking open parts orders.
  • Follow up with vendors on pricing, availability, lead times, and outstanding orders.
  • Verify received parts against purchase orders and packing slips.
  • Ensure parts are properly labeled with part numbers, equipment information, and storage locations.
  • Maintain organized storage locations for electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, and facility parts.
  • Track repairable components that are sent to outside vendors for repair.
  • Maintain records for warranty parts and returned components.
  • Assist Maintenance leadership with controlling parts inventory costs.
  • Identify obsolete, duplicate, or excess inventory.
  • Maintain appropriate inventory records in Plex, Redzone, or other company systems as required.
  • Maintain maintenance consumables and commonly used shop supplies.
  • Keep the parts room secure and ensure parts are properly issued and accounted for.

Critical Spare Parts Management

The Parts Coordinator will work with Maintenance leadership to identify and maintain critical spare parts for production equipment.

This may include:

  • Motors
  • Gearboxes
  • Bearings
  • Chains and sprockets
  • Belts
  • Pumps
  • Sensors and photo eyes
  • VFDs
  • HMIs
  • PLC components
  • Electrical components
  • Pneumatic cylinders and valves
  • Solenoids
  • Conveyor components
  • Packaging-machine components
  • Fuses, relays, contactors, and overloads
  • Equipment-specific replacement parts

Critical spare inventory should be reviewed based on equipment importance, failure history, replacement cost, vendor lead time, and potential production downtime.

Inventory & Parts Room Organization

The Parts Coordinator is expected to maintain a parts room where Maintenance Technicians can quickly identify and locate required components.

Responsibilities include:

  • Establishing clearly identified storage locations.
  • Labeling shelves, bins, cabinets, and parts.
  • Maintaining accurate part numbers and descriptions.
  • Linking parts to the appropriate equipment when possible.
  • Maintaining quantities on hand.
  • Establishing minimum and maximum stock levels.
  • Identifying low-stock and out-of-stock items.
  • Performing scheduled cycle counts.
  • Investigating inventory discrepancies.
  • Maintaining designated areas for new, used, repairable, warranty, and obsolete parts.
  • Preventing uncontrolled removal of parts from inventory.

The goal is for a mechanic to be able to quickly locate the correct part during a production breakdown without searching through unorganized inventory.

Purchasing & Vendor Coordination

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Strong attendance and punctuality.
  • Ability to work independently with limited supervision.

Physical & Work Environment Requirements

  • Stand and walk for extended periods.
  • Bend, reach, kneel, push, and pull as necessary.
  • Move and organize maintenance parts and supplies.
  • Use ladders or approved equipment to access storage locations when trained and authorized.

title: Quality Inspector - Electromechanical - Level 2
description:
For almost 30 years, SQA Services has been a premier leader in the provision of managed supplier quality services for audits, assessments, remote surveillance assessments, corrective actions, remediation, inspections, and engineering to manufacturers within the aerospace, electronics, and life sciences industries. We deliver services by deploying associates who are located in 90+ countries around the world to various supplier sites.
We are seeking a dedicated and highly skilled Electro-Mechanical Inspector to join our team to support source inspections at Opole, Poland. This critical role requires an experienced professional with a keen eye for detail and a deep understanding of quality assurance practices. If you have a background in the inspection of electro-mechanical parts, are proficient with all precision hand tools, and can interpret complex GD&T requirements. This position will be on site 5 days a week, for 4-8 hours a day on 2nd shift hours (2pm-10pm) This is a 1+ year contract.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Conduct visual, physical, and dimensional inspections (both in-process and final) of parts, per project specifications and requirements.
  • Perform incoming inspections from external providers of products and services (e.g., nickel plating).
  • Conduct in-process and final inspections of critical features, including witness inspections (e.g., CMM program run).
  • Compile final inspection sign-off sheets and inspection packages.
  • Verify that inspection equipment is capable of detecting defects and ensure inspection methodology aligns with drawing intent.
  • Review and validate the justification for parts not inspected at final inspection.
  • Audit and validate the execution of inspection plans as applicable.
  • Document non-conformances using approved methods and submit non-conformance reports for customer disposition.
  • Verify hardware cleanliness and absence of internal or external foreign object debris.
  • Verify fasteners are properly installed; assure torque stripe is continuous and of correct color.
  • Assure products are free of gaps, mismatches, fairing, and of acceptable contour and waviness.
  • Ensure products are of good workmanship and meet specified standards (e.g., oil canning, riding conditions, loose fasteners, drill starts, scratches, dings, burrs, fastener edge distance).
  • Review and validate First Article Inspection (FAI) documentation, including completeness, traceability, and compliance.
  • Ensure the protection and preservation of inspected products for subsequent processing and shipment.
  • Verify applicable shipping documentation for legibility and completeness, including part number, serial number, configuration change letter, and shipping destination.

Required Qualifications:

  • Extensive experience as a Quality Inspector or CMM Operator, with industry and commodity-specific expertise.
  • Proficiency in dimensional inspection of precision tolerance parts.
  • Strong knowledge and hands-on experience with all inspection tools.
  • Ability to understand and interpret complex GD&T requirements and validate complex assemblies.
  • Experience with multiple primary and secondary part numbers (e.g., brackets, clips, doublers, splices, brackets, drip shields, etc.).
  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. What you'll bring

  • Strong experience in electrical network design and development, ideally up to 33kV.

  • Knowledge of electricity distribution networks and associated engineering standards.

  • Ability to balance technical, commercial and customer considerations when developing solutions.

What you'll need

  • Relevant engineering qualification or equivalent industry experience.

  • Network construction and/or operational experience.

  • Strong IT and system skills.

  • Due to the nature of the role, you'll be required to travel to sites across Central and Southern Scotland, so a full UK driving licence is essential.

What's in it for you

As well as a competitive salary reviewed annually, you'll benefit from a generous rewards package designed to support your wellbeing, lifestyle and future career.

SP Energy Networks is playing a leading role in the transition to a cleaner, greener energy system. Our Distribution network serves millions of customers across Central and Southern Scotland, delivering the essential infrastructure that connects homes, businesses and low-carbon technologies to the electricity network.

As we prepare for a significant period of growth through ED3 and beyond, we're investing in the engineers who will help shape the future of our network. Whether that's supporting decarbonisation, enabling new connections, or delivering innovative engineering solutions, you'll have the opportunity to work on projects that make a real difference.

With the backing of the Iberdrola Group, one of the world's leading energy companies, you'll enjoy genuine career development opportunities, access to industry-leading expertise and the chance to help build the network of the future.

description:
Job Description

Meet the Team


Cisco's Webex Engineering Group is redefining the future of collaboration. We’re building a world where people connect effortlessly to enjoy modern, uncompromised collaboration across every room, desk, pocket, and application.


Our technology powers industry-leading products like Webex Meetings, Webex Calling, and Webex Contact Center. As a member of our team, your work will shape experiences used by millions of people globally, enabling seamless collaboration regardless of device or location and empowering the hybrid working patterns of the future.


Our engineering teams are trusted to make the right decisions and are empowered to act on them. This is a friendly, energetic environment with a fast pace of delivery, working closely with co-located UX design and product management teams.


Your Impact



  • Design, build, and lead the technical direction of end-user features used by millions of people worldwide.

  • Own architectural decisions within your domain — defining, evolving, and clearly communicating scalable, maintainable designs aligned with broader platform strategy.

  • Break down complex product requirements into clear technical designs and executable work, guiding teams from concept through delivery.

  • Act as a technical leader and role model within the team, setting high standards for code quality, testing, reliability, and operational excellence.

  • Mentor and coach junior and mid-level engineers, supporting their technical growth through pairing, reviews, feedback, and knowledge sharing.

  • Partner closely with product managers and designers to influence roadmap decisions, balancing customer value, technical health, and long-term sustainability.

  • Listen to the customer and elevate their experience. CSAT, NPS, feedback, and metrics are their voice — drive investigations, identify root causes, and lead impactful improvements.

  • Optimise — champion effective use of AI tools across the team to improve productivity, accelerate delivery, and focus effort on the most complex engineering challenges.

  • Lead by example — bring curiosity, accountability, and positivity, helping foster a culture of ownership, learning, and collaboration.


Minimum Qualifications



  • Education: Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in an analytical subject such as Computer Science, Electronic Engineering, or Software Engineering.

  • Experience: 5+ years of professional software development experience or equivalent, delivering high-quality, production-grade software in complex environments.

  • Technical Leadership: Demonstrated experience leading architecture and design discussions, influencing technical direction, and driving alignment across teams.

  • Engineering Excellence: Deep programming and system design expertise, with the ability to evaluate trade-offs and make sound technical decisions.

  • Problem Solving: Proven ability to lead a structured, scientific, and creative approach to solving complex technical and product challenges.

  • Collaboration & Communication: Strong ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to engineers, product partners, and stakeholders at varying levels.

  • Quality Focus: A strong commitment to quality, including test strategy definition, code reviews, operational readiness, and continuous improvement.


Preferred Qualifications



  • Full stack development, in some or all of the following areas:

    • Languages: TypeScript/JavaScript, Java

    • UI Frameworks: React or Angular

    • Back-end: Java (Spring), RESTful APIs, WebSockets, distributed systems, and API design

    • Database: Postgres/AWS Aurora



  • Proven experience scaling systems to handle growing traffic, data volume, and user load, including horizontal scaling, caching, and load balancing.

  • Significant experience contributing to or owning system architecture for large-scale, customer-facing applications.

  • Strong experience with unit, integration, and end-to-end testing, including contract testing and test automation in CI/CD pipelines.

  • Practical experience or strong interest in AI-assisted development, including hands-on use of LLM-based tools for design exploration, scaffolding, refactoring, test generation, debugging, and improving developer productivity — with strong ownership of validated, production-ready solutions.

  • Deep familiarity with Git, DevOps practices, continuous integration, and continuous delivery.

  • Experience optimising applications across Windows, macOS, Linux, and Web platforms and ecosystems.


Why Cisco?

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.


Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.


We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

  • 2+ years of experience in an IT support or application support role.

title: Cloud & Mobile TPM

title: CT Technologist, Float
description:
We are so glad you are interested in joining Sutter Health!

Organization:

SMF-Sutter Med Foundation- Central

Position Overview:

Competently performs routine and specialized computerized tomography procedures to produce quality images to physicians and other health care providers for the diagnosis, treatment, monitoring and prevention of injury or disease. Works independently, exercising sound judgment, and developed clinical skills to execute safe and precise procedures to deliver accurate results in a timely manner. Gains confidence and cooperation from the patient, their family/support group, and other healthcare providers through competent patient assessment, attentive monitoring, and effective communication. Adheres to all local/state/federal regulations, codes, policies and procedures to ensure privacy and safety while delivering optimal patient care. May also be responsible for performing specific procedures and/or may help orient other staff to the department.

NOTE: This position is a float pool position supporting multiple sites. Travel is required within and around Greater Sacramento Area to include Auburn, Elk Grove, Roseville, Folsom, Carmichael and Yuba City.

  • RHF-Radiology Fluoroscopy within 180 Days of hire if required at the affiliate.


SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE:

  • General knowledge of diagnostic computerized tomography principles, procedures, views, and equipment, including some experience responding to traumas and various hospital emergencies.

  • Capable of performing routine CT examinations as well as a basic understanding of human anatomy, physiology, pathology, and medical terminology.

  • Possess written and verbal communications skills to explain sensitive information clearly and professionally to diverse audiences, including non-medical people.

  • Well-developed time management and organizational skills, including the ability to prioritize assignments and work within standardized operating procedures and scientific methods to achieve objectives and meet deadline.

  • General knowledge of computer applications, such as Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel and Outlook) and related information systems (Radiology (RIS), laboratory (LIS), electronic health records (EHR), EPIC, and picture archive and communication system (PACS).

  • Prioritize assignments and work within standardized policies, procedures, and scientific methods to achieve objectives and meet deadlines.

  • Work independently, as well as be part of the team, including accomplishing multiple tasks in an environment with interruptions.

  • Identify, evaluate and resolve standard problems by selecting appropriate solutions from established options.

  • Ensure the privacy of each patient’s protected health information (PHI).

  • Build collaborates relationships with peers and other healthcare providers to achieve departmental and corporate objectives.

title: Undergrad Intern – Data Engineer – Amgen’s Technology & Medical Organizations (Summer 2027)
description:
Career Category

College Job

Job Description

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Undergrad Intern – Data Engineer – Amgen’s Technology & Medical Organizations (Summer 2027)

What You Will Do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. During this internship, you will acquire the valuable hands-on skills and foundational experience needed to become a professional in your chosen field.

This role requires working closely with product owner/Product Architect and various functional teams to understand the data requirements and implementing data engineering solutions. This position is responsible for design and development of data pipelines to extract, transform, and load data from various data sources in various data formats to Enterprise Data Lake. Responsibilities may include:

  • Collaborating with lead Architects, Business SMEs and Data Scientists to design and develop end-to-end data pipelines and support infrastructure
  • Building new infrastructure and analytics tools using Python, SQL and AWS
  • Proactively identifying & implementing opportunities to automate tasks and develop reusable frameworks; participating in efforts to design, build, and develop rapid Proof-of-Concept (POC) solutions and services

  • Expected continued enrollment in an accredited college or university following the internship program

  • Must be available to work a full-time schedule.
  • Must be available to accept and commit to future full-time employment by July 2028, if offered

What We Expect of You

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The passionate and driven individual we seek exemplifies the following qualifications:

Basic Qualifications:

Amgen requires that all individuals applying for an undergrad internship or a co-op assignment at Amgen must meet the following criteria:

  • 18 years or older
  • Currently enrolled in a full-time Bachelor’s Degree program from an accredited college or university with a 3.0 minimum GPA or equivalent

Preferred Qualifications

  • Degree concentration(s) in Information Technology, Computer Science (e.g., CS, CPE, SE), Engineering, Business, or related field
  • Biotechnology, pharmaceutical or health care industry experience
  • Intermediate knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel and Power Point
  • Strong interpersonal, project management, analytical and quantitative skills
  • Proficient in one of the coding languages (Python, Java, Scala, SQL)
  • Detail oriented
  • Demonstrated personal initiative, self-motivation, flexibility, adaptability and resourcefulness
  • Ability to operate independently, across functional lines, and with both internal and external customers
  • Coursework in one or more of the following areas:
  • Business Systems analysis, Lean, Agile (SCRUM) and other SDLC processes, Software Development, Database Modeling, Web Design and Development, IT Management, Management of Cloud based application, B2B Collaboration, Enterprise systems such as configuration and management of ERP, CRM systems

What You Can Expect of Us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

The base pay range for this opportunity in the U.S. is $28.87 per hour.

title: Patient Continuity and Needs Advocate (PCNA)
description:
We’re unique. You should be, too.

We’re changing lives every day. For both our patients and our team members. Are you innovative and entrepreneurial minded? Is your work ethic and ambition off the charts? Do you inspire others with your kindness and joy?

We’re different than most primary care providers. We’re rapidly expanding and we need great people to join our team.

The Patient Continuity and Needs Advocate (PCNA) serves as a vital bridge between patients and comprehensive care, ensuring every eligible patient receives the right healthcare plan and support services tailored to their unique needs. Directly supports ChenMed’s core goal of transforming senior care by maintaining strong patient relationships, reducing healthcare disruptions, and ensuring our most vulnerable patients receive consistent, comprehensive primary care and other services they may be entitled to. The PCNA role is critical to building trust within our communities and maximizing the impact of our patient-centered care model.

ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Patient Advocacy & Connection: Evaluates patient needs and connects eligible individuals with health plans and community resources that suit their unique healthcare needs and enhances their care experience and outcomes.
  • Retention & Re-engagement: Proactively reaches out to disenrolled members to understand barriers to care and facilitates their return to our medical centers through personalized outreach and support.
  • Collaborative Partnership: Works closely with center leadership, sales teams, brokers and clinical staff to develop and execute targeted patient retention strategies that strengthen our patient-provider relationships.
  • Care Continuity: Ensures seamless transitions and sustained engagement to prevent gaps in care that could lead to hospital visits or adverse health outcomes.
  • Documentation: utilizes an Electronic Medical Records (EMR) system, Medals and Salesforce to gather and store patient information, respond to questions on behalf of the patient and appropriately and timely document patient issues and resolutions. Maintains assigned work queue of patient accounts.
  • Completes relevant patient documentation in compliance with all regulatory agencies, including HIPAA.
  • Performs other duties as assigned and modified at manager’s discretion.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

  • Competent level business acuity
  • In-depth knowledge and understanding of general/core job-related functions, practices, processes, procedures, techniques and methods
  • Fundamental knowledge and understanding of local, state and federal healthcare benefit services and plans
  • Ability to build and maintain exceptional customer service relationships with healthcare services agencies, patients, providers and peers
  • Dependable and time conscious
  • Flexibility, agility, self-starter, comfortable with frequent changes and innovations
  • Understanding of member attribution, eligibility and the disenrollment process
  • Demonstrated skill in customer service and service recovery
  • Knowledge of and experience in working with insurance brokers or agents preferred
  • Detail-oriented with proficiency in Salesforce
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Positive attitude and the ability to build trust with internal and external partners
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite products including Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook, plus a variety of other word-processing, spreadsheet, database, e-mail and presentation software
  • Spoken and written fluency in English

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE CRITERIA:

  • High School diploma or GED equivalent required
  • BA/BS degree preferred OR additional experience above the minimum may be considered in lieu of the required education on a year-for-year basis
  • A minimum of three (3) years’ work experience required; working with seniors a plus as is a general understanding of Medicare Advantage
    



    PAY RANGE:

    $17.0 - $24.26 Hourly

    The posted pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for this position. Final compensation will depend on a variety of factors including but not limited to experience, education, geographic location, and other relevant factors. This position may also be eligible for a bonuses or commissions.

    EMPLOYEE BENEFITS

    We’re ChenMed and we’re transforming healthcare for seniors and changing America’s healthcare for the better. Family-owned and physician-led, our unique approach allows us to improve the health and well-being of the populations we serve. We’re growing rapidly as we seek to rescue more and more seniors from inadequate health care.

Seize your opportunity to make a personal impact as a SIGINT Network Development (NetDev) Analyst (TS/SCI) supporting the U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) is the law enforcement arm of the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) and conducts criminal investigations concerning theft of mail, mail fraud, violent crimes, and the mailing of prohibited items.

The Analytics Group (AG) Communications Support Unit (CSU) of the USPIS provides technical solutions and communications analysis in support of field investigations. A key CSU capability is live collection of communications and detailed analysis of data and records to advance criminal investigations.

USPIS requires specialized personnel who can leverage modern communications environments to support criminal investigations against suspects who aim to do harm to the Postal Service, Postal employees, and Postal customers. The CSU specifically needs advanced analytical support to identify, track, and dismantle criminal networks utilizing the U.S. Mail to facilitate illicit activities, relying on Signals Intelligence (SIGINT), Network Development (NetDev), and geospatial analysis in support of field operations and investigations.

MEANINGFUL WORK AND PERSONAL IMPACT

  • Conduct advanced SIGINT/COMINT and Network Development (NetDev) analysis in support of USPIS criminal investigations and operations.
  • Perform Social Network Analysis (SNA) and target development to identify key actors, relationships, and vulnerabilities in criminal networks.
  • Support tactical SIGINT operations and geo-location techniques in coordination with investigative personnel.
  • Analyze multi-source communications data (telephony, mobile networks, IP-based communications, social media, and other digital platforms) to build network, pattern-of-life, and suspect profiles.
  • Develop and maintain network diagrams, association charts, timelines, dashboards, and geospatial visualizations to support investigative strategy and case presentations.
  • Design and execute complex analytic workflows using large, heterogeneous datasets; generate investigative leads and actionable intelligence for law enforcement personnel.
  • Support lawful intercept and live-collection activities in accordance with applicable legal, policy, and privacy requirements.
  • Collaborate with investigators, analysts, and technical staff to refine workflows, tools, and methodologies aligned with evolving communications technologies.
  • Ensure strict adherence to legal, privacy, classification, and ethical standards in all aspects of data handling, storage, querying, and analysis.
  • Produce clear, concise written reports and deliver oral briefings to Postal Inspectors, investigative leadership, and other law enforcement partners.
  • Strong understanding of lawful intercept concepts, constraints, and relevant legal/policy frameworks.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, mission-focused, multidisciplinary environment.

  • 12+ years’ experience in the Intelligence Community (IC) performing Signals and Communications Intelligence (SIGINT/COMINT) analysis and Network Development (NetDev)

  • Proficiency with government-approved geospatial desktop, enterprise, and online capabilities used for analysis and dashboard creation;
  • Proficiency in Python and notebook-based analysis for automation and data processing;
  • Expertise with Penlink PLX, Gladiator (or IC equivalent) and i2 Analyst Notebook (or IC equivalent);
  • Experience with query syntax (Boolean, REGEX) and massive dataset querying.
  • Experience with tactical SIGINT operations and geo-location techniques.

title: Lead Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) Engineer
description:
At Jabil (NYSE: JBL), we are proud to be a trusted partner for the world's top brands, offering comprehensive engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions. With 60 years of experience across industries and a vast network of over 100 sites worldwide, Jabil combines global reach with local expertise to deliver both scalable and customized solutions. Our commitment extends beyond business success as we strive to build sustainable processes that minimize environmental impact and foster vibrant and diverse communities around the globe.

Located in Byhalia, MS Sterilization Facility (X-ray Medical Devices)
Jabil’s new state-of-the-art facility in Byhalia, Mississippi is a cutting-edge sterilization site dedicated to supporting the medical device industry through advanced X-ray sterilization technology. This site plays a critical role in ensuring the safety, quality, and regulatory compliance of life-saving medical products. Equipped with innovative processing capabilities and a focus on operational excellence, the Byhalia facility strengthens Jabil’s global healthcare network by delivering fast, reliable, and scalable sterilization solutions. Team members at this site contribute directly to improving patient outcomes while working in a highly technical, quality-driven environment that emphasizes safety, precision, and continuous improvement.

How will you make an impact?

The Lead EHS Engineer manages the establishment, implementation, and maintenance of a safe, accident-free, healthy work environment, compliant with all applicable H.S.E. regulations, company policies and procedures, and the safety statement ensuring safety objectives are implemented site-wide.


What will you do?
· Develop and update the site safety statement and policy in partnership with plant management ensuring all employees are communicated periodically on the safety statement and policy.
· Provide direction and advice to site management in the area of Health & Safety legislation and Codes of Practice and how best to implement at site level including but not limited to, the company meetings its objectives under the Safety, Health and Welfare at Work Act 2005 and the Safety, Health and Welfare at Work (General Application) Regulations 2007.
· Responsible for regulatory internal reporting, internal auditing and validation of compliance activities and reporting all relevant accidents and dangerous occurrences to the HSA through the EHS Manager.
· Implementation of corporate Health & Safety systems with specific emphasis on process safety management, process hazards analysis, industrial hygiene, risk assessment, accident and injury reporting and change control.
· Develop a proactive approach to accident/incident prevention through the visual management system leading indicator (near miss / good catch reporting).
· Support the review and assessment of plant modifications. Provide technical safety input to the design and construction of new facilities including impact on automation lines and process equipment.
· Participate in pre-start up safety reviews and equipment walk-downs to identify relevant safety items and complete Health & Safety audits.
· Conduct process HAZOPs and risk assessments. Review and update existing risk assessments.
· Establish properties for development of hazard control programs and participate in the implementation.
· Devise/update key safety programs in line with legislation/best practice and coordinate Jabil’s health & safety management system as outlined in the safety statement & corporate AIMS process.
· Assess training needs in conjunction with the Training Coordinator, source and select suitable training providers and deliver appropriate H&S training to personnel on site incl. contractors as needed. Ensure the timely delivery of mandatory regulatory health & safety training within legal timeframes.
· Ensure sufficient numbers of staff are trained and hold the positions of first aider and fire warden and monitor the systems for ensuring that fire precautions are adequate.
· Familiarity with emergency response planning, in addition to fire protection systems and ensure that a minimum of two emergency evacuations are carried out on an annual basis.
· Lead continuous improvement efforts to reduce occurrences of recordable injuries. Monitor the performance of safe systems of work and current safe operating procedures. Implement improvements as required.
· other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

How will you get here?

  • Excellent communication, presentation, organizational and training skills.
  • Ability to interpret relevant legislation, and regulatory compliance procedures.
  • Lead the company safety team where appropriate to continuously improve the company safety systems.
  • Self-starter with demonstrated efficient work methods, analytical and problem solving skills and ability to handle multiple tasks in a fast paced environment.
  • Knowledge with any of the following skills is a plus: Manual Handling Instructor, Trained VDU Assessor, Current Safe Pass card.
  • Actively promote and increase awareness and behaviors with regards to safe H&S practices including but not limited to staff communication sessions and other employee engagement forums.
  • Strong interpersonal skills with an ability to work with all levels within the organization and third parties.
  • Competent in MS Office.
  • Experience with industrial radiation / Radiation Safety Officer (RSO) training.
  • Develops and implements general EHS policies and procedures to be followed by company personnel in compliance with local, state, regional, and nation regulations.
  • Requires working knowledge of US-OSHA and EPA compliance requirements associated with manufacturing operations.
  • Strong leadership skills with the ability to build working relationships with individual employees, site leaders, regional EHS team, and site contractors.
  • The ability to prioritize tasks with a focus on completing tasks in a managed approach with attention to technical accuracy and within established timelines.
  • Knowledge of incident investigations and root cause analysis.
  • Familiar with new equipment introduction and validation processes; including, User defined criteria, FAT and SAT reviews, PSSR, and other steps to ensure the appropriate review and validation of equipment prior to site operation.
  • Maintains safety files and records.
  • May report to management on health and safety issues and concerns.
  • Support EHS programs and initiatives.
  • ISO 14001 Standard and system is preferred.

Education & Experience:

A minimum of (5) years of experience working in a manufacturing environment. Preference given to candidates with education and/or training specific to EHS in a manufacturing environment.

Successful candidates will be able to demonstrate creativity in identifying solutions which balance supporting customer and operational goals along with ensuring EHS requirements are compliance.

  • Medical, Dental, Prescription Drug, and Vision Insurance with HRA and HSA options

title: Fault & Autonomy Engineer - Experimental Space Programs (Associate or Experienced)
description:
Fault & Autonomy Engineer - Experimental Space Programs (Associate or Experienced)

Company:

The Boeing Company

The Boeing Experimental Systems Group (ESG) has an exciting opportunity for an Associate or Experienced Fault & Autonomy Engineer to join our team located in Seal Beach, CA, with potential options to work from El Segundo, CA, Aurora, CO, or Herndon, VA based on candidate eligibility. As a Fault & Autonomy Engineer in ESG, you will have the opportunity to personally contribute to the development of new first-of-kind space vehicles and missions. The ESG portfolio consists of a range of platforms and technologies including the X-37B, the world’s first fully autonomous reusable spaceplane, which is continuing to shape the future of space technology while currently flying its eighth mission.

As a member of our Systems Engineering Integration & Test (SEIT) Mission Design team, you will join a diverse team of system architects, Concept of Operations (ConOps) developers, fault and autonomy designers, and recommended operating procedure (ROP) authors.

As a Fault and Autonomy Engineer, you will be expected to lead coordination across all internal and external stakeholders to drive development and implementation of an optimal fault and autonomy architecture for your assigned program(s). You will serve as a core point of contact for customers and will work directly with subject matter experts across the business to quickly iterate and converge on achievable solutions that meet our customers’ needs. Our development timelines are aggressive and you will be asked to develop solutions to previously unsolved problems.

In this role, you will work in multidisciplinary teams to bring concept of operations to fruition in support of our customers’ mission objectives. You will work both as an individual contributor and as a project lead. An ideal candidate has a strong technical background across all spacecraft subsystems with particular depth in Attitude Control Systems (ACS)/Guidance Navigation & Control (GNC), flight software, or spacecraft operations as well as a strong system background spanning both space and ground domains. You will need to be able to dive into broad, minimally-defined design spaces and effectively lead integrated efforts.

Position Responsibilities:

· Support technology integration for and development of first-of-kind space vehicles and missions

· Develop and present review packages to internal and external senior leadership

· Work proactively and independently in a fast-paced, demanding atmosphere

· Ensure system hardware designs have adequate redundancy for required levels of fault tolerance

· Develop autonomy aligned with customer risk tolerance in the presence of anomalies

· Analyze system failure modes (via failure mode effects and criticality analysis (FMECA) or fault tree analysis)

· Develop software requirements for onboard fault protection to detect and isolate failures and transition to spacecraft safing modes

· Design autonomy or ground procedures to recover from failures

· Provide occasional on-call support for system anomalies

This position is expected to be 100% onsite. The selected candidate will be required to work onsite at one of the listed location options.

Work Authorization:

This position requires a current Tier 5 (T5), formerly known as a Single Scope Background Investigation (SSBI) (U.S. Citizenship required) or requires candidate agreed to enter a Continuous Evaluation program.

Basic Qualifications (Required Skills/Experience):

· Bachelor's, Master's or Doctorate of Science degree from an accredited course of study, in engineering, computer science, mathematics, physics or chemistry

Preferred Qualifications (Desired Skills/Experience):

· Master’s degree from an accredited course of study in engineering, computer science, mathematics, physics or chemistry

· 3 years of systems engineering experience

· 2 years of project management experience

· Strong oral, written, and visual communication skills

· Experience working with cross-functional teams and external customers

· Experience in spacecraft, launch vehicles, or highly autonomous unmanned systems

· Experience with failure analysis techniques (e.g, Fault Tree, FMECA)

· Experience with spacecraft mission operations

· Broad knowledge across spacecraft subsystems

title: Senior Associate Director of International Enrollment
description:
Position Title:

Senior Associate Director of International Enrollment

Position Type:

Regular

Hiring Range:

$77,600 - $93,170 annual; Compensation will be based on education, experience, skills relevant to the role, and internal equity.

Pay Frequency:

Annual

A. POSITION PURPOSE

Santa Clara University, a Jesuit and Catholic institution located in the heart of Silicon Valley, seeks a dynamic and collaborative professional for the position of Sr. Associate Director of International Enrollment. The University is committed to enrolling a talented global community of students who contribute to the academic excellence and mission of the institution.

Reporting to the Director of Undergraduate Admission, the Sr. Associate Director serves as a leading recruitment and enrollment ambassador to schools and communities worldwide. This role involves crafting strategic communication plans, utilizing data to drive enrollment priorities, and fostering vital partnerships with students, counselors, community colleges, and national and international organizations to attract and enroll the next generation of global leaders.

The Senior Associate Director will serve as one of the members of the mid-level management team that develops, manages, administers, implements and interprets university and/or department admission policies, processes and procedures.

B. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

International Recruitment and Outreach (35%)

  • Develop and cultivate relationships with prospective international first-year and transfer students and families, providing high-quality, student-oriented service from inquiry through enrollment.

  • Cultivate relationships with high school officials as well as independent counselors and international student-focused agencies and organizations. Facilitate and/or establish formal agreements with partnering organizations.

  • Travel, both internationally and domestically, to recruit international students and represent Santa Clara University at college fairs and information sessions.

  • Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with high school counselors, agency partners, and government entities worldwide.

  • Craft and implement specialized recruitment strategies and marketing materials tailored for international audiences, including printed and digital communications.

  • Act as a front-line representative to share the benefits of a Jesuit education and the university's academic and campus life opportunities.

  • Regularly engage with prospective students, families, and partners across multiple time zones, which may require working outside standard business hours, including early mornings, evenings, or weekends during peak recruitment periods.

  • Conduct virtual information sessions, interviews, and counselor/agency meetings to complement in-person recruitment travel, ensuring consistent outreach to markets not covered by scheduled travel.

​

Admission Evaluation and Operations (35%)

  • Evaluate international undergraduate applications and credentials; and assess transcripts for admission accuracy and completion.

  • Serve as a liaison with the ISS office to support their efforts towards visa processing and ensure proper immigration documents for international students. Collaborate with ISS on communication that will inform students on the enrollment process while fostering engagement and sense of community.

  • Oversee inbound and outbound communications and supporting systems to ensure prompt and accurate correspondence with international students and families. Work alongside additional campus departments participating in onboarding to deliver precise updates and support international students during their arrival at SCU, while considering new practices to support a growing and internationally diverse population.

  • Identify and foster new and existing markets for prospective international students using data and trend analysis.

  • Serve as Slate-CRM administrator for building and maximizing customer service & events related features to international students.

  • Consult Director of EM Marketing and with the Dean of Undergraduate Admission on key initiatives including planning development, business processes implementations, systems understanding, and implementation follow through.

  • Territory management for assigned region(s).

  • In addition, manage, mentor and evaluate supervised staff and students in effective outreach and application evaluation for international first year and transfer students.

​

Student Engagement and Leadership (20%)

  • Lead and supervise admission student interns/ambassadors focused on international engagement by providing ongoing mentorship and establishing clear expectations.

  • Support prospective students at every stage of the enrollment process, including application completion, enrollment deposits, and financial aid guidance.

  • Assist with new international student orientation and other campus engagement activities.

  • Design and participate in on-campus and weekend admission events as required.

  • The role will not initially have direct reports, though supervisory responsibilities may be added at a later time. The role will be expected to share coaching, training, and best practices in international enrollment with others across the admissions team.

​

Additional Responsibilities (10%)

  • Participate in domestic admission and recruitment as needed, based on a specifically assigned territory.

  • Make higher level management, evaluative and programmatic decisions.

  • Make recommendations to senior leadership for improvements and needs related to marketing, communications, and services support.

  • Recommend intra- and interdepartmental policies, guidelines, processes and procedures to the senior leadership team.

  • Participate in the University community via committees, projects, and events.

  • Provide backup support to other members of the Admission team as needed.

  • Perform additional duties as assigned.

​

C. QUALIFICATIONS

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.

  • Minimum 4-5 years experience in higher education admission with some specific experience working with international student populations.

  • Demonstrated ability to travel internationally and work effectively with people from diverse backgrounds and cultures.

  • Knowledge of immigration policies, procedures, and regulations as applicable to international students.

  • Virtual and in-person event management experience.

  • Demonstrated exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail.

  • Demonstrated excellent written and verbal communication.

  • Demonstrated ability to strategically manage budgets and maximize limited financial resources.

  • Ability to exercise sound judgment in a fast paced work environment.

  • Self-motivated to perform tasks with minimal supervision.

  • Proficiency with technology platforms and CRM systems (preferably Technolutions Slate).

  • Possession of a valid driver’s license with a satisfactory driving record.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree and admissions related work in a college or university is highly desirable.

  • Ability to speak a second language, with a preference for Spanish, Hindi, and/or Mandarin Chinese.

  • Experience working with first-years and transfer student populations in an undergraduate admission environment.

  • Familiarity with and support of Jesuit higher education values and mission.

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate data into actionable recruitment strategy.

D. PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described below are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, as amended, the California Fair Employment & Housing Act, and all other applicable laws, SCU provides reasonable accommodations for qualified persons with disabilities. A qualified individual is a person who meets skill, experience, education, or other requirements of the position, and who can perform the essential functions of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.

  • Travel to other buildings on campus.

E. WORK ENVIRONMENT

Job Description:

MEANINGFUL WORK AND PERSONAL IMPACT:

The work you’ll do at GDIT will be impactful to the mission of USSTRATCOM. USSTRATCOM is a Combatant Command responsible for strategic deterrence, nuclear operations, and enterprise IT services essential to national security. It oversees Nuclear Command, Control, and Communications (NC3), Joint Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations (JEMSO), Global Strike, and Missile Threat Assessments, working closely with other Combatant Commands, Services, and defense agencies. SCITLS will be a key component that will ensure mission success and the safety of the U.S. and its allies by providing 24/7 IT services and network support for NIPRNet, SIPRNet, JWICS, and SAP/SAR environment.

You will play a crucial role in providing support in the following areas:

  • Authoring formal Requests for Change (RFCs) with comprehensive implementation and rollback plans, scheduling Authorized Service Interruptions (ASIs), and executing technical tasks within approved maintenance windows
  • Managing and resolving assigned Tier I-III network incidents, service requests, and task orders within ServiceNow while creating/maintaining detailed troubleshooting documentation
  • Scheduling, testing, and performing operating system upgrades and security patches across Cisco IOS, IOS-XE, and NX-OS devices while validating pre- and post-upgrade operational stability
  • Auditing network switches and routers against DISA Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) benchmarks, implementing required configuration hardening, and maintaining compliance documentation and vulnerability remediation tracking
  • Monitoring enterprise network health and telemetry alerts using platforms such as SolarWinds to proactively triage, diagnose, and resolve Tier I-III campus and datacenter connectivity issues
  • Assisting with firewall operations, recommending security rule modifications, and traffic troubleshooting across Palo Alto appliances
  • Troubleshoot Network Access Control (NAC) and authentication issues utilizing ForeScout, Cisco TACACS+, and RADIUS platforms
  • Assisting with the monitoring and operational maintenance of datacenter Cisco Nexus spine-leaf fabrics, routing, and VXLAN overlay environments
  • Supporting network hardware lifecycle initiatives, including hardware refresh planning, inventory auditing, tracking end-of-life/end-of-support assets, and sanitizing decommissioned gear
  • Creating, updating, and sustaining detailed physical and logical network diagrams and rack elevation schematics
  • Performing physical installations, including racking, cabling, labeling, and decommissioning network hardware across telecommunication closets and datacenter facilities
  • Executing technical infrastructure project tasks, hardware deployments, provisioning, and special assignments as directed by engineering leadership
  • Ability to perform after-hours work on an as-needed basis may be required

  • Education: BA/BS or equivalent relevant experience
  • Experience: 8+ years of related experience
  • Required Certifications:
    • Security+ or DoD 8140 Compliant Certification
    • ITIL Foundations v4 Certificate or the ability to obtain within 9 mos
    • Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA)
  • Must have a current/active Top Secret clearance with the ability to obtain TS/SCI status
  • Location: Offutt AFB, NE
  • Hands-on experience configuring, administering, and updating enterprise and datacenter network devices running Cisco IOS, IOS-XE, and NX-OS
  • Direct experience reviewing DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) and applying STIGs to harden Cisco network infrastructure
  • Working knowledge or operational experience with enterprise firewalls, including Palo Alto Networks (PAN-OS)
  • Practical experience administering or supporting Network Access Control (NAC) solutions and authentication protocols such as 802.1X, including ForeScout, TACACS+, and RADIUS
  • Familiarity with enterprise network monitoring and management systems (such as SolarWinds) for fault isolation and performance analysis
  • Foundational understanding of datacenter spine-leaf architecture, routing protocols (OSPF/BGP), and VXLAN overlay concepts
  • Experience supporting hardware lifecycle management, including equipment refreshes, inventory tracking, and device decommissioning
  • Demonstrated experience preparing change requests and executing work within scheduled Authorized Service Interruptions (ASIs)
  • Experience developing and maintaining network topology diagrams and rack elevation layouts
  • Practical experience with physical hardware deployment, including racking, stacking, and copper/fiber cabling standards
  • Proven track record of supporting structured infrastructure project work, equipment cutovers, and directed technical tasks
