Below is the full job description:

JOB OPPORTUNITY

Job Title: DevOps Specialist

Detail Information
Contract Duration 12 Months
Location Remote – Canada (may require onsite meetings in Edmonton up to 15%)
Client Public Sector
Start Date ASAP

Position Overview

The Digital Design and Delivery Division (DDD) is the Province's centre for digital delivery. It was established to maximize capability and confidence in modern digital practice by ensuring service quality and value through standards and controls. This includes utilizing human-centred design approaches together with agile methodology and modern data practices. DDD works in partnership with GoA ministries to deliver programs that better serve Albertans.

DDD requires up to seven (7) DevOps Specialists to work with DDD on service innovation, program review, and digital transformation projects across the GoA. The DevOps Specialists will work as part of cross-functional program review or product delivery teams. These teams, led by GoA product owners and DDD, work collaboratively and collectively participate in a full range of activities including field research, backlog definition and refinement, and sprint planning and execution.

Digital transformation projects review the current state of services, identify future opportunities, and then deliver new services that are efficient, effective, and affordable.

DevOps Specialists will be responsible for overseeing the quality in the delivery of digital services and ensuring that a team's focus is on quality. A DevOps Specialist is typically responsible for creating test plans, test cases, and scenarios, identifying required test types, assets, and data environments and tools, and creating automated test suites.

Scope of Services

The DevOps Specialists will be required on a full-time basis, working across two (2) to three (3) projects. Time, location, and frequency of work will vary depending on the needs of the project. At the end of each term, it is expected that the DevOps Specialists may work a maximum of 1,960 hours, unless otherwise agreed upon with the Province. However, DevOps Specialists may be required to work fewer or more hours depending on the nature and needs of their work, as directed by the Province.

Services and project deliverables should evolve as the work progresses, in response to emerging user and business needs, as well as design and technical opportunities. However, the following must be delivered iteratively over the course of the project:

Key Responsibilities & Deliverables

Automation & Operations

  • Create scripts, tools, and procedures for operations by designing and implementing automation for limited downtime deployment and maintenance.

  • Lead operations of digital services in production by:

    • Managing configuration and credentials for the production environment

    • Planning and managing maintenance activities

    • Managing database upgrades and migrations, backups, recoveries, etc.

CI/CD & Environment Management

  • Provide operations support for implementation and enhancement of digital services by:

    • Creating templates and patterns for application deployments and CI/CD pipelines

    • Creating scripts and tools to automate the establishment of environments for development and testing

Observability & Monitoring

  • Create tools, scripts, and processes that will enable application teams to have better observability of the application through monitoring and telemetry tools.

Best Practices & Testing Support

  • Support delivery teams in adopting best practices by:

    • Providing operations support for early and frequent integration testing, security scans, system testing, and performance and load testing

    • Providing operations support for early and frequent delivery to end-users in limited availability launches (Alphas and Betas)

AI & Process Automation

  • Removal of manual processes through the implementation of automated/AI solutions.

The Province and the Contractor shall determine changes to Services and Materials as required through the Artifacts.

Required Skills & Experience

Education

  • University degree or college diploma in Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or a related discipline.

  • An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

Experience

  • 5+ years of progressive experience in DevOps, cloud operations, or site reliability engineering.

  • Demonstrated experience designing and implementing automation for deployment and maintenance.

  • Strong experience with CI/CD pipelines, application deployments, and environment automation.

  • Proven experience managing production environments, including configuration, credentials, maintenance, and database operations.

  • Experience with monitoring, telemetry, and observability tools.

  • Experience supporting integration testing, security scans, system testing, and performance/load testing.

  • Experience implementing automated/AI solutions to remove manual processes.

Technical Skills

  • Strong knowledge of cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP).

  • Proficiency with CI/CD tools (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, GitLab CI).

  • Experience with containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes, OpenShift).

  • Experience with Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Ansible, CloudFormation).

  • Scripting skills (Python, Bash, PowerShell).

  • Experience with database management (SQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB).

  • Knowledge of security best practices and compliance requirements.

  • Experience with AI/automation tools for process improvement is an asset.

Knowledge & Competencies

  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.

  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

  • Ability to work effectively in cross-functional Agile teams.

  • Strong organizational and time-management skills.

Work Requirements

Location

  • DevOps Specialists will primarily work remotely; however, may be required to attend meetings or work sessions in Edmonton on reasonable notice from the Province, up to 15%.

  • Time to travel and any associated expenses to and from Edmonton will be at no cost to the Province.

Work Authorization

  • Work MUST be done within Canada due to network and data security requirements.

Hours

  • Full-time basis, working across two (2) to three (3) projects.

  • Maximum of 1,960 hours per term, unless otherwise agreed upon with the Province.

Equipment

  • The resource must provide their own computer and related equipment.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is an experienced DevOps Specialist with a strong background in automation, CI/CD, cloud operations, and production support. They bring proven experience managing digital services in production, creating automated test suites, and implementing observability tools. The candidate is highly collaborative, detail-oriented, and capable of working across multiple projects while maintaining high-quality standards and compliance with government policies.

title: Receiving Clerk
description:
Receiving Clerk
OVERVIEW
Cincinnati Test Systems (CTS) is a leader in the design and manufacture of leak test and assembly verification instrumentation, providing standard and custom solutions for a wide range of manufacturing applications. CTS serves customers across diverse industries, including transportation, energy, medical, consumer, and industrial markets.
The Receiving Clerk is responsible for the accurate and efficient receipt of incoming materials, components, small packages, and equipment. This position verifies incoming shipments against purchase orders and documentation, records receipts in the ERP system, and ensures materials are properly identified and moved to the appropriate location within the facility.
This role works closely with Inventory, Purchasing, Accounting, Production, and Shipping to resolve discrepancies and keep materials moving efficiently throughout the operation.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Receive and process incoming domestic and international shipments, including small packages, components, materials, and equipment.
  • Verify incoming materials against purchase orders, packing slips, and other receiving documentation for accuracy.
  • Accurately record receipts and related transactions in the ERP system.
  • Identify and communicate quantity, part number, purchase order, or other receiving discrepancies.
  • Work with Purchasing, Accounting, and other departments to resolve purchase order and receiving discrepancies.
  • Complete and maintain required receiving paperwork and documentation.
  • Unload inbound shipments using a forklift, hand truck, pallet jack, or other material-handling equipment.
  • Safely move received materials to designated inventory, inspection, production, or staging areas.
  • Process miscellaneous receipts, including customer-supplied parts, sample parts, and other non-standard incoming materials.
  • Receive and process parts and materials for assembly teams.
  • Assist with loading outbound shipments as needed.
  • Support Inventory and Shipping activities as needed to maintain efficient material flow.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe Shipping & Receiving area, including associated storage and mezzanine areas.
  • Follow established receiving, inventory control, quality, and safety procedures.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.
QUALIFICATIONS
  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • One to two years of receiving, shipping, warehouse, inventory, material handling, or related experience preferred.
  • Experience working with an ERP, MRP, shipping/receiving, or inventory management system preferred; Epicor experience is a plus.
  • Basic computer skills with the ability and willingness to learn company software and systems.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to accurately verify part numbers, quantities, purchase orders, and shipping documentation.
  • Ability to accurately follow written and verbal instructions.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to prioritize work in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with other departments.
  • Forklift experience preferred; must be willing and able to complete company-required forklift certification.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS
The physical demands described below are representative of those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this position.
  • Ability to regularly stand, walk, reach, and handle materials throughout the workday.
  • Ability to occasionally stoop, bend, crouch, kneel, push, and pull.
  • Ability to lift and move items weighing up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to safely operate a forklift and other material-handling equipment as required.
  • Ability to perform close visual inspection of parts, labels, documentation, and materials, including distinguishing colors when necessary.
  • Ability to safely move throughout warehouse, receiving, production, and storage areas.
WORK ENVIRONMENT
This position is performed on-site in a manufacturing and shipping/receiving environment. The employee will regularly work in receiving, warehouse, inventory, production, and shipping areas and may be exposed to typical manufacturing conditions, including noise, moving equipment, varying levels of activity, and frequent movement of incoming and outgoing materials.
WHY CINCINNATI TEST SYSTEMS?
At Cincinnati Test Systems, we offer the opportunity to build a career with a growing, global organization while working alongside a team focused on delivering high-quality products and solutions to our customers.
CTS offers competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, career development opportunities, and the opportunity to contribute to an organization serving customers and industries around the world.

title: Senior Security Engineer - Sec Ops
description:
Are you a collaborative Sec Ops Engineer looking to work for a mission driven global organization?

About our Team

You’ll be joining the Security Engineering team within Elsevier’s Information Security & Data Protection department. Our team designs, builds, and operates the security tooling and platforms used across Elsevier Technology, spanning both vendor platforms and team-built services. The team works closely with Incident Response, Threat Engineering, and Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC), and partners with business and engineering teams to ensure security tooling is effectively adopted across our cloud estate.

About the Role

As a Senior Security Engineer, you help lead in designing, building, and operating security tooling at scale, while raising the technical bar for the wider team. You will own architecture decisions for one or more platforms, guide junior and mid-level engineers through code and design review, and act as a trusted technical voice with Incident Response, Threat Engineering, and GRC. This role suits someone with deep, hands-on cloud security engineering experience who is ready to take ownership beyond individual delivery, shaping how the team builds and operates security tooling

Responsibilities

  • Leading the design, architecture, and delivery of security platforms and services.
  • Owning and evolve Infrastructure as Code standards (Terraform) and CI/CD practices (GitHub Actions) across the team, ensuring reliable, secure, and repeatable deployments.
  • Providing technical leadership and mentorship to junior and mid-level engineers, including design review, code review, and guidance on secure engineering practices.
  • Driving integration, tuning, and lifecycle management of core security tooling.
  • Partnering with Incident Response, Threat Engineering, and GRC to translate emerging threats, incidents, and compliance requirements into engineering solutions and roadmap priorities.
  • Championing adoption of AI-assisted engineering practices (e.g. Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) to improve team velocity, code quality, and test coverage.
  • Leading troubleshooting and root-cause analysis for security tooling incidents, and drive resilience improvements through capacity planning, disaster recovery planning, and runbook development.
  • Representing SENG in architecture reviews and cross-functional technical forums, advocating for secure-by-design and secure-by-default practices.
  • Delivering production-ready systems on time and within budget, and hold the team accountable to engineering and security standards.

Requirements

We recognize that no one will meet every requirement. If you are excited about this role and have relevant experience, we encourage you to apply.

  • Significant hands-on experience in security engineering or a related field, including designing and operating cloud-native security platforms at production scale.
  • Demonstrated ownership of security architecture in AWS (or OCI/Aliyun), including multi-account environments and cross-region/CN considerations.
  • Advanced proficiency with Terraform and Infrastructure as Code practices, with experience setting standards and patterns for a team.
  • Experience designing and maintaining CI/CD pipelines (e.g. GitHub Actions) for reliability and security.
  • Broad, hands-on experience across security tool categories: SIEM, EDR, DLP, PAM, WAF, SOAR, and vulnerability management,
  • Proven track record mentoring engineers and leading technical design decisions within a team.
  • Advanced scripting and software development skills (e.g. Python), including experience building and operating production services (APIs, cronjobs) on Kubernetes/EKS.
  • Practical experience with AI-assisted engineering tools (e.g. GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Spec-driven development) and sound judgment on where they add the most value.
  • Experience with Agile and/or DevOps frameworks, including driving improvements to team process and delivery practices.

At Legacy Community Health, we believe in making a difference in the lives of our communities, and we need your passion and dedication to join our journey! Education

description:

EmergeOrtho is committed to being the trusted leader in innovative, quality-focused comprehensive musculoskeletal care. With offices across North Carolina, our Blue Ridge Region is currently seeking a Physical Therapy Technician to join us at our Waynesville location. The Physical Therapy Technician supports both the Physical Therapist and their Assistant in planning and implementing patient care. The Technician is responsible for administering physical therapy modalities of treatment under the direct supervision of the Physical Therapist. The primary functions of this role include assisting with patient preparation before treatment, responding to patients’ requests for assistance while performing the exercise program, and maintaining the equipment used during the treatment session. Additional responsibilities include maintaining patient confidentiality, cleaning, and sterilizing treatment areas, performing laundry services, and clerical tasks as requested.

  • High school diploma required
  • Bachelor’s degree preferred but not required
  • Previous experience in an orthopedic clinic setting preferred

title: Senior Program Officer
description:
About the role

The Senior Program Officer (SPO) is a key contributor to QueensCare’s Charitable Division activities, including modernization of policies, processes, and evaluation frameworks, while strengthening alignment with QueensCare’s charitable purpose and community impact goals. They will drive cross-departmental collaboration, ensuring QueensCare’s grantmaking and direct service programs work seamlessly together to improve access to care and services for Los Angeles residents.

Reporting to the Chief Strategy and Program Officer (CSPO), the SPO designs, implements, and evaluates a portfolio of grants and scholarships aligned with board approved strategy. The SPO will supervise the Program Officer (s), grant operations, support engagement with the Board and relevant Committees, and partner closely with the Program Officer and Associate Director, Community Partnerships to drive strategic impact through grants and QueensCare Health Alliance community health services.

What you'll do

ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Leadership and Oversight

  • Provides direct supervision and leadership to the Charitable Division Team, mentoring and developing staff to support professional growth and high performance.
  • In partnership with the CSPO and Program Officer, develops, executes, and evaluates grantmaking strategies to advance community health improvement in Los Angeles, including charitable grantmaking and scholarship programs.
  • Modernizes grantmaking policies, procedures, and systems to ensure compliance, efficiency, and alignment with organizational priorities.
  • Leads improvements to QueensCare’s grant management and evaluation systems, including strengthening data quality and effective reporting.
  • Serves as a bridge between grantmaking and QueensCare Health Alliance services, strengthening grantee relationships and services to drive community impact.

Partnership & Collaboration

  • Maintains and develops relationships with current and prospective grant partners.
  • Identifies, cultivates, and stewards strategic alliances with healthcare providers, community-based organizations, faith-based organizations, government agencies, and philanthropic institutions.
  • Directly engages impacted communities around grantmaking strategy; builds internal capacity to execute community-informed grantmaking and health programming.
  • Works closely with grantmaking and QueensCare Health Alliance teams to ensure partnership opportunities are integrated across the organization (i.e., linking grantees with QueensCare’s direct care programs to amplify community impact).
  • Leads planning of grantee and community partner convenings.
  • Represents QueensCare at philanthropic and healthcare, nonprofit, and community affinity groups, conferences, and other external venues.

Governance & Stewardship

  • Leads creation of Board and Committee packets for grant review and approval, including writeups, dashboards, and reports that support decision-making and compliance.
  • Ensures completion of financial and other diligence for all grant partnerships.
  • Supports Committee and Board engagement, including orientations, retreats, site visits, and other opportunities for learning and governance improvements.

Policies and Organizational Alignment

  • Supports and implements the organization’s mission, vision, and values across all services and partnerships.
  • Develops, updates, and enforces policies and procedures to ensure effective service operations.
  • Promotes a culture of service excellence, accountability, and continuous learning.
  • Ensures staff are trained and supported to meet organizational and regulatory expectations.
  • Expected to uphold organizational standards of professionalism, accountability, ethics, and integrity, while fostering a respectful and high-performing work environment.
  • Responsibilities include providing ongoing coaching and performance feedback, addressing performance or conduct concerns in a timely manner, and utilizing progressive counseling, when appropriate, to support employee accountability and development.

Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and ability required.

EDUCATION

Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy, Public Health, Health Administration, Social Work, Psychology, or a related field required. Master’s degree preferred.

EXPERIENCE

  • Minimum of seven (7) years of progressive leadership experience in grantmaking, nonprofit, or government services.
  • At least three (3) years of direct management experience of philanthropic or nonprofit staff.
  • Demonstrated ability to contribute to strategy development and execution across complex organizations and multiple teams.
  • Proven experience managing teams and cultivating collaborative, trust-based cultures.
  • Experience with facilitating conversations with impacted communities and direct community engagement on philanthropic strategy, or community organizing around shared goals.
  • Familiarity with healthcare access, community health, and the needs of underserved populations.
  • Proficiency with grants management systems (Salesforce preferred) and data-informed evaluation tools.
  • Excellent writing, communication, and facilitation skills; confidence in presenting to Boards and diverse audiences.

KNOWLEDGE

  • Deep understanding of grantmaking processes, impact measurement, and philanthropic compliance.
  • Knowledge of both strategic and trust-based grantmaking.
  • Knowledge of community health systems, education, and social services.
  • Knowledge of interdisciplinary care models and/or collective impact models.
  • Strong understanding of program evaluation and data-driven decision-making.

SKILLS

  • Strong leadership, mentorship and supervisory skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities effectively.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage diverse stakeholders.
  • Strategic thinking with strong operational execution.
  • Strong organizational and analytical skills.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment and decision-making in complex situations.
  • Bilingual (Spanish) preferred.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to use hands to finger, handle or feel and reach with hands and arms. The employee frequently is required to stand, walk, and sit. The employee is occasionally required to climb or balance, stoop, kneel, crouch or sit. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 30 pounds. The employee is occasionally required to ascend and descend one flight of stairs. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, color vision, and ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. We’re looking for innovators who can help us keep building on our wide portfolio of secure, affordable, integrated, and multi-domain systems and technologies that fuel those missions. By joining in our shared mission, we will support yours by expanding your personal network and developing skills, whether you are new to the field or an industry thought leader. At Northrop Grumman, you will have the resources, support, and team to do some of the best work of your career.

The Northrop Grumman Classified Solutions team is seeking a Principal Computer Systems Analyst - Windows to support information system lifecycle activities. The selected candidate will be required to work on-site, full-time at our Sunnyvale, CA location.

Job responsibilities will include but not be limited to the following:

  • Maintain smooth operation of multiple Windows based networks and multi-user computer systems, including coordination with network, software, and system engineers, PC desktop technicians, project managers, end users, and customer and IT management.

  • Provide regular monitoring and security analysis to meet U.S. Government security standards.

  • Analyze internal and external customer requirements and determine equipment and software requirements for solutions to problems by means of automated systems.

  • Recommend and implement system enhancements that will improve the performance and reliability of the system including installing, upgrading/patching, monitoring, problem resolution, and configuration management.

  • Provide backup and recovery services, manage file systems and disk space, and manage virus protection on a routine basis.

  • Create and maintain user and computer accounts and modify file permissions and security access list.

  • Test new releases of products to ensure compatibility and minimize user impact.

  • Develop and document technical processes and procedures as needed.

  • Make recommendations to purchase hardware, software, and system components

  • Interact, meet, discuss, and troubleshoot issues with vendors, and evaluate vendor products, services, and suggestions.

  • Adhere to strict Information Systems security guidelines in all cases.

  • Prepare security documentation for input to Computer Security.

  • Report project status as required for all recurring and non-recurring efforts.

  • Provide specifications and detailed schematics for network architecture as needed.


Basic Qualifications:

  • Associate's degree with 7 years of experience, or a Bachelor's degree with 5 years of experience, or a Master's degree with 3 years of experience; a High School diploma or equivalent with 9 years of experience may be considered in lieu of a completed degree.

  • Applicants must have a current U.S. Government Secret level security clearance (at a minimum), to include a closed investigation date completed within the last 6 years, or must be enrolled in the U.S. Government Continuous Evaluation Program (CEP), in order to be considered; the required security clearance must be maintained as a condition of continued employment.

  • Current Security+ CE certification; the required certification must be maintained as a condition of continued employment.

  • Windows experience to include proficiency with Windows OS (Windows 11 and Server 2012/2016 preferred) and Active Directory concepts (including DHCP and DNS).

  • Experience with server management.

  • Experience installing, configuring, and maintaining computer hardware in a networked environment.

  • Ability to work after hours and weekends as needed.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Active U.S. Government Top Secret security clearance.

  • Hardware experience with HPE and Dell Servers, to include firmware patching, hardware upgrades, lights out management experience, troubleshooting, and visualization.

  • Experience with Certification & Accreditation process.

  • Basic understanding of Linux OS functionality, commands, and file structures and/or certification for current versions.

  • SAN Knowledge – Interactions with VMware applications (vSphere objects, Horizon View, etc.), and fiber channel infrastructure concepts.

  • Ability to perform network analysis.

  • Experience operating under and managing systems within NISPOM Chapter 8, DCID 6/3-ICD 503, RMF, STIG, JAFAN, or JSIG information system environments.

  • Experience with SCCM.

  • Experience with routers, switches, IPS/IDS, and firewalls.

  • Experience with Windows, file, web, and remote execution servers and Terminal Services.

  • Experience with information security technologies such as event log management, intrusion detection, HIPS, anti-virus, and vulnerability assessments.

  • Rudimentary scripting experience.

  • Experience with the creation and deployment of system images in an enterprise environment.

  • U.S. Government 8570/8140 Certification in a primary OS (Windows, Linux, Cisco).

  • Ability to design and troubleshoot VPNs.

title: Scrum Master
description:
emergiTEL is hiring for Scrum Master
Location: Remote – Edmonton Canada (may require onsite meetings in Edmonton up to 15%)
Client: Public Sector
Contract Duration: 1 Year
Start Date: ASAP

Below is the full job description:

JOB OPPORTUNITY

Job Title: Scrum Master

Detail Information
Contract Duration 1 Year
Location Remote – Canada (may require onsite meetings in Edmonton up to 15%)
Client Public Sector
Start Date ASAP

Position Overview

The Public Sector client has embarked on transforming the work of government to deliver simpler, more efficient, and better services for citizens, ensuring that their needs are effectively met in the digital age. The Province has a strategic role within government to drive efficiencies, innovation, and modernization.

The Digital Design and Delivery Division (DDD) is the Province's centre for digital delivery. It was established to maximize capability and confidence in modern digital practice by ensuring service quality and value through standards and controls. This includes utilizing human-centred design approaches together with agile methodology and modern data practices. DDD works in partnership with ministries to deliver programs that better serve citizens.

DDD requires ten (10) Scrum Masters to work with DDD on service innovation, program review, and digital transformation projects. The Scrum Master will work as part of cross-functional program review or product delivery teams. These teams, led by product owners and DDD, work collaboratively and collectively participate in a full range of activities including field research, backlog definition and refinement, and sprint planning and execution.

Digital transformation projects review the current state of services, identify future opportunities, and then deliver new services that are efficient, effective, and affordable.

Scrum Masters identify and remove roadblocks and distractions that affect sprint commitments and prevent delivery of product features. Scrum Masters will be responsible for the management of the agile sprint process for cross-functional program review or product delivery teams, and will provide leadership and mentoring in agile principles, policies, and procedures, to enable the teams to self-organize and deliver consistently on sprint deliverables. Scrum Masters will be expected to manage communication, maximize transparency, disseminate information related to service delivery, and resolve any conflict when it arises.

Scrum Masters are expected to demonstrate AI fluency through daily use of generative AI and agentic tooling for delivery-grade work, including drafting, analysis, structured retrieval, meeting synthesis, backlog support, delivery reporting, and automation. Scrum Masters should be comfortable with prompt design, retrieval-augmented generation, and evaluation of AI output for risk, hallucination, privacy, sensitivity, and appropriateness for use in the delivery environment. Scrum Masters are expected to build AI-augmented routines that improve team delivery practices and reduce administrative overhead; they do not only consume AI tools.

Scrum Masters are also expected to demonstrate process automation literacy, including working knowledge of process-automation patterns such as workflow automation, digital forms, structured intake, status reporting, agentic process orchestration, and the implications of these patterns for roles and workflows. Scrum Masters must be able to translate technical change into accessible communication for business, product owners, delivery teams, and stakeholders.

Scope of Services

The Scrum Master will be required on a full-time basis, working across two (2) or more projects. Time, location, and frequency of work will vary depending on the needs of the particular project. At the end of each term, it is expected that the Scrum Master may work a maximum of 1,960 hours, unless otherwise agreed upon with the Province. However, the Scrum Master may be required to work fewer or more hours depending on the nature and needs of their work, as directed by the Province.

Services and project deliverables should evolve as the work progresses, in response to emerging user and business needs, as well as design and technical opportunities. However, the following must be delivered (iteratively) over the course of the project:

Key Responsibilities & Deliverables

Agile Leadership & Mentorship

  • Lead and mentor cross-functional program review and product delivery teams in agile principles, policies, and procedures.

  • Lead and facilitate key agile ceremonies, including planning sessions, stand-ups, sprint reviews, product demos, retrospectives, and refinement. This could also include ad hoc sessions.

Coaching & Facilitation

  • Facilitate effective delivery of Services and deliverables by the cross-functional program review and product delivery teams through coaching and guiding the product owner and the team. Specifically:

    • Coach the team on the application of agile methodology including how to provide effective estimates and sprint commitments, how to adjust for external dependencies, how to eliminate blocking issues, etc.

    • Promote the successful achievement of sprint goals and commitments, by acting as the intermediary between the product owner and team.

    • Guide the product owner on reporting, release planning, and road-mapping.

Metrics & Reporting

  • Maintain delivery metrics and report on product level plans, progress, and quality assurance using project management tools and Artifacts such as sprint burndown/velocity charts, product backlogs, and sprint backlogs.

  • Report on progress to the Province as directed.

AI Fluency & Automation

  • Demonstrate AI fluency through daily use of generative AI and agentic tooling for drafting, analysis, structured retrieval, backlog support, meeting synthesis, delivery reporting, and automation.

  • Apply prompt design, retrieval-augmented generation, and review of AI output for risk, hallucination, privacy, sensitivity, and delivery use.

  • Build AI-augmented routines to improve agile delivery support; do not only consume AI tools.

  • Demonstrate process automation literacy, including workflow automation, digital forms, structured intake, status reporting, and agentic process orchestration.

  • Translate technical change and automation impacts into accessible communication for staff, product owners, delivery teams, and stakeholders.

Digital Service Delivery

  • Participate in digital service delivery activities, such as user research and usability testing.

The Province and the Contractor shall determine changes to Services and Materials as required through the Artifacts.

Required Skills & Experience

Education

  • University degree or college diploma in Computer Science, Information Technology, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

  • An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

Experience

  • 5+ years of progressive experience as a Scrum Master, Agile Coach, or similar role.

  • Demonstrated experience leading and facilitating agile ceremonies (planning, stand-ups, sprint reviews, demos, retrospectives, refinement).

  • Proven experience coaching teams on agile methodology, estimates, sprint commitments, and removing blockers.

  • Experience guiding Product Owners on reporting, release planning, and road-mapping.

  • Experience maintaining delivery metrics (burndown/velocity charts, product backlogs, sprint backlogs).

  • Experience working in cross-functional digital delivery teams.

  • Experience with user research and usability testing is an asset.

  • Public sector experience is an asset.

AI & Automation Skills

  • Demonstrated AI fluency – daily use of generative AI and agentic tooling for delivery-grade work.

  • Experience with prompt design, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and evaluation of AI output for risk, hallucination, privacy, and sensitivity.

  • Experience building AI-augmented routines to improve delivery practices and reduce administrative overhead.

  • Process automation literacy – workflow automation, digital forms, structured intake, status reporting, agentic process orchestration.

  • Ability to translate technical change into accessible communication for diverse stakeholders.

Certifications

  • Certified Scrum Master (CSM) or Professional Scrum Master (PSM) certification is required.

  • Advanced Agile certifications (A-CSM, CSP-SM, SAFe) are an asset.

Knowledge & Competencies

  • Strong facilitation, coaching, and mentorship skills.

  • Excellent communication and conflict resolution skills.

  • Strong organizational and time-management skills.

  • Ability to work effectively across multiple projects simultaneously.

Work Requirements

Location

  • This resource will work remotely; however, the resource may be required to attend meetings or work sessions in office on reasonable notice from the Province, up to 15%.

  • All travel time and costs associated with relocation, commuting, accommodation, meals, and any travel to or within Edmonton or Alberta will be the sole responsibility of the resource and will not be any cost to the Province.

Work Authorization

  • Work must be done from within Canada due to network and data security issues.

Hours

  • Standard hours of work are 08:15 – 16:30 Alberta time, Monday through Friday, excluding holidays observed by the Province.

  • Full-time basis, working across two (2) or more projects.

  • Maximum of 1,960 hours per term, unless otherwise agreed upon with the Province.

Equipment

  • It is preferred the resource has their own equipment, though the Province will provide a laptop/desktop if necessary.

  • If the resource requires their own equipment, the computer's operating system must be a modern version of Windows or MacOS compatible with Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) and related software for remote access. Windows is preferred.

  • AVD/remote-related software will be installed on the resource's computer.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is an experienced Scrum Master with a strong background in agile delivery, team coaching, and facilitation. They bring proven experience leading agile ceremonies, coaching teams and Product Owners, and maintaining delivery metrics. The candidate demonstrates AI fluency through daily use of generative AI tools for drafting, analysis, backlog support, and reporting, and has experience with process automation patterns. They are highly collaborative, detail-oriented, and capable of working across multiple projects while maintaining high-quality standards and compliance with government policies.

title: Virtual IOP Therapist - California (Internal Hire)
description:
Job Description

We are seeking a highly skilled clinician with advanced expertise in ERP and ACT to provide intensive, evidence-based virtual care for individuals with high-acuity OCD. A strong therapist candidate for a virtual OCD Intensive Treatment Service is a clinician with advanced training in CBT, ERP, ACT, HRT, and PE. This role requires exceptional clinical judgment, strong crisis-management skills, and the ability to deliver structured individual and group therapy in a fast-paced higher level of care setting. The ideal candidate demonstrates steady clinical presence, clear directive intervention, excellent documentation, and the capacity to support complex presentations. Reliability, strong boundaries, and effective collaboration across a multidisciplinary, virtual team are essential.This clinician is skilled in delivering clear, directive interventions while maintaining warmth, transparency, and collaborative communication with both members and their families. They excel in virtual care delivery, adapt seamlessly across time zones, and can confidently hold boundaries, manage crises appropriately, and document to a high standard. Ideal candidates bring experience treating complex presentations (including co-occurring PTSD and body-focused repetitive behaviors) even if formal program tracks for those conditions are not yet active. Above all, they show strong clinical presence, reliability, and the ability to motivate members through intensive, evidence-based work while contributing to a cohesive, high-functioning clinical team.



Key Responsibilities:

  • Conduct evaluations virtually for internal and external candidates for Intensive
  • Treat high-acuity OCD as the primary presentation, including common co-occurring conditions (depression, anxiety, trauma, body-focused repetitive behaviors), using CBT, ERP, ACT, HRT, Motivational interviewing and PE.
  • Demonstrates knowledge of the variety of ways clients express stress reactions both behaviorally (e.g., avoidance, aggression, passivity) and psychologically/emotionally (e.g., hyperarousal, avoidance, intrusive memories)
  • Provide individual and group therapy in a virtual setting with a team approach to clinical and administrative functions.
  • Provide ongoing case management, ensuring continuity between members, clinicians, external providers, community agencies, and support systems.
  • Ongoing assessment of safety concerns and risk, escalating per protocol
  • Support Members’ engagement and treatment adherence through check-ins, motivational strategies, and consistent communication.
  • Session-level clinical adjustments and exposure hierarchy changes
  • Group redirection and in-the-moment management of treatment-interfering behavior
  • Initial risk assessment and safety planning within protocol
  • Routine coordination with outside providers and community agencies
  • Aftercare and discharge planning within program guidelines
  • Maintaining assigned caseload for members individual and family therapy while members are in program
  • Develop treatment plans, assist in aftercare and discharge planning.
  • Maintain strategic relationships with community therapists and local agencies to support referral pathways and program partnerships..
  • Collaborate cross-departmentally (clinical, operations, leadership) to maintain clinical excellence, communicate program needs, and support workflow efficiency.
  • Maintain accurate documentation and track program outcomes, including EHR records, metrics, KPIs, workflow updates, and improvement feedback.
  • Maintain Member records and ensure compliance with ethical and legal standards.
  • Develop and implement individualized treatment plans using evidence-based practices.
  • Provide individual, group, multi-family groups, and family therapy sessions.
  • Collaborate with other clinicians to provide comprehensive care.
  • Full Time Providers:
    • 40 hour work week
    • Complete 25 hours of direct clinical work per week
    • Attend a world-class training program developed by industry leaders
    • Attend 2 hours of weekly group clinical consultation
    • Will participate in and complete cross-license application as needed for program expansion
    • Approximately 15 hours per week facilitating Intensive groups and Intensive admission assessments, individual sessions, supported ERP, pre-screening calls, and family sessions. The ratio is set by program census and reviewed monthly. The other 12 expected clinical hours are in the outpatient network.
    • Clinicians move between both functions within the same day.
  • Organized, quick and enthusiastic learner, excellent communicator, good with time management
  • Have a confidential, private location to work remotely from with reliable internet access
  • Comfortable and efficient with using technology to communicate
  • Ambitious and ready to keep up with a goal-driven, start-up environment

Qualifications:

  • Full and unrestricted license in good standing to practice in your state.
    • Masters Degree Required
    • Licensed Psychologist, Licensed Professional Counselor, Licensed Clinical Social Worker or equivalent in California.
    • Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist preferred
  • Highly organized and flexible professional who is a quick and enthusiastic learner, equipped with excellent communication, strong interpersonal skills, and effective time-management capabilities.
  • Navigate complex cases in a group setting
  • Raises disagreement with the person involved, close to when it happens, with a specific proposal rather than letting concerns accumulate or escalating first.
  • Takes clinical feedback in group consultation and applies it to program skills
  • Navigation of group dynamics and works collaboratively with team to pivot the milieu
  • Have a confidential, private location to work remotely from with reliable internet access
  • Comfortable and efficient with using technology to communicate
  • Ambitious and ready to keep up with a goal-driven, start-up environment
  • Proficiency in various treatment modalities like CBT, ERP, and ACT. MI is a plus.
  • 2 year+ experience Group curriculum, facilitation and therapeutic milieu skills preferred
  • 2 year+ experience in higher level of care models (IOP, PHP, RES, IP).
  • 3 year + Experience with a wide range of evidenced based interventions.
  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
  • Empathy and a genuine desire to help patients with high levels of avoidance and resistance.
  • Ability to handle high-stress situations with members in group settings, including risk assessments, variable use of interventions and strategies, and needed follow-up.
  • Flexibility to work in shifts, including evenings.
  • A positive attitude and a commitment to delivering exceptional customer experiences and team support.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a virtual team
  • Effective with shifting roles, responsibilities, and expectations in an unpredictable environment.

Benefits include:

  • Health insurance, including dental and vision
  • Life insurance
  • 401(k)
  • Employee discount
  • Paid time off
  • Parental leave

title: Credit Resolution Representative II - PFS (Remote)
location: SE MI PFS Service Ctr Trinity Health Corporate - Farmington Hills, Mi
description:
Employment Type:

Full time

Shift:

Day Shift

Description:

POSITION PURPOSE

Work Remote Position

(Pay Range: $19.5965--$29.3948)

Performs day-to-day activities required to process credit account balances from patients and insurances within the Hospital and/or Medical Group revenue operations ($3-5B NPR) of a Patient Business Services (PBS) location. Serves as a member of a team at an assigned PBS location responsible for reducing account receivable credits, communicating with insurance companies, and coordinating with the customer service team to communicate to patients regarding overpayments. Responsibilities require expertise in determining the root cause of credit balances and in taking the appropriate steps to resolve issues resulting in full adjudication of an account. Work activities include posting payments and rejections from insurance companies and rebilling claims as needed to maintain manageable credit accounts receivable and to ensure accurate submission of claims and patient statements. This position reports directly to the Supervisor Payment Posting.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Knows, understands, incorporates, and demonstrates the Trinity Health Mission, Vision, and Values in behaviors, practices, and decisions

Performs daily activities of the Payment Posting team which reviews, monitors and performs follow up on insurance, patient, and Medicare credit accounts receivable as part of the revenue cycle process for an assigned PBS location

Documents corrections regarding discrepancies created, and outstanding items and exceptions in appropriate systems regarding rejections and follow up activities performed in order to enable others to review claim history on all accounts.

Tracks data on payment activity and findings for the Supervisor.

Performs account adjustments or write-offs as needed in accordance with the Write-off- Policy.

Researches credit balances caused by payment posting and prepares appropriate documentation.

Provides feedback to the Cash Posting team based on credits worked.

Serves as a back up to the Payment Posting Representatives.

Prepares refund checks to patients and insurances and enters data into appropriate system.

Performs duties in a manner which promotes accurate cash posting and reconciliation.

Adheres to proactive practices, including cash posting of all incoming payments in a timely and effective manner.

Performs processes related cash posting to ensure such activities are submitted timely, tracked, trended and reported to key stakeholders.

Maintains a working knowledge of applicable Federal, State, and local laws and regulations, Trinity Health’s Integrity and Compliance Program and Code of Conduct, as well as other policies and procedures in order to ensure adherence in a manner that reflects honest, ethical, and professional behavior.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

High school diploma or Associate's degree in Accounting or Business Administration or related field, with up to three (3) or more years of relevant knowledge of revenue cycle functions and systems and experience within a hospital or clinic environment, a health insurance company, managed care organization or other health care financial service setting, performing medical claims processing, financial counseling, financial clearance, accounting or customer service activities or an equivalent combination of education and experience. CPA certification preferred. Experience in a complex, multi-site environment preferred.

Proficient in Microsoft Office, including Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills and organizational abilities.

Strong interpersonal skills in interacting with internal and external customers.

Strong accuracy, attention to detail and time management skills.

Completion of regulatory/mandatory certifications and skills validation competencies preferred.

Must be comfortable operating in a collaborative, shared leadership environment.

Must possess a personal presence that is characterized by a sense of honesty, integrity, and caring with the ability to inspire and motivate others to promote the philosophy, mission, vision, goals, and values of Trinity Health.

PHYSICAL AND MENTAL REQUIREMENTS AND WORKING CONDITIONS

This position operates in a typical office environment. The area is well lit, temperature controlled and free from hazards.

Incumbent communicates frequently, in person and over the phone, with people in all locations on product support issues.

$60k-$75k base salary + annual bonus target

About BBH:

Brown Brothers Harriman (BBH) is a premier global financial services firm, known for premium service, specialist expertise, technology solutions and partnership approach to client management. Across Investor Services and Capital Partners, we work with an enviable roster of sophisticated clients who make BBH their first call when they are tackling their hardest challenges. Delivering for our clients and each other energizes us.

We believe that how we do our work is just as important as what we do. We are relentless problem solvers who know our best ideas come from collective debate and development—so we are never possessive about our ideas. Every day we come together as a diverse community of smart and caring people to deliver exceptional service and expert advice—creating success that lasts. No matter where you sit in the organization, everyone is empowered to contribute their ideas. BBHers can pick up the phone and call any colleague, and they are happy to help. Expanding your impact beyond your daily role is part of how we operate as trusted partners to one another.

We believe stability is a competitive advantage, but being stable means having the knowledge, skill, and discipline to evolve, often—pushing the boundaries of innovation. As a private partnership, every investment we make is in the relationships, technologies, products and development we believe are in the long-term interests of our clients and our people. Our long-tenured leaders are experts in their areas and are actively involved in the day-to day business, taking the time to provide guidance and mentoring to build the next generation of BBHers. Because we know, our success begins with yours.

title: *INTERNAL CANDIDATES ONLY* Student Assistant - Systematic Review - Hybrid
description:
The California's Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment (OEHHA) is seeking to hire two (2) undergraduate Student Assistants to assist with the systematic review of scientific publications related to quaternary ammonium compounds (QACs). QACs are a broad group of chemicals used in personal care, environmental, and agricultural products, which have potential adverse health effects and are of concern to public health.

This position is for internal candidates only. External candidates will not be considered.

Conditions of

Employment

This is a part-time, temporary, non-benefited, student position. Employment in all positions with University Enterprises, Inc. is dependent upon the mutual consent of University Enterprises, Inc. and the employee. This means that either University Enterprises, Inc. or the employee can, at any time, terminate the employment relationship at will, with or without cause.

Depending on the type of position you are applying for, a pre-employment background check consisting of one or more of the following may be conducted: employment history, professional references, criminal check: educational verification (degree, license, or official transcript) or DMV clearance. Applicants will be required to pass required pre-employment checks to the satisfaction of University Enterprises, Inc. (UEI) and the hiring Agency or Department.

UEI does not allow students to hold more than one UEI Job at a time, or work in more than one account per pay period. UEI employees who are considering leaving their current UEI student assistant position for a different UEI student assistant position should inform their supervisor in writing and provide at least a week’s notice.

UEI is not a multi-state employer. UEI only employs candidates who live and work in the state of California. If selected for the position you must reside in California and all work must be performed in the state of California throughout the course of employment.

Prerequisites

Must be a college student attending classes during the regular term (Fall, Spring and Winter, if applicable), at one of the accredited colleges or universities on our affiliation list. To view our current affiliation list please paste the following URL into your browser: http://www.calinterns.org/wp-content/uploads/Affiliation_List.pdf


Students must be enrolled in at least: six-semester units or nine quarter units for undergraduate students; four-semester units or six quarter units for graduate students.


Students declared major must match the major(s) listed in the job posting.

Majors/Fields of Study

Public Health, Environmental Health, or Environmental Toxicology.

Work Schedule

Flexible workdays and work hours, Monday – Friday, between 8 AM – 5 PM. The final work schedule will be determined by the supervisor.

Additional Work Schedule

Student Assistant and Graduate Assistant employees generally work up to 24 hours per workweek (Sunday – Saturday) during the academic year and up to 40 hours per workweek during breaks; (winter, spring, and summer).

Compensation

$18.27 - $22.37 per hour.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Interest in chemical toxicity assessment, systematic literature reviews, systematic evidence mapping.
  • Experience performing literature reviews and conducting online research .
  • Experience working with large datasets.
  • Coursework and/or research experience in public health, environmental health, environmental science, toxicology, or a related field.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Individuals who are, or have been, a dependent child in foster care, a homeless youth or a formerly incarcerated youth as defined by Government Code section 18220 are encouraged to apply and will be given priority. Please note that prior to appointment, individuals claiming preference under one of these categories will be required to furnish documentation establishing their eligibility.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Conducting literature title/abstract screening and full text reviews.
  • Extracting and organizing data.
  • Analyzing data and mapping results.
  • Summarizing scientific information.
  • Developing data visualizations.
  • Presenting findings.
  • During the first two to three months, the student’s primary responsibility will be to screen/review scientific studies and extract toxicity data on QACs. Depending on project needs, available time, and the student’s interests, the work may extend into later phases of the systematic evidence map project. These activities may include developing a literature inventory, summarizing and visualizing database information, and evaluating individual studies.

Physical Requirements

Sit for extended periods; frequently stand and walk; manual dexterity and hand-eye coordination; corrected hearing and vision to normal range; verbal communication; use of office equipment including computer workstations, telephones, calculators, copiers, printers, and scanners with or without reasonable accommodation.

Working Conditions

Work will be performed in a hybrid environment.

Students/Employees will be required to work according to the current UEI remote workplace policy and sign a UEI Work from Home Agreement. The decision to permit an employee to work from home is at the discretion of the supervisor or employer and may, at any time and with or without cause, unilaterally terminate the option to work from home.

title: Chief Clinical Officer (CCO) - Trinity Health Michigan (9 Hospitals)
description:
Employment Type:

Full time

Shift:

Description:

Trinity Health Michigan (THMI) is looking for its next Chief Clinical Officer (CCO) who will be a data-driven, strategic, clinical and operational executive. The CCO acts as the bridge between clinical care, emerging technologies, and Trinity Health's strategy.

Candidate must reside near or be willing to relocate to one of our nine hospital locations within Michigan.

POSITION PURPOSE

The Chief Clinical Officer reports directly to the President and CEO of Trinity Health Michigan serves as a member of THMI's Executive Team providing strategic thought leadership and direction for the THMI Clinical and Medical Staff Services, Quality, Patient Safety, Research, Graduate Medical Education and Care Management programs across the acute care and ambulatory environment. The CCO serves as the Chief Clinical Leader for Quality working with the THMI regional and local boards to oversee quality, care management, risk, research, regulatory reviews, patient safety and a broad scope of performance improvement support functions for the health system. The Chief Clinical Officer leads the enabling strategies to assure regulatory compliance, and risk management necessary to fulfill and sustain the ministries mission and vision. The Chief Clinical Officer serves as internal consultant to senior medical leadership including each hospital’s President, Chief Medical and Nursing Officer and other medical staff leaders (e.g. Quality and Informatics). Serves with matrix oversite of Chief Medical Officers and Regional Chief Nursing Officer to advance quality, safety and integration of Systemwide Clinical Services.

ABOUT TRINITY HEALTH MICHIGAN

For more than a century, the hospitals and doctors of Trinity Health Michigan have been dedicated to caring for our communities.

Our expert teams combine advanced medicine with compassionate, personalized care—so patients get the best treatment close to home.

With operating revenues of $4.74 billion, our faith-based ministry provided $232.4 million in community benefits and activities in FY24.

As part of Trinity Health, one of the largest health systems in the country, we offer access to a vast network of medical experts, leading research, state-of-the-art facilities, clinical trials, and the latest technology.

9 Hospitals

2,314 licensed beds

34 outpatient medical centers

11 emergency departments

23 urgent cares

701,000 attributed lives

90,891 surgeries (IP/OP)

26,918 colleagues

5,720 credentialed physicians and clinicians

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  • Meets Health System Code of Conduct Standards including interpersonal communication, professional conduct expectations, and compliance with core values.

  • Develops the five-year quality, patient safety, risk management and care management strategic plan and the annual operations plan, then monitors and directs regional, hospital and medical group performance to the plans.

  • Develops consistent strategies for the system quality and focused approach to improving quality and value for the system strategic five-year plan. Works with appropriate hospital and ministry senior leadership team and medical directors to assure consistency and achieve long term quality and utilization objectives.

  • Leads THMI Integrated Clinical Leadership Team, CMO/CNO Council and Co-Chairs the THMI PC3 (i.e. quality subcommittee of the THMI regional board). Facilitates other statewide clinical advisory teams as needed (e.g. readmissions, physician advisors).

  • Attends Trinity Health Michigan Board meetings as staff and provides relevant clinical and patient updates as requested.

  • Leads key service, operational, and staff areas as assigned by the RHM CEO & President including the stewardship of human, financial, and material resources; quality and efficient services; and the alignment of the services of the assigned areas to the strategic plan.

  • Liaisons to Trinity Heath by serving on various councils, collaboratives and task forces as assigned and as a participant in the Trinity Health leadership group. Implements Trinity Health programs and directives.

  • Represents THMI to the State of Michigan business, service, and healthcare community by active participation and leadership within various organizations (e.g. Michigan Hospital Association, Michigan State Medical Society, MDHHS) for quality, patient safety, and utilization matters.

  • Liaison and staff to the Medical Staff and Medical Staff Committees for bylaws standards, clinician credentialing and privileging standards and related quality, patient safety and utilization matters.

  • As the Chief Clinical Officer, ensures coordination across all entities for the entire quality and patient safety efforts of the organization; this includes oversight of risk management, infection control function, case management and Quality Departments.

  • Responsible for fulfillment of all regulatory requirements of The Joint Commission (TCJ), Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS), and State Health and Welfare.

  • Responsible as the Patient Safety Officer for the RHM to improve and enhance all patient safety efforts and initiatives.

  • Provides senior leadership and oversight for the Clinical Resource Management and Acute Social Work Departments and is an available physician liaison for clinical documentation.

  • Provides strategic support to the RHM Leadership to assure development of value driven healthcare across a broad continuum and durable and sustainable physician relationships.

  • Participates in various committees and structures including Quality and Informatics Committee, payer and employer negotiating teams, and various administrative councils as needed.

  • Serves as the accountable executive for the Institutional Review Board (IRB) and associated research while partnering with the local graduate medical education leaders.

Trinity Health Physician Executive Core Responsibilities:

  • Physician strategy: Engaging physicians as partners in growth, development, and operational and financial excellence across the continuum with a focus on community-based services. Develops lasting partnerships with physicians. Leads efforts to reduce unnecessary clinical variation in partnership with Service line leaders, Medical Group Leaders, and Clinical Framework teams. Actively works to recruit and retain top physicians, including activities to promote wellbeing and reduce burn out.

  • Care Excellence: Assembles high performing teams and works collaboratively to achieve top decile performance in all aspects of care excellence (member experience, safety, quality and operational efficiency). Expert in regulatory and accreditation preparation resulting in positive survey results. Establishes policies and procedures to ensure compliance with applicable state and federal laws and regulations to maintain accreditation. In conjunction with medical group, leads efforts on accurate clinical documentation within patient medical records. Bridges gap between strategic priorities and clinical outcomes.

  • Service line and clinical programs: Actively participates in regional service line development and growth in partnership with dyad service line and medical groups leaders to achieve strategic priorities including clinical program growth. Holds contracted hospital-based groups accountable for performance to drive results. Aligns and integrates care across the continuum. Participates in development of enterprise strategy with shared accountability for financial and clinical outcomes. In collaboration with CNO and Medical Group leadership reshapes care delivery across the continuum to meet operational and financial needs.

  • Connected care: Coordinates clinical activities across the continuum to achieve system goal of connected care. Identifies and collaborates on efforts to close care gaps and improve outcomes of care, including member experience. Innovates care model beyond traditional episodic visits to link patients, care teams and health data in real time, incorporating technologic solutions where appropriate.

  • AI & Tech Integration: Drives the implementation of predictive analytics, AI-assisted diagnostics, and digital health tools to streamline workflows and augment clinician/physician decision-making, improve care excellence, and physician efficiency. In partnership with health informatics, accountable for optimizing usage of approved tools.

  • Workforce Development: Collaborates with Medical Group Leadership and the CNO on physician and APP workforce development and education and training to meet the strategic staffing needs of the future. Collaborates and advises on innovative care models to address workforce challenges. Leads efforts to enhance physician leadership opportunities and growth, including succession planning. Collaborates with CNO and Medical Group leadership on physician and APP workplace health, mental wellbeing, and safety across the continuum.

  • Medical Staff: Leads the medical staff in adopting best practices in credentialing and peer review to assure robust processes to attract and retain the highest quality of privileged providers across the continuum. Facilitates, intervenes and moderates all major Physician-physician, Physician-patient and physician-colleague concerns in collaboration with Chief Nursing Officer and other appropriate medical staff and executive team leaders. Engages and aligns credentialed medical staff.

  • Graduate Medical Education: Serves as system lead for graduate medical education and research activities across the continuum. Strategically aligns GME programs with physician recruitment needs. Partners with Medical Group leadership to recruit and retain trainees within Trinity Health.

  • Health Equity: Shifting the focus toward reducing health disparities and addressing health related social needs.

  • Ethics: Serving as the ethical voice of the organization when balancing clinical risk with innovation, and guiding public-facing medical strategy.

  • Advocacy: Develops a collaborative working relationship with advocacy teams to strengthen the advocacy position of Trinity Health to assure sustainability of the mission.

LEADERSHIP COMPETENCIES

As a Trinity Health Executive, the incumbent is expected to demonstrate leadership traits which support our Mission Statement and Core Values as identified below:

Mission Statement: We, Trinity Health, serve together in the spirit of the Gospel as a compassionate and transforming healing presence within our communities.

Core Values:

  • Reverence: We honor the sacredness and dignity of every person.

  • Commitment to Those who are Poor: We stand with and serve those who are poor, especially those most vulnerable.

  • Justice: We foster right relationships to promote the common good, including sustainability of Earth.

  • Stewardship: We honor our heritage and hold ourselves accountable for the human, financial and natural resources entrusted to our care.

  • Integrity: We are faithful to those we say we are.

  • Safety: We embrace a culture that prevents harm and nurtures a healing, safe environment for all.

Vision

As a mission-driven, innovative health organization, we will become a leader in improving the health of our communities and each person we serve. We will be the most trusted partner for life.

Promise Statement

We Listen. We Partner. We Make it Easy.

Our Actions

  • Listen to understand.

  • Learn continuously.

  • Keep it simple.

  • Create solutions.

  • Deliver outstanding service.

  • Own and speak up for safety.

  • Expect, embrace and initiate change.

  • Demonstrate exceptional teamwork.

  • Trust and assume goodness of intentions.

  • Hold myself and others accountable for results.

  • Communicate directly with respect and honesty.

  • Serve every person with empathy, dignity and compassion.

  • Champion diversity, equity and inclusion.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • Relevant clinically related doctoral degree, MD or DO with board certification in specialty. An unrestricted licensure, or ability to be licensed, in the state of Michigan required.

  • Advanced business degree in health care management or MBA preferred.

  • At least 5-10 years of experience in a medical leadership role. Additional advanced degrees preferred in additional to 5-10 years of clinical experience. Track record of continuous improvement in operational quality (e.g. process improvement methodologies), including confirmed success in leveraging clinical systems and technology solutions to support evidence-based decision making. Experience managing healthcare outcomes/costs across multiple locations is required.

  • Previous experience as Chief Medical Officer or other significant Physician Leadership position preferable.

  • Experience with physician contracting, proformas and finance desired.

  • Continued clinical practice preferred.

  • Ability to interpret complex health datasets, predictive models, and clinical efficacy metrics rather than just lagging quality indicators.

  • Demonstrated team, performance analysis, presentation, interpersonal, facilitation, planning, and communication skills.

  • Exceptional emotional intelligence to guide clinical staff through rapid technological adoption and evolving healthcare delivery models. Strong ability to lead by influence, aligning clinical, financial and operational stakeholders.

PHYSICAL AND MENTAL REQUIREMENTS AND WORKING CONDITIONS

  • Must be able to adapt to frequently changing work priorities.

  • Must be able to travel as needed to the various Trinity Health sites.

Our Commitment

Rooted in our Mission and Core Values, we honor the dignity of every person and recognize the unique perspectives, experiences, and talents each colleague brings. By finding common ground and embracing our differences, we grow stronger together and deliver more compassionate, person-centered care. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by federal, state, or local law.

description:
Labcorp is a global leader in laboratory services, providing the insights and answers that help healthcare providers, patients, researchers, pharmaceutical companies and health systems make confident decisions and improve outcomes. Through our unparalleled science, data, technology and laboratory network, we advance diagnostics, accelerate innovation and help address some of the world’s most important health challenges. With our global scale and deep expertise, you’ll have the opportunity to do meaningful work, grow your career and make a real impact on people’s health around the world. Together, we’re improving health and improving lives.


Labcorp is seeking a Lab Assistant to join our team our team in Burlington, NC.

Work Schedule: Tuesday-Saturday 12:00am to 8:30am

Job Responsibilities

  • Receive and sort clinical lab specimens
  • Prepare specimens for testing and analysis
  • Scan and/or data entry of specimen and patient information
  • Ensure all lab equipment is working properly and perform minor instrumentation maintenance
  • Troubleshoot any specimen related issues
  • Replenish test bench supplies as needed
  • Maintain a clean and safe work environment
  • Complete record logs and other administrative duties as requested
  • Follow all Standard Operating Procedures to ensure safety and quality standards

Minimum Qualifications

  • Integrates new practices and coordinates the planning and launch of acquisitions to ensure seamless transition for patients, physicians, and employees. Works to achieve cultural integration. Manages the Baptist brand by exporting the culture of service excellence and standardized care.
  • Develops schedules based on task breakdown, materials, and information and resource allocation plans.
  • Lead contract labor calls to ensure proper onboarding of contract labor by market.

  • Apprises Strategic Project Manager, and appropriate operational leaders, of organization issues, problems or trends; prepares reports, analyses and other written communication setting forth progress, adverse trends, and appropriate recommendations or conclusions as necessary or requested.
  • Collects feedback from BHMG operations leads, as well as physicians, to demonstrate effectiveness of integration/practice assimilation strategies.
  • Strive to ensure optimal physician integration to BHMG.
  • Ensures compliance with all law and regulation and keeps abreast of new regulations and standards.
  • Develops schedules based on task breakdown, materials, and information and resource allocation plans.
  • Ensures positive customer relations interactions
  • Manages difficult or emotional customer situations
  • Responds promptly to customer needs
  • Solicits customer feedback to improve service
  • Responds to requests for service and assistance
  • Meets commitments
